purpose.text: Develop a source-bound model of a heavy-water pressure-tube reactor, including on-power refuelling. The intended system connects physical geometry, material state, coupled fields and each fuel bundle’s history. It also defines separate forecasting and inspection responsibilities.

scope.text: The current repository implements development validation: source and metadata admission, document checks, a versioned CI graph/result policy and a bounded local gate supervisor. The reactor boundary remains architecture-only with empty public capabilities and runtime dependencies. The coupled physical solver, fuel-history engine, prediction and 3D/CAD workflow remain research targets. This atlas inspected source; it did not execute or independently qualify those tools or the proposed science.

inputs.title: Exact physical case
inputs.text: Source edition, supported model profile, pressure-tube/channel geometry, material and nuclear-library state, boundary conditions and units identify what the calculation would mean.

inputs.title: Fuel and operating history
inputs.text: Each physical bundle needs its own nuclide inventory, irradiation and energy history, geometry/material association, and scheduled incoming, retained and discharged states.

inputs.title: A defined observation or forecast question
inputs.text: Requests must distinguish present-state observations from future field, inventory or burnup forecasts. Forecasts need a target, horizon and explicit future boundary/history schedule.

outputs.title: Coupled physical state and observations
outputs.text: Target results retain the actual geometry/material state, effective inputs, supported quantities, numerical method and evidence for the adopted physical profile.

outputs.title: Fuel lineage and refuelling transitions
outputs.text: Intended outputs include evolved per-bundle inventories and committed incoming, retained and discharged states. Restart must not commit a failed or cancelled event twice.

outputs.title: Separate forecasts and engineering views
outputs.text: A predictor would produce model-conditional future fields or inventory/burnup results. Inspection would consume identified geometry, materials and quantities for 3D/CAD, workbench and teaching views, with its own qualification.

components.title: Source and profile contract
components.text: Bind edition, rights, quantities, units, coordinates and supported physical domain before interpreting the case.

components.title: Geometry and material occurrence graph
components.text: Keep physical bundles, computational cells and thermal groups distinct. The world model includes the identified physical state and its permitted model evolution.

components.title: Own coupled solver
components.text: Couple spatial neutronics and poison feedback with conservative solid heat and the supported coolant/network model. These are interacting fields, not a simple one-way processing chain.

components.title: History and refuelling
components.text: Evolve bundle inventory and move inventory, provenance and geometry/material associations together when a refuelling transition commits.

components.title: Prediction and inspection consumers
components.text: Read the same identified physical subject while keeping forecast, observation, presentation and engineering evidence scopes separate.

connections.text: The source assigns reusable mathematical primitives to this library; PHWR retains its own model, solver, closures and prediction choices.
The source assigns registry semantics to the orchestrator. The proposed PHWR configuration is not an accepted active registry assignment.

limits.title: A benchmark is a bounded profile
limits.text: Reproducing a reference case cannot qualify the additional nuclear chain, reaction/decay data, energy accounting or event dynamics needed for full fuel-history operation.

limits.title: Geometry is not a solved physical model
limits.text: Mesh refinement must not duplicate a bundle’s atoms. A 3D/CAD view must retain physical identities and field support rather than imply a new solved model.

limits.title: Forecast and interface admission remain separate
limits.text: Scenario spread is not a calibrated confidence interval. The source requires refusal for unsupported regimes or targets; public API, wire schema and installed consumer interfaces remain unaccepted.

implementation.title: Local repository admission
implementation.text: Candidate files, the declared project boundary, citation/funding schemas, document links and development-tool licence evidence are inputs to dedicated validation commands. Their outputs are acceptance/refusal, diagnostics and explicitly requested development inventories; they do not consume reactor state or produce physical fields or control commands.

implementation.title: Seven CI categories and required-result policy
implementation.text: The source defines correctness, hook integration, documentation, dependency audit, static analysis, component inventory and supply-chain assessment lanes. The coordinator needs all seven. The result evaluator requires success for applicable lanes and permits only declared event-inapplicable skips. This is implemented policy/configuration, not evidence that a hosted run succeeded.

implementation.title: Bounded local gate supervisor
implementation.text: The supervisor invokes a selected existing Make gate, preserves its exit status and stops its owned process group on timeout or cancellation. It accepts a finite positive deadline. A focused check does not qualify the exhaustive validation contract, and this helper is not a simulation or deployed reactor service.

external_roles.title: Reusable mathematics and registry semantics
external_roles.text: SCPN-REACTOR-KERNELS owns reusable primitives and SCPN-PHASE-ORCHESTRATOR owns registry semantics. PHWR retains its physical equations, closures, solver and prediction choices. Its current boundary declares no runtime dependency or accepted active configuration.

external_roles.title: Studio, workbench and control ownership
external_roles.text: Presentation, workbench execution, supervisory control and final machine-protection veto keep their external owners. Producer/consumer contracts and category assignment must be accepted before a runtime or Studio descriptor can be emitted. No hardware I/O is implemented.

source_notes.text: The refreshed source describes working repository-validation tooling alongside unimplemented scientific components. Earlier source captures remain available with their original dates and fingerprints. The newer capture is a source update, not an accepted reactor capability, publication or full-project completion.

purpose.text: Own the plasma-solver mathematics and evidence-producing research workflows that other SCPN projects consume. The documented laboratory spans equilibrium, transport, control research, diagnostics, geometry and selected engineering models.

scope.text: These explanations describe documented solver and I/O responsibilities. Qualification belongs to the exact case, backend and evidence artefact; downstream control, deployment and facility interlock authority belong to their owners.

inputs.title: Equilibrium and solver configuration
inputs.text: Grid, coils, pressure/current profiles and boundary information define an equilibrium problem. GEQDSK carries poloidal flux, profiles and boundary/limiter data; JSON configuration supplies solver settings.

inputs.title: Transport and diagnostic data
inputs.text: Electron/ion temperature and density profiles plus geometry feed transport. Documented ingest routes include IMAS structures, bounded NPZ series, optional facility interfaces and complete source-bound MAST archive records.

inputs.title: A bounded control or replay context
inputs.text: Controller studies consume the selected plant/model state and their replay or safety policy. Solver outputs alone do not determine downstream actuation permissions.

outputs.title: Equilibrium and evolved profiles
outputs.text: Documented equilibrium results include flux, magnetic axis, X-point and magnetic field. Transport produces evolved profiles, transport coefficients and bootstrap current within its selected model.

outputs.title: Interchange and controller artefacts
outputs.text: The source lists GEQDSK and IMAS outputs, source-bound magnetic envelopes, compiled .scpnctl.json controller artefacts, and selected NPZ weights/datasets.

outputs.title: Inspection and validation records
outputs.text: Figures, structured physics logs and JSON/Markdown evidence report the selected calculation and its scope. Source/archive qualification envelopes preserve unresolved fields and review-only authority.

outputs.title: Distinct field, profile, surface and evidence records
outputs.text: A flux field, time-evolved profiles, virtual/reconstructed diagnostic data, triangle mesh/OBJ and reduced-force result describe different representations and calculations. Export or discovery success does not combine them into one accepted full-fidelity plant model; each retains its own inputs, source, numerical resolution and review evidence.

components.title: Ingest and source contract
components.text: Decode supported formats without losing source identity, field meaning or file-loading bounds.

components.title: Equilibrium and transport owners
components.text: Keep the equilibrium field solve, differentiable paths, transport closures and their reference/parity requirements attached to their own models.

components.title: Control and diagnostics research
components.text: Use controller, state-estimation, replay, synthetic-sensor and inspection modules in their documented scopes; offline tuning remains separate from live deployment.

components.title: Evidence and consumer seam
components.text: Emit source-bound data and reports through documented I/O, manifest or public integration surfaces. Consumers retain responsibility for their own runtime and claim boundary.

connections.text: CONTROL wraps the equilibrium/transport/free-boundary and control-compiler subset behind its bounded control APIs; it owns its facade, loop integration and downstream safety envelope.
The source assigns FRC equilibrium, Faraday and pulsed-compression physics seams to Fusion, while MIF owns magneto-inertial workflow integration.
Fusion supplies classical phase/disruption-feature contracts; quantum execution and quantum-specific evidence remain with Quantum Control.
Studio consumes physics verbs and generated manifest/evidence metadata. Discovery or routing does not qualify a physical result.

limits.title: Synthetic notebook profiles retain their origin
limits.text: The validation notes identify bundled disruption profiles as generated DIII-D-like references, not raw EFIT/MDSplus downloads. Their labels must not turn into a real-shot claim.

limits.title: A geometric or reduced-order view keeps its own scope
limits.text: The source distinguishes toroidal geometry, reduced spectral/3D paths and a post-solve balancing utility. It also marks patch AMR as an offline/validation utility until its production parity lane exists.

limits.title: Shared ownership is not shared deployment approval
limits.text: Unreconciled consumer contracts remain blocked or diagnostic in the source. TORAX runtime outcomes are provenance, not actuation commands.

limits.title: Source detail is not a new physics or runtime acceptance
limits.text: This refresh inspects the clean canonical source and selected public contracts only. It does not run the JAX solver, transport, tomography, 3D force calculation, export or external-code comparison; it does not qualify convergence, hardware rate, full-fidelity parity, downstream actuation or a complete reactor design. Those remain exact-case/consumer decisions.

implementation.title: Equilibrium fields from a declared forward problem
implementation.text: The laboratory’s equilibrium surfaces use grid, coils, pressure/current profiles and boundary data to compute poloidal flux, axis/X-point and magnetic fields under the selected Grad-Shafranov formulation. The explicit compiled JAX predictive route accepts coil currents, profile derivatives, grids and response/boundary data, and caches an on-device fixed-point iteration; a batched route shares model settings across input batches. Imported reference fields, reduced surrogates and a predictive solve keep separate origins and convergence/reference requirements.

implementation.title: Radial transport with selected closure and power sources
implementation.text: The documented 1.5D transport path evolves temperature and density profiles on a normalised radial coordinate using equilibrium geometry, particle/heat sources and declared transport closures. Outputs include evolved profiles, diffusivities and bootstrap-current estimates within that model. Heating normalisation keeps auxiliary MW, volume-normalised deposition and temperature-source units explicit. Empirical scaling, neural closures, external turbulence codes and the native research models require their own selected case and evidence; their names do not establish mutual parity.

implementation.title: Synthetic measurements and inverse diagnostic views
implementation.text: The diagnostic surface supplies virtual magnetic/kinetic/neutron instruments, forward channels and tomography. Its documented diagnostics runner generates synthetic measurements, adds noise, reconstructs an emissivity field and reports quality. A line-integrated signal, reconstructed field and underlying model state are distinct records. The separate GEQDSK/IMAS/NPZ/archive intake surfaces carry their own source and loading contracts; a synthetic diagnostic demonstration is not a measured-shot reconstruction.

implementation.title: Three-dimensional surfaces and a reduced force-balance model
implementation.text: Reactor3DBuilder can trace an approximate 2D last-closed flux surface and revolve it into triangle vertices/faces, or sample the separately supplied reduced Fourier geometry. When a ray has no strict crossing it can use the closest sampled boundary value; too few traced points trigger an ellipse fallback. It exports that surface to Wavefront OBJ. VMECStyleEquilibrium3D maps flux coordinates through Fourier boundary coefficients; ForceBalance3D separately iterates those coefficients against a sampled reduced force residual. The source explicitly distinguishes this reduced formulation from a full VMEC solve. A mesh export and a converged reduced residual are different outputs, neither a complete reactor engineering design.

implementation.title: Case-bound reports and separately owned consumer seams
implementation.text: The package emits interchange fields, model/controller artefacts, figures and JSON/Markdown evidence under explicit producer contracts. Solver capability discovery and a selected backend do not qualify every physics lane. The TORAX seam keeps complete simulation output/provenance apart from a deliberately bounded review projection; failed or truncated runs do not become successful plant states. CONTROL owns downstream admission, while MIF, Quantum Control and Studio retain their workflow, quantum-execution and interface responsibilities.

model_layers.title: Forward prediction, reconstruction and surrogate keep different inputs
model_layers.text: A computed psi(R,Z) field has the meaning of its declared solver problem. Imported reference/current/boundary information and a learned surrogate descriptor are different information sources from a coil/profile-driven predictive solve. Reference agreement, physical data qualification and convergence must attach to the actual path; one result cannot automatically validate the others.

model_layers.title: Profile evolution has a declared spatial and physical resolution
model_layers.text: The radial transport model evolves selected profile quantities using its chosen geometry, sources and closures. That state is not a fully resolved three-dimensional kinetic or multiphysics plant. External-code comparisons, conservation, training-domain suitability and synthetic/measured provenance retain separate evidence rather than following from a transport API or a familiar solver name.

model_layers.title: A visible surface and a physical 3D solve are separate artefacts
model_layers.text: The toroidal triangle surface represents shape and can retain closest-sample or ellipse fallback approximations. Fourier shaping adds declared non-axisymmetric geometry; the separate spectral residual model adds a reduced force-balance calculation. Mesh resolution, force-residual convergence and full non-axisymmetric physical fidelity are different checks. Blanket, wall, thermal-hydraulic and balance-of-plant models also keep their own reduced assumptions and do not turn the surface into a fabrication-ready reactor design.

model_layers.title: Simulated diagnostics and measured signals need separate provenance
model_layers.text: A virtual instrument predicts a signal from a model; tomography solves an inverse problem with chosen geometry and regularisation. Noise and reconstructed quality do not authenticate a physical source, calibration, observation geometry or facility clock. Source-bound archive qualification and consumer admission remain their own contracts.

purpose.text: Keep a connected development workbench for modelling neural behaviour, encoding signals as bitstreams or events, simulating and training networks, compiling selected computations for hardware, and inspecting the resulting evidence.

scope.text: The repository distinguishes supported package surfaces, optional backend paths and source-only research. The canonical map is a document source, not a new blanket proof that every listed backend, model or hardware path is qualified.

inputs.title: Signals and stochastic representation
inputs.text: Input values can enter an encoder as probabilities and become binary or packed bitstreams. The model must preserve the chosen unipolar/bipolar arithmetic and encoding meaning.

inputs.title: Network and simulation state
inputs.text: The documented network path combines populations, projection weights, stimuli and per-timestep neuron state. Learning and optional synchronisation have their own execution-path scope.

inputs.title: A hardware-oriented model and target
inputs.text: Selected hardware workflows start from equations or an imported network and retain weights, delays, thresholds, hierarchy and precision through graph lowering and emission.

outputs.title: Spike and state observations
outputs.text: The documented simulation spine produces spikes, membrane voltages, firing rates and packed bitstreams, followed by analysis, decoding or export.

outputs.title: Interchange and generated hardware source
outputs.text: NIR graph interchange and selected .v/.sv generation connect software models to compilation. HDL bundles, formal collateral, synthesis/placement records and target decks retain the selected workflow’s scope.

outputs.title: A composed research workflow
outputs.text: The permanent parent workbench brings model, data, learning, silicon and evidence responsibilities together. The named focused repositories are a roadmap of responsibilities, not independent release proof.

components.title: Encoding and arithmetic substrate
components.text: Translate values into the chosen stochastic representation and use the matching arithmetic before decoding or passing results onward.

components.title: Network evolution and learning
components.text: The documented Python step applies stimuli and projections, advances neurons, records state, then updates plasticity and optional synchronisation.

components.title: Execution backend selection
components.text: Keep the canonical SC-inference selector distinct from per-package polyglot dispatch and optional feature-gated runtimes. A backend name in a priority list does not establish registered execution.

components.title: Graph lowering and hardware evidence
components.text: Preserve model meaning while converting through network/SC-NIR representations, precision choices, HDL emission and the selected formal or EDA toolchain.

connections.text: The canonical map describes the get_backend/sc_forward entry as a consumer seam for CONTROL’s Petri-net compiler path. Installed/current consumer qualification remains a separate check.

The captured adapter connects spike-history arrays to local Ry/controlled-rotation statevector processing and returns scaled binary spike outputs. SC-NeuroCore is optional for the array path; the ArcaneNeuron wrapper imports it explicitly. This is a software representation boundary, with separate runtime/model/evidence scope; it does not establish classical/quantum dynamical equivalence or hardware execution.

limits.title: Core, research and contributed material differ
limits.text: The canonical map keeps source-only research and non-package contributed work outside its supported binary surface. They must not become production capabilities through the portfolio map.

limits.title: Backend feature coverage is path-specific
limits.text: The document distinguishes Python network features from Rust/MPI subsets and canonical SC dispatch from independent polyglot kernels. Broad backend lists cannot establish full feature parity.

limits.title: Generated evidence is not certification
limits.text: The hardware pipeline describes traceability, formal and caller-supplied safety evidence. Its library tooling does not provide certification or approval of a deployed product.

limits.title: One conformance axis cannot replace another
limits.text: Software-runtime parity, scientific source-model fidelity, Python/RTL agreement, synthesis/timing and measured hardware behaviour need their own evidence. Base-package generated RTL and a complete polyglot row cannot stand in for all of those results.

implementation.title: Stochastic neuron and bitstream arithmetic
implementation.text: The base-package workflow document supplies neuron stepping and seeded Bernoulli-stream multiplication with explicit expected outputs. An AND gate represents a probability product only under the required stream independence; reusing the same stream changes the meaning. This atlas records the documented examples without rerunning them.

implementation.title: Equation-defined neurons and generated RTL
implementation.text: A neuron can be defined through the supported arithmetic equation namespace, threshold/reset and an explicit time step. Selected equations lower to fixed-point Verilog text. Python/RTL comparison needs its own simulator workflow; generating text does not establish synthesis, timing, power or device behaviour.

implementation.title: Optional acceleration with an explicit fallback
implementation.text: In the captured canonical SC-inference selector, actual probes resolve Rust and NumPy; the other named acceleration lanes are not implemented by this selector. Per-package polyglot kernels have separate dispatch and evidence. The Rust engine is optional and the package has a Python floor.

implementation.title: Package, extras and source-checkout boundaries
implementation.text: The base wheel, optional extras, separate Rust engine and source checkout provide different surfaces. The supported-workflow page explicitly lists analysis and world_model among source-only subpackages. The parent workbench composes research and hardware workflows; a named component or example does not qualify the entire model catalogue or a device.

purpose.text: Provide a repeatable workbench from coupled-system specification to simulator studies, quantum-control experiments, bounded optimisation and reviewable result artefacts. It keeps numerical modelling, execution targets and evidence interpretation separate.

scope.text: The workbench remains under active development. The source explicitly disclaims broad demonstrated quantum advantage and distinguishes simulator, hardware and scoped-failure claims; new component names do not announce independent releases.

inputs.title: A typed scientific problem
inputs.text: Coupling matrix and frequency vector need an explicit model, normalisation, graph/coordinates, units, initial/history state, observable and objective. Phase and quantum state shapes are different.

inputs.title: Circuit and readout semantics
inputs.text: Compilation or transformation must preserve the declared unitary body, original final readout/barrier block, bit indices and logical-to-physical mappings.

inputs.title: An admitted execution target
inputs.text: A reference kernel or QPU route needs explicit execution provenance, parameters, seeds/resources and the applicable submission/promotion gates. A physical-coordinate declaration alone is not calibration evidence.

outputs.title: Bound scientific and compiled representations
outputs.text: The documented pipeline produces scientific companions, Hamiltonian representations and selected executable circuits or simulator kernels without silently changing the declared model or claim class.

outputs.title: Raw results and reference artefacts
outputs.text: Execution stages retain counts or reference results with job identifiers, commands, hashes and source provenance. Observable extraction and mitigation remain separate stages.

outputs.title: Interpretation and evidence records
outputs.text: Reports and ledgers tie observables and method claims to the exact result artefact and simulator/hardware/falsification class. Bounded optimisation results require their own gradient or convergence evidence.

components.title: Problem and model validation
components.text: Check complete scientific meaning before exporting or compiling. Units are checked rather than converted by labels; a phase declaration cannot silently become a quantum XY declaration.

components.title: Compilation and kernel construction
components.text: Create the selected Hamiltonian/circuit/kernel while preserving readout and representation contracts.

components.title: Reference or hardware execution
components.text: Route to the chosen classical reference or provider runner and retain the actual raw output and execution origin.

components.title: Mitigation, observable extraction and reporting
components.text: Apply the selected correction or record its absence; derive named observables and retain artefact-backed evidence classes through reports and ledgers.

connections.text: The architecture assigns the original phase numerical kernels to oscillatools. Scientific companions consume those owners without introducing another solver.

The captured adapter connects spike-history arrays to local Ry/controlled-rotation statevector processing and returns scaled binary spike outputs. SC-NeuroCore is optional for the array path; the ArcaneNeuron wrapper imports it explicitly. This is a software representation boundary, with separate runtime/model/evidence scope; it does not establish classical/quantum dynamical equivalence or hardware execution.

The source describes payload/artifact and feedback bridges around UPDE state, quantum order-parameter and fidelity fields. Consumer control admission is distinct from the presence of a bridge description.
The control_plasma_knm boundary described by Quantum converts plasma-native coupling data into the declared standard representation; Fusion retains classical physics ownership.

limits.title: Matched coefficients do not imply matched dynamics
limits.text: Phase Kuramoto and quantum XY have different state spaces and observables. The source treats their mapping as an encoding/modelling choice, not dynamical equivalence.

limits.title: Typed metadata does not execute the experiment
limits.text: The scientific companion describes and validates a problem; it does not run a trajectory or optimise its declared objective. Physical placement and calibration need their own evidence.

limits.title: Method and hardware claims stay artefact-specific
limits.text: A simulator result, successful provider selection or component roadmap cannot substitute for raw-count-backed hardware evidence or a demonstrated speed advantage.

limits.title: Local bridge size and interpretation
limits.text: The dense layer guards allocation before constructing a statevector over input and neuron qubits. Its thresholded marginal probabilities are local software results. This bridge supplies no hardware calibration, quantum advantage or proof of a biologically equivalent neural model.

implementation.title: Stable problem and result contracts
implementation.text: Problem, Backend, Experiment and Result define the durable data boundary. The source validates shape, capability/objective and metadata requirements; hardware-enabled experiments require preregistration metadata. These constructors do not compile, run a simulation or submit a circuit by themselves.

implementation.title: Local compile, reference and result workflow
implementation.text: The documented pipeline connects a problem to a Hamiltonian, circuit or simulator kernel, then execution results, mitigation, observables and evidence records. Reference simulation, an admitted hardware provider and offline replay are separate routes with their own inputs and provenance. The atlas does not execute any of them.

implementation.title: Bounded differentiation and resource decisions
implementation.text: The gradient guide keeps local implemented routes at bounded-candidate status, with no promoted differentiable row. Compile/dense resource guards return an allowed/refused estimate under explicit caps. Neither a budget decision nor a derivative interface proves host-memory immunity, QPU-gradient execution or a performance advantage.

implementation.title: A concrete local neural-to-quantum software bridge
implementation.text: SNNQuantumBridge reads a trailing spike-history window, forms mean firing rates and rotation parameters, runs QuantumDenseLayer and scales the returned binary spike vector into output currents. The optional ArcaneNeuron wrapper supplies neurons; NumPy spike arrays work without that sibling package. This code path is local statevector software and contains no QPU submission.

source_notes.title: Probability helpers and the actual bridge output differ
source_notes.text: The current-conversion helper accepts probabilities or binary indicators, but this bridge calls QuantumDenseLayer.forward, which thresholds exact marginal probabilities and returns integer spikes. The bridge therefore scales binary outputs. Its probability-to-current documentation must not be read as raw probability readout from a QPU.

purpose.text: Preserve completed quantum-job observations in offline evidence packs so a reviewer can distinguish original bytes, provenance, numerical derivation and the policy used to evaluate the result.

scope.text: This is an intended standalone domain workflow under implementation preparation. Its source documentation and development checks do not establish accepted capture/import/derive/seal/verify/inspect/render operations.

inputs.title: Original observations and custody facts
inputs.text: Completed-job bytes arrive with origin, job/quantity inventories, timestamps and calibration associations. Requested shots, observed totals, probability estimates and counts retain different meanings.

inputs.title: An explicitly installed numerical programme
inputs.text: Derivation must bind the actual installed programme and environment, ordered inputs, output schema/scalars, units, precision, comparison and optional seed.

inputs.title: Policy, time and caller-owned trust context
inputs.text: Verification uses an explicit policy/time and the selected trust context. Source versions and installed types must agree with the complete request and evaluation inputs.

outputs.title: Preserved and sealed evidence pack
outputs.text: Intended packs retain foreign/native originals, representations, field origin, quantities and missing information without relabelling their provenance.

outputs.title: New verification observation
outputs.text: Evaluation creates a separate immutable report for the actual policy and time instead of editing the original pack. Numerical agreement and domain eligibility stay distinct.

outputs.title: Readable inspection and rendering
outputs.text: Consumers must see complete claims, reasons, quantities, references and unavailable states. Inspection/rendering must not execute a received programme or grant eligibility.

outputs.title: Review chain with explicit unavailable states
outputs.text: The target deliverable connects preserved job bytes and custody facts, a bound numerical derivation and a separately immutable verification report to readable inspection/rendering. Complete quantities, reasons and source references must remain visible, including missing information. The seven domain operations are required semantics under construction; this illustration adds no accepted quantum-job result or executable implementation.

components.title: Capture — completed observations and their origin
components.text: The domain workflow is being built around completed-result producers. Capture must retain original result bytes alongside separate acquisition and custody facts: job identity, timestamps, calibration associations and quantity inventories. A declared provider or requested resource cannot stand in for an observed event.

components.title: Import — preserve meaning across representations
components.text: Import must preserve foreign/native originals, original representations, field origin and missing information while providing a normalised reading view. Requested shots, observed totals, counts and probability estimates remain distinct quantities; normalisation must not invent an observation or promote a reported estimate into a count.

components.title: Derive — bind the actual numerical programme
components.text: The required derivation path binds the caller-owned installed programme and environment lock, ordered inputs, complete output schema and scalar inventory, units, precision, comparison rule and optional seed. It validates earlier raw output before later execution/output wrappers. Failure, cancellation or resource refusal retains diagnostics without a successful result. A received artefact cannot choose executable code.

components.title: Seal — shared evidence and domain responsibilities
components.text: The separately owned evidence runtime is responsible for content addressing, canonicalisation, signing and Common evaluation. The pack is responsible for domain comparison and policy conjunction. The intended sealed pack preserves provenance and scope; success at the shared evidence layer does not establish physical measurement qualification or current domain eligibility.

components.title: Verify — a new report for an explicit policy and time
components.text: Verification must create a separate immutable observation, leaving the original pack unchanged. It binds explicit policy/time and the caller-selected unsigned or protected trust context. Actual installed types and selected source versions must agree with the entire request. Historical intervals require genuine event evidence, rather than a later operational evaluation witness.

components.title: Inspect — retain the full reviewable record
components.text: The required inspection view retains complete claims, reasons, quantities, references and unavailable states. It presents preserved observations and evaluation scope without running a received programme or granting eligibility. A reviewer can distinguish numerical agreement, provider assurance, producer authenticity and measurement qualification.

components.title: Render — readable output without changing assurance
components.text: Rendering must escape foreign text and preserve the full scope already present in the record. Assurance follows actual class information, rather than relabelling a declared validation token. This is a passive document-consumer responsibility, separate from execution, scientific acceptance and the still-open standalone domain workflow.

external_roles.title: Completed-result producer
external_roles.text: Owns the original observations and separate custody facts; this explanation does not assign producer ownership to a particular repository.

external_roles.title: Numerical programme and shared evidence runtime
external_roles.text: These are separately owned dependency roles. Their exact installed identities and interfaces must be bound; the explanation does not infer a repository identity from a role name.

limits.title: Agreement is not measurement qualification
limits.text: Numerical agreement, provider assurance, producer authenticity, physical measurement qualification and current eligibility are distinct outcomes.

limits.title: Historical intervals need genuine event sources
limits.text: An operational evaluation witness cannot replace historical event evidence; selected types/source versions must remain consistent with the whole request.

limits.title: A received artefact cannot choose executable code
limits.text: Inspection and rendering are passive; only a caller-owned installed binding can control programme execution. Standalone domain acceptance remains open.

model_layers.title: Observation and representation model
model_layers.text: The pack is an evidence model, not a quantum-state or physical-device simulator. Original bytes and separately supplied acquisition facts support representations of observed/reported quantities. Requested shots, observed totals, probability estimates and counts keep their original meaning and unavailable fields.

model_layers.title: Numerical re-derivation contract
model_layers.text: A numerical comparison is meaningful only for the selected installed programme, environment, input order and complete output contract. Units, precision, comparison and optional seed are part of that contract. Agreement under it does not independently establish the origin or physical quality of the measurements.

model_layers.title: Assurance, domain policy and measurement qualification
model_layers.text: Content addressing, canonicalisation, signing and Common evaluation concern the shared evidence layer. Domain comparison and policy conjunction belong to the pack. Provider assurance, producer authenticity, measurement qualification and current eligibility are distinct decisions; one successful layer cannot substitute for the others.

model_layers.title: Historical events and a current evaluation
model_layers.text: A report evaluates a particular policy, time and caller-selected trust context. It is a new immutable observation, not a rewrite of the original job. A later operational witness cannot supply missing historical events or silently change the source/type bindings of the complete request.

Those checks do not demonstrate capture/import/derive/seal/verify/inspect/render domain acceptance. Current architecture files still identify that standalone implementation as not integrated. purpose.text: Provide one versioned mathematical and geometry substrate for reactor-family projects, so shared primitives do not become separate, drifting implementations inside each device model.

scope.text: The captured source exposes geometry, deterministic numerics and optional CAD adapters at computational-prototype scope. The broader shared-physics remit is not an inventory of completed kernels. The source keeps its claim inventory empty and supplies no reactor solver or controller. This update inspects source; it does not rerun geometry, CAD, parity or scientific validation.

implementation.title: STL and glTF/GLB with explicit precision boundaries
implementation.text: Both mesh exporters store positions as float32 while the canonical mesh digest identifies the float64 mesh representation. The source checks the geometry that storage would preserve. GLB can retain a body in local coordinates with a node translation; STL has no transform and requires an explicit caller-owned translation when rebasing. Unsupported storage is refused rather than silently presented as an unchanged body.

implementation.text: The optional CAD lane builds ordered B-rep assemblies, exports STEP with native metre unit contexts, facets solids back into the mesh contract and meshes STEP into MSH 4.1 tetrahedra. The volume-mesh contract uses metre coordinates/cell size and cubic-metre volumes, with explicit gmsh session ownership. CAD determinism is scoped to a pinned environment; independent Python/Rust bit parity is not claimed for third-party CAD kernels.

implementation.title: Petri-net compilation with an explicit export boundary
implementation.text: FusionCompiler builds ordered dense input/output matrices, transition thresholds, delays and initial marking, with packed stochastic weights when the optional SC-NeuroCore path is available. A CompiledNet retains dense and packed representations. Export adds the control tick, feature injection and action readout configuration. A structure may admit inhibitor arcs for formal work while controller artefact export refuses those arcs until its topology format can represent them.

implementation.title: Observation-to-action execution at one control tick
implementation.text: The shared feature kernel normalises (target minus observation) by declared scales, clamps the signed error and splits positive/negative channels. NeuroSymbolicController injects those features into places, evaluates its selected stochastic path and optionally a float oracle, then decodes action channels with gain, slew-rate and absolute limits. The method returns named commands to its caller; that return does not itself establish a physical actuator connection.

implementation.title: Traceable vectors and conditional deadline handling
implementation.text: The source also supplies fixed-order observation-vector execution for axis-only injection configurations. Optional JSONL records retain observations, features, firings, marking, actions and measured timing. When a runtime-bound certificate supplies a deadline monitor and strict handling is selected, a deadline overrun restores control-relevant cycle state; strict execution refuses synchronous file logging. These are mode-specific software contracts, not a universal guarantee that every caller is deadline-admitted.

implementation.title: A separate stateful exact-current LIF profile
implementation.text: The compiler can explicitly bind an additional persistent exact-current runtime to a specific SC-NeuroCore profile, distribution, units, source digests and commits. The captured guide pins sc-neurocore 3.16.0; this is the consumer contract in that source, not a latest-release claim. Membrane voltage, shot identity/time and reset epoch persist, and complete packets/checkpoints retain the declared transition order. This deterministic reference profile does not replace the established stateless lif_fire Petri gate or admit arbitrary stochastic/adaptive models.

Admission also requires the matching live binding/target and successful proof replay. Hardware campaign policies separately distinguish off, warn and require: workstation warnings and parsed historical reports cannot establish a qualified live host. These records prepare further review; they do not supply facility safety approval.

implementation.title: Domain contracts and separate signal-extraction surfaces
implementation.text: A BindingSpec declares hierarchy, oscillator families, coupling, drivers, objectives, boundaries, actuator mappings and sample/control periods. Signal extractors accept waveforms, event timestamps or symbolic state sequences and produce typed phase/frequency/amplitude/quality records under algorithm-specific meanings. This extraction surface is distinct from the generic CLI simulation: spo run validates a research-tier binding and calls simulate, whose model starts from seed-generated phases and declared frequencies. A source-file declaration alone does not establish measured-signal ingestion by that loop.

implementation.title: Coupled phase or amplitude evolution
implementation.text: The generic loop builds coupling and phase-lag matrices, then selects a phase engine or the binding’s amplitude-mode Stuart-Landau model. UPDE inputs retain oscillator cardinality, phase/frequency units, coupling, lag and external drive; documented integrators include Euler, RK4 and adaptive RK45. Per-layer coherence and boundary diagnostics describe the selected model. Optional engine/backend routes have their own input, output and availability contracts; this source inspection does not freshly qualify them.

implementation.title: Projected proposals close a loop inside the model
implementation.text: At each configured control interval, the supervisor and optional adjacent policy rules evaluate model diagnostics. ActionProjector constrains proposals before the generic loop applies supported coupling/drive changes to its next model state. policy_enabled=False supplies the open-loop baseline; the only generic live control_mode is supervisor_policy. A calibrated conformal gate needs the caller’s matching confidence source and can suppress an action set. None of this loop opens a hardware connection or assigns facility control authority.

implementation.title: Audit, replay and result records retain distinct checks
implementation.text: SimulationResult retains final phases, optional amplitudes, good/bad coherence histories, regime, boundary/action counts and optional audit-stream integrity. AuditLogger writes a SHA-256-chained JSONL record and can also write a protobuf stream. HMAC signatures depend on a supplied audit key; production-mode construction requires it, while unsigned-development records are allowed. An attached stream is checked at run end, with strict failure enabled by default. Chain/replay correspondence does not establish sensor truth, qualified timing or permission to actuate.

implementation.title: Reactor semantics is a separate review handoff
implementation.text: SPO owns typed reactor-semantic interpretation and comparability. Fusion/MIF producers retain responsibility for their values, units, frames, clocks, calibration and provenance; CONTROL owns its separate evidence admission. Carrier types distinguish phase, events, noncyclic features, model coordinates and review evidence. Configuration assignment or an observability candidate is descriptive; it does not establish an active producer, a qualified physical phase or a control action.

purpose.text: Timestamp complete control-loop or accelerator events in FPGA fabric so scheduling, computation, loop latency, deadline response and energy can be studied with one reproducible run identity.

scope.text: The instrument is in development. Source describes implemented capture, buffer, controller, simulation and host-analysis components, while the qualified instrument remains architecture_only and no board measurement exists. This map reads source; it does not run the instrument or qualify physical clocks, processor timing, power acquisition, safety or the unfinished neural workflow.

inputs.title: Declared event vocabulary and one capture timebase
inputs.text: CONTROL records sample readiness/read, timely and late actuator commands, deadlines, safe state and faults. COMPUTE has input/start/done/output/interrupt events. Each run binds the actual event-domain snapshot, profile and cycle identity; a timestamp is meaningful within that declared timebase.

inputs.title: Controller, plant and run configuration
inputs.text: Placement, controller coefficients, mechanical/thermal fixed-point plant, sample period, warm-up, load and fault schedule belong to the run. Native or ISA execution in simulated transactions still declares rtl_simulation; host monotonic timestamps do not become fabric ticks.

inputs.title: Original event bytes and completion/loss status
inputs.text: The host needs complete 16-byte little-endian records, source/build artefacts, manifest hashes and final coherent loss/status information before reset. A completion receipt cannot fill missing events or repair an invalid run.

inputs.title: Power acquisition with its own provenance
inputs.text: Driver/BSP revision, rail/shunt mappings, units, sample configuration and per-read host/fabric brackets accompany PAC1934 acquisition. Its raw journal is distinct from a qualified power series; no physical acquisition or aligned energy result is established here.

outputs.title: Source-bound run package
outputs.text: Event bytes, optional tracking/power series and a versioned manifest retain the exact run-domain, configuration and referenced artefacts. Actual native source/context bindings belong to the original acquisition. This explanation creates no new run package.

outputs.title: Latency distributions with explicit denominators
outputs.text: Scheduling is SAMPLE_READ minus SAMPLE_READY; compute is ACT_WRITE minus SAMPLE_READ; loop latency is ACT_WRITE minus SAMPLE_READY. Reports retain sample counts, duration, distributions and deadline/fault response. Missing observations remain visible.

outputs.title: Jitter and tracking with bounded coverage
outputs.text: Adjacent-cycle jitter uses the absolute change in the same complete post-warm-up interval, without bridging gaps; peak-to-peak spread is separate. Tracking RMS/peak describes observed samples when declared, with expected/observed/missing coverage and an invalid partial run.

outputs.title: Window-mean energy and scoped reports
outputs.text: Energy is averaged over many cycles and reported per rail and together, not per core or as an atomic per-cycle rail snapshot. JSON/CSV/SVG reports retain simulation or unverified board-declaration scope; a valid file structure cannot supply independent board acceptance.

outputs.title: Visible failure and refusal evidence
outputs.text: Overflow remains invalid even if capture later recovers. Saturated drop counters are lower bounds; missing records cannot establish an absent actuator write or reconstruct an interval. Reset flushes the run, so status custody precedes reset.

components.title: Sampled plant or generic accelerator slot
components.text: Mechanical/thermal emulation and PID/LQR exercise the CONTROL path. COMPUTE exercises a generic slot with a fixed-latency test peripheral; accelerator-specific adapters remain in the accelerator repository.

components.title: Timestamp capture and event arbitration
components.text: The single-event capture samples the pre-increment counter value into a fixed record. Simultaneous control strobes require upstream retention/arbitration; shared-counter channels use separate FIFOs and the same capture timestamp.

components.title: Dual-clock buffering and common run reset
components.text: Gray-pointer FIFO flags are conservative across clocks; capture does not stall the measured source. Overflow drops the newest pending record. Shared reset flushes both domains, and processor status requires a coherent snapshot.

components.title: Deadline, safe-state and injected faults
components.text: The monitor records misses and applies the configured safe value after consecutive misses. Injected interrupt delays/drops, actuator freezes and overload requests have explicit event identities. Emulated safe-state behaviour is distinct from a physical machine-protection system.

components.title: Native/logger and separate power acquisition
components.text: Linux, dedicated-hart and fabric placements have distinct source/runtime bindings. A logger drains events and retains status; a separate power worker preserves individual acquisition brackets. Processor and I/O qualification is still open.

components.title: Manifest verification and host interpretation
components.text: The host verifies bytes against their manifest/domain, then derives reports with count, duration and missing-data meaning. Simulated fabric timing and host elapsed runtime remain separate clocks and evidence classes.

connections.text: Neuro owns adapters that place its generated peripherals into the instrument's device-under-test slot. Loop Timing owns the measurement interface/manifest, not Neuro models or code.

limits.title: An instrument in progress is not a measured board result
limits.text: Implemented source and described simulations do not qualify physical clocks, CDC, processor placements, I/O, control quality or power. architecture_only is the source qualification state, while development is actively in progress.

limits.title: Loss remains a measurement failure
limits.text: Nonzero overflow invalidates the run; saturating counts are lower bounds and drain frequency alone cannot establish throughput. Completion receipts do not reconstruct missing event pairs.

limits.title: Energy is window-aligned and whole-rail
limits.text: Sequential rail reads do not share an exact instant, and the core rail supplies both processors and fabric. Power units, window timing and calibration need qualification; energy per cycle is a window mean rather than an atomic per-cycle/per-core observation.

limits.title: This map supplies documentary correspondence
limits.text: The cited architecture reading retains its earlier date; newly selected document/code readings carry current byte fingerprints. The evolving neural document is an uncommitted source observation pending owner acceptance. No instrument, neural experiment, benchmark, proof or hardware run was executed for this update.

implementation.title: The capture module stores the original counter tick
implementation.text: event_record_capture increments its 64-bit counter each active edge, forwards event_valid as record_valid and stores counter_ticks, cycle_number, zero reserved fields and event_code when an event is present. Nonblocking assignments retain the pre-increment tick; capture pipeline/drain latency does not replace it.

implementation.title: Buffering preserves accepted records and exposes loss
implementation.text: The documented single-channel witness connects capture to the dual-clock FIFO. A full FIFO drops the newest pending record, sets sticky overflow and increments a saturating counter. The port consumes one event tuple per edge; simultaneous source events must be handled before it.

implementation.title: Shared-counter capture is a generic instrument surface
implementation.text: The committed generic shared-counter design gives independent channels the same pre-increment timebase, with channel-specific attempt/accepted/drop/drain status and common reset. The inspected document also describes evolving neural decoding/correlation components; their presence is not complete neural-run or producer/encoder qualification.

implementation.title: The software/RTL loop has a declared simulation clock
implementation.text: The described integrated plants, fixed-point controllers, native commands and dedicated-hart capture use simulated transactions and explicit production-source bindings. Native host computation does not automatically advance model time, and these routes do not measure physical U54 scheduling or device I/O.

implementation.title: Analysis refuses to invent missing observations
implementation.text: The source-described host pipeline validates run/domain/input bindings before deriving intervals, tracking and reports. Native completion counters are reconciled with captured events; loss cannot be repaired using the receipt. Adjacent jitter pairs exclude warm-up and missing-cycle gaps.

implementation.title: Power logging retains acquisition rather than claiming calibrated energy
implementation.text: The documented PAC1934 IIO worker validates selected driver/configuration and retains raw attributes with individual read brackets. Sequential reads are not an atomic rail snapshot; the journal needs separate board acquisition and window-alignment qualification before use as measured energy.

Their tracking error describes the emulated plant, not a physical reactor or general device model. COMPUTE describes accelerator event intervals, not a model-specific numerical verdict.

model_layers.text: Latency, adjacent jitter, spread, observed tracking error and window-mean energy answer different questions. Counts, duration, coverage and alignment determine the scope; neither missing pairs nor missing power observations are filled with a substitute.

model_layers.text: The declared 100 MHz capture clock and 10 ns tick are design settings, not demonstrated board resolution or timing closure. RTL functional checks, normalized synthesis/equivalence, device CDC/placement, same-bitstream acceptance and external metrology remain distinct evidence.

Those trusted-caller premises are not created by parsing a received success flag or producer timestamp.

inputs.text: The caller supplies receipt bytes in original order. Signed sealing requires signing request, actual signer and current trust together; unsigned construction is an explicitly different selection. UTC token validity does not qualify the clock, and signer configuration cannot enroll an implementation.

outputs.title: Canonical content and selected byte reference
outputs.text: canonicalize_json returns complete canonical JSON bytes; reference_bytes binds the selected raw or canonical basis without storing input or registering a schema. Different representation identities must not be silently substituted.

outputs.title: Passive inspection and comparison
outputs.text: inspect returns declarations/diagnostics with acceptance not_evaluated. diff retains both content identities, changed pointers and ordered receipt identities. Neither operation authenticates a receipt or grants evidence eligibility.

outputs.title: Unsigned content or a separately checked detached envelope
outputs.text: SealResult keeps canonical_content, content_ref and envelope_json. The unsigned result has no envelope; a signed result checks current authority before invoking the actual signer and verifies the returned complete-message signature. Failed signing does not produce an unsigned fallback.

outputs.title: All fifteen verification fields
outputs.text: VerificationReport separately retains content/policy/registry identities, evaluation mode/time, evaluated claims, structure, integrity, authenticity, availability, common_eligibility, domain_verdict, current_eligibility, reference observations and reasons. The common runtime leaves domain_verdict as not_evaluated.

outputs.title: Complete immutable local transport result
outputs.text: The offline grammar describes a fresh seal directory or exclusively created report file. Complete JSON output, typed refusals and failure precedence remain visible. Publication success or exit zero cannot clear failed gates or establish scientific/current acceptance.

components.text: Strict content handling and explicit bounds distinguish original bytes, canonical content and metadata declarations. Shape, length and digest are checked when actual source bytes are acquired.

components.title: Static registry and bounded reference closure
components.text: The caller selects schema bytes, dependencies, reference paths and common semantics. Resolver reads share the operation budget and preserve exact missing full references or digest-only requests. An artifact URL is not an instruction to fetch code or a filesystem path.

components.title: Read-only inspection and difference
components.text: These operations expose declarations and differences without installing trust, authenticating receipts or silently converting an observation into an acceptance verdict.

components.text: Four CLI grammars handle explicit local inputs/object store and fresh output destinations. Repository metadata/dependency/workflow guards remain distinct checks and do not implement evidence acceptance or prove hosted execution.

external_roles.text: Scientific or engineering consumers supply the domain judgement the common report deliberately does not evaluate. A need for a common runtime, including the QPU domain contract, is not proof of a qualified installed binding to EMT. No new project connection is asserted here.

implementation.title: The public module exposes six documented operations
implementation.text: The inspected facade exports canonicalize_json, reference_bytes, inspect, diff, seal and verify with explicit public value types. The documented four CLI commands transport seal/verify/inspect/diff; canonicalisation and byte-reference construction are Python functions rather than additional claimed CLI grammars.

implementation.title: Sealing checks configuration and required content before producing a result
implementation.text: seal validates Limits, registry/schema selection and all-or-none signing options, then creates one ReferenceBudget, validates the schema registry and prepares the complete content. Missing closure or content reasons refuse construction. Only the explicitly unsigned branch returns an envelope-free SealResult.

implementation.title: Signed construction invokes a selected signer after authority checks
implementation.text: The signed branch constructs the complete statement, initializes the local verifier and obtains the allowed key through signing_public_key before sign_statement is called. It returns the resulting detached envelope with the same canonical content/reference; no failed-signer retry into the unsigned branch appears in this path.

implementation.title: Verification retains the whole selected claim and receipt context
implementation.text: verify passes complete bytes, ordered envelopes, schema, resolver, limits, policy and trust into acquire_verification_inputs. It selects trust state under the same operation budget, derives actual content claim IDs, evaluates each supplied envelope through receipt_authority and composes the complete report. This is inspected source flow, not a new successful verification run.

implementation.title: Offline acquisition is local and bounded
implementation.text: The CLI document describes a read-only digest-addressed object directory, anchored descriptor, regular-file/no-symlink checks and bounded reads. Repeated signature flags preserve caller order; signatures are not silently discovered in the store. Unavailable signer/provider paths retain their distinct failure semantics.

implementation.title: Output creation and exit status retain their own meaning
implementation.text: The documented local directory publisher uses no-replacement publication on the supported Linux/filesystem route; existing destinations survive. Failures after publication can leave a complete immutable output while returning I/O failure, so retry requires a new destination. Refusal reports can be published successfully without becoming accepted evidence.

limits.text: The documented PyZX QASM2 parser route can lose global phase and cannot establish unitary_exact. A total injection or an exact byte replay does not qualify ancilla states, isometry or quantum equivalence. Shared conversion code is not independent corroboration.

implementation.title: Read the actual compiler and checker source surfaces

implementation.title: Byte comparison preserves unmodified output identity
implementation.text: compare_replay_bytes accepts immutable bytes or actual None. It returns unavailable if either side is missing, the first differing offset for unequal bytes, the shorter prefix length when only file lengths differ, or equal with actual lengths. It never normalises QPY serialisation or treats empty bytes as missing.

implementation.title: Mapping checks an explicit total injection
implementation.text: assess_mapping validates positive plain integer widths, retains None as unavailable, requires a tuple and separates completeness, range, injectivity and surjectivity. A valid total injection can have unequal source/target widths. It does not infer ancilla state, measurement order, isometry or equivalence.

implementation.title: Routing requires two complete explicit bijections
implementation.text: routing_permutation refuses missing maps, checks both initial/final maps at the full declared width and derives initial physical slot to final physical slot through the common source slot. It cannot manufacture identity routing when a map is absent.

implementation.title: Engine replay checks original problem and distinct execution
implementation.text: compare_engine_replay reads actual first/replay raw sources under the same VerificationReads budget, checks complete selected pair/profile/semantics/environment/inputs/conversion references, joins the original problem, and requires witness versus evaluation request stages, a distinct raw reference/run and the same engine identity. Stored normalisation is recomputed by the source reader.

implementation.title: Replay state preserves negative and undecided outcomes
implementation.text: The inspected comparison returns unavailable if either execution lacks a usable native result or reports no_information; different definite native verdicts diverge and equal definite verdicts match. A matching not_equivalent observation is still negative. These rows and prepared candidate captures supply no whole evaluator, scientific, Clock or current-admission verdict.

model_layers.text: Ordered callbacks and SDK/layout state describe a compilation. Exact raw-output equality is a distinct fact; repeated QPY serialisation can differ even when observed circuit/layout state agrees. Neither observation is a compiler-wide determinism or quantum correctness proof.

model_layers.text: QCEC phase/probabilistic vocabulary and PyZX reduction outcomes retain native meaning. Engine replay compares observations of the same original problem in distinct runs; a consistent negative remains negative, and shared converter logic remains correlated.

purpose.text: Own conventional and spherical tokamak device declarations: configuration, shot lifecycle, diagnostic meaning and device model records, while keeping shared solvers, control admission and protection under their respective owners.

model_layers.text: Exact B-rep construction and STEP export retain the same reduced scope; they do not add fabrication tolerances, material loads, a field map, poloidal coils or a qualified engineering design.

The device supplies typed review-only semantics and data-only registry pins; those declarations do not form an actuation permission.
The device owns an adapter specification; CONTROL forms admitted software actions, and independent machine protection keeps the final plant veto. Studio portfolio federation remains separate.

model_layers.title: Observation geometry — coordinate meaning
model_layers.text: Flux/Boozer/laboratory frames and their declared transformations specify meaning and planned acquisition geometry. A transformation declaration is not an evaluated equilibrium mapping.

model_layers.title: Shared 3D physics — separately owned solver scope
model_layers.text: Fusion currently owns the shared 3D equilibrium and stellarator solver surfaces; the device architecture lists no active versioned solver seam. The device inventory does not list local level-0/mesh/CAD capabilities.

connections.text: Shared 3D equilibrium and stellarator solver mathematics remain with Fusion, pending exact consumer/migration acceptance.
Data-only reactor/observability pins align declaration meaning; typed semantics are review-only and ingress remains not_declared in the diagnostic evidence record.
The device-owned adapter is specification-only, while CONTROL owns admitted software actions and independent protection retains the final veto.
A derived portfolio descriptor describes presentation scope; the source architecture keeps federation not_federated rather than treating the descriptor as a deployed integration.

limits.title: Synthetic plans remain declarations
limits.text: No diagnostic channel describes a real facility; hard synthetic scope survives envelopes, typed frames and clock relations.

limits.title: Topology does not qualify transformations or clocks
limits.text: Methods/quantity-unit tokens and connected graphs do not prove SI/UCUM validation, numerical frame correspondence or mapping to physical wall time.

limits.title: 3D domain meaning is not local 3D simulation
limits.text: The two-capability inventory and solver-owner seam keep configuration/observation declarations separate from evaluated field/transport/stability or engineering CAD results.

source_notes.title: Inventory description needs reconciliation
source_notes.text: The machine-readable inventory and architecture introduction list two capabilities, but the architecture layout still calls the inventory empty. This descriptive inconsistency is retained for source-owner review.

purpose.text: Own laser-driven inertial-fusion device declarations for direct drive, indirect hohlraum drive and staged fast/shock ignition, including shot lifecycle, diagnostic semantics and declared capsule/model records.

scope.text: The current inventory lists five computational-prototype capabilities and no scientific claims. Level-0 relations and pre-drive geometry describe declared inputs; they are separate from solving radiation hydrodynamics or predicting an actual shot.

inputs.title: Driver and capsule configuration
inputs.text: The device configuration owns laser energy/pulse/wavelength and outer capsule radius; a separate capsule declaration owns layer thicknesses and fuel inventory. Micrometre input lengths convert once to metre geometry.

inputs.title: Declared implosion outcome
inputs.text: In-flight shell state, burnup fraction and other implosion quantities are supplied inputs to algebraic definitions. The package does not calculate the implosion that would produce them.

inputs.title: Optional hohlraum and model resolution
inputs.text: An enclosure is mandatory for indirect drive and refused for the two directly driven identifiers. Case dimensions and independent segment/ring resolutions belong to the selected geometry scope.

outputs.title: Device and synthetic diagnostic records
outputs.text: Configuration, shot-relative timing and observation declarations retain registry-bound device semantics without becoming measured diagnostics or a protection path.

outputs.title: Level-0 ignition and inventory record
outputs.text: The record evaluates necessary ignition conditions, implosion definitions, fuel inventory and declared-input yield/gain. It reports source-prescribed conditions and discrepancies rather than forecasting a successful shot.

outputs.title: Pre-drive G1 capsule/hohlraum mesh
outputs.text: The record contains three ordered concentric capsule bodies; indirect drive adds a fourth hohlraum-wall body. Exact input/digest/units and profile/resolution meaning remain part of the result.

outputs.title: Optional G2 CAD assembly and STEP
outputs.text: The selected backend supplies B-rep bodies, assembly manifest, analytic/faceted/G1 comparisons and normalised STEP bytes with backend/version/digest identity. These remain pre-drive simplified bodies.

components.title: Configuration and shot semantics
components.text: Resolve the owned drive identifier and driver/target declarations, preserving the distinction between direct, indirect and staged energy delivery.

components.title: Algebraic physics composition
components.text: Evaluate ignition conditions, implosion definitions and inventory/yield/gain from explicit inputs with their source-prescribed conditions.

components.title: Layer geometry construction
components.text: Derive capsule radii from their original owners, convert units once and refuse incompatible layering or enclosure configuration.

components.title: Mesh, CAD and byte identity
components.text: Preserve ordered bodies, independent resolutions, original input digests, backend scope and refusal observations rather than silently changing a model to fit an anchor.

model_layers.title: Configuration and diagnostics — declared shot
model_layers.text: Pulse/drive/capsule and synthetic shot-relative observation semantics describe the experimental boundary. Their existence does not imply data acquired from a laser facility.

model_layers.title: Level-0 physics — necessary algebraic conditions
model_layers.text: Hot-spot thresholds, efficiency/convergence definitions and inventory relations retain declared inputs. Ignition floors do not predict ignition; declared burnup is not a computed burn solution.

model_layers.title: G1 representation — pre-drive layers
model_layers.text: Inscribed bodies of revolution describe ablator, solid fuel and vapour, plus the indirect-drive enclosure. The generating profile is their analytic reference; ideal-sphere formulas describe different solids.

model_layers.title: G2 representation — optional backend solids
model_layers.text: CAD compares the same shapes with analytic and G1 evidence and exports version-bound STEP. It does not add engineering loads, roughness, layer non-uniformity or fabrication tolerance.

model_layers.title: Whole-shot dynamics — outside this package
model_layers.text: Radiation hydrodynamics, transport, laser-plasma interaction and burn calculations are not performed locally. Shared solver mathematics remain owned by Fusion and require an accepted versioned seam.

connections.text: Implosion hydrodynamics, radiation transport and burn solver ownership remain with Fusion until exact migration/consumer gates accept a seam.
The two spatial tiers use the shared geometry/CAD groups while this device owns capsule/enclosure meaning and family-specific evidence limits.
Typed device and timing semantics remain review-only declarations tied to the source registry boundary.
The device-owned adapter is specification-only and campaign/shot-level; CONTROL admission and independent machine-protection veto stay separately owned.

limits.title: Algebraic yield is conditional on declared input
limits.text: Yield/gain follow a supplied fuel inventory and burn fraction. Printed source values that do not reconstruct from the stated inputs remain discrepancies, not values repaired by tuning an input.

limits.title: Geometry is before the drive, not during implosion
limits.text: Uniform concentric layers and a plain enclosure omit fill tube, stalk, roughness, layer variation and engineering features. No dimension describes or validates an actual shot.

limits.title: Backend limits do not transfer across scales
limits.text: The source retains measured mixed ring-count regimes and the cause of parity remains unknown. The conservative default, radius-dependent refusal boundary and pinned backend scope cannot become universal CAD settings.

source_notes.title: Current inventory and earlier summary differ
source_notes.text: README/current inventory list five capabilities, while the architecture introduction describes two. ADR 0005 records its own earlier three-capability step; the later CAD/mesh records extend it. This guide keeps those chronology/source scopes visible rather than counting every historical statement as current.

purpose.text: Develop the component boundary that turns supported neural equations and intermediate representations into numerical hardware artefacts, co-simulation/equivalence collateral and selected ASIC export workflows.

scope.text: This is a named extraction destination in the group map. The source described here is the current SC-NeuroCore workbench; it does not establish a separately installed SC-NC-COMPILER package or completed migration.

inputs.title: Declared equation or network representation
inputs.text: A validated EquationNeuron or supported NIR/SCNetwork graph supplies equations, committed state, weights, delays, thresholds and network structure. The selected integration method retains its own recurrence semantics.

inputs.title: Explicit numerical policy
inputs.text: Q-format widths, fractional bits, product rounding, overflow and LUT domains are selected contracts. Stochastic threshold sampling does not provide an implicit random source for product rounding.

inputs.title: Target and external toolchain
inputs.text: Profile settings, work directory and actual external tools define the selected flow. Compiler metadata alone cannot establish a target’s physical behaviour.

outputs.title: Model-specific generated representations
outputs.text: The source describes registered or folded Verilog, SC-NIR bundles, MLIR lowering and top-level assembly. These are distinct selected paths rather than a guarantee that every model completes every stage.

outputs.title: Numerical and verification collateral
outputs.text: Precision planning, fixed-point lowering, formal/testbench and hardware numerical contracts retain their selected model and state/event scope. A LUT size is not a global accuracy percentage.

outputs.title: Tool-produced reports and export artefacts
outputs.text: Synthesis/P&R/ASIC paths require actual tool results. Generated paths or source-line counts do not supply area, timing, power or energy evidence.

components.title: Graph and recurrence lowering
components.text: Preserve network structure and the chosen Euler, sequential Euler, RK4, exponential-Euler or direct-map meaning before hardware emission.

components.title: Fixed-point expression generation
components.text: Share product-rounding and LUT geometry across emitted integer/RTL paths, retaining unsupported input/domain refusals.

components.title: Public compiler facade
components.text: Consumers use documented facade or direct-public modules. Compatibility facades and internal build tools have different stability boundaries.

components.title: External-flow orchestration
components.text: Resolve actual executable tools and their output status. Missing synthesis/P&R artefacts remain evidence gaps, not successful hardware compilation.

model_layers.title: Source model and recurrence
model_layers.text: The selected numerical recurrence defines state evolution; sequential and simultaneous updates are not interchangeable.

model_layers.title: Fixed-point and RTL representation
model_layers.text: Widths, rounding, overflow and LUT domains define the emitted numerical system. Their model-level state/event correspondence needs scoped co-simulation evidence.

model_layers.title: EDA result and physical implementation
model_layers.text: Generated RTL/MLIR and external tool artefacts are intermediate results. A device implementation requires its own synthesis, placement, timing, power and physical evidence.

connections.text: The public workbench is the current implementation/integration home; the destination names ownership under construction rather than an already extracted release.
Target profiles, mapping/adapters and deployment are a separately named component responsibility; compiler output crosses an explicit consumer boundary.
Formal checks and fault/resilience verification retain their own scope; compiler collateral does not supply a blanket verification or safety verdict.

limits.title: A pipeline list is not universal completion
limits.text: The source lists multiple frontends, representations and external tools. Installed availability, supported model semantics and completed artefacts need exact per-flow evidence.

limits.title: Local timings are not production performance
limits.text: The compiler timing record comes from a loaded, unreserved workstation. The source expressly keeps it as local regression context and reports no maintained cross-language compiler timing comparison.

limits.title: The component name grants no new release or licence
limits.text: Independent packaging, migration and commercial boundaries remain separately decided. Parent implementation facts cannot become a standalone component release claim.

external_roles.title: EDA toolchain and target owners
