external_roles.text: Actual external tool versions, constraints, synthesis/P&R/timing/power reports and target-specific consumer qualification are required for physical conclusions.

source_notes.title: Rounding support differs between source pages
source_notes.text: The general hardware-profile guide describes stochastic rounding using an external LFSR; the current equation-to-Verilog API says public emitters reject that policy because they do not own the required rounding source. Read support at the exact emitter boundary.

purpose.text: Develop target profiles, mapping, adapters, drivers and physical deployment boundaries that connect selected neuromorphic computations with their intended hardware environment.

scope.text: Current source surfaces are in SC-NeuroCore. Hardware profiles and chip emulators describe numerical/target constraints; named platforms do not by themselves qualify vendor specifications, installed drivers or physical deployment.

inputs.title: Selected hardware profile
inputs.text: The profile supplies identity, platform class, signed width/fraction, rounding/overflow and DSP constraints. Selection is configuration metadata with its own supported consumer path.

inputs.title: Generated computation and interface
inputs.text: Supported compiler/HDL outputs, wrappers and driver contracts must match the selected model and target. A profile name does not resolve an arbitrary hardware instruction path.

inputs.title: Actual implementation and measurement evidence
inputs.text: Tool versions, constraints, physical flow and matching raw/report artefacts define what hardware claim can be made for the selected deployment.

outputs.title: Target-specific numerical configuration
outputs.text: Public profile lookup/listing exposes the selected target’s metadata through the established compiler.platforms API without importing private registration internals.

outputs.title: Integration collateral
outputs.text: The parent describes HDL assembly, target-oriented drivers and deployment/ASIC collateral. Their existence is separate from installing and exercising a genuine device consumer.

outputs.title: Scoped hardware evidence
outputs.text: Matching synthesis/placement/timing/power and physical-device records support their own selected claims. Configuration/emulation cannot replace those records.

components.title: Profile registry and public interface
components.text: Preserve metadata values, insertion order and duplicate-name refusal while keeping private registration modules behind the public lookup facade.

components.title: Chip emulation
components.text: Model a selected target’s neuron dynamics, precision and routing limits as an emulator, retaining the distinction from the physical device.

components.title: Interface and driver integration
components.text: Join supported generated hardware and model contracts with the selected wrapper/driver path. Independent package extraction remains a separate transition.

components.title: Implementation evidence boundary
components.text: Retain target/model/Q-format/tool/constraint identity and actual reports rather than treating a successful configuration lookup as a device result.

model_layers.title: Profile — selected numerical metadata
model_layers.text: A named platform encodes configuration choices. It does not prove vendor documentation correspondence or a qualified deployment.

model_layers.title: Emulator — target behaviour model
model_layers.text: The chip abstraction simulates selected dynamics and routing constraints; it is not a physical chip observation.

model_layers.title: RTL and tool flow — selected implementation
model_layers.text: Generated RTL, synthesis/P&R and driver artefacts carry their own tool and model scope before any board claim.

model_layers.title: Device — measured physical result
model_layers.text: A physical claim requires matching committed evidence for the actual device and flow, not an emulator or theoretical profile maximum.

connections.text: The workbench currently integrates these surfaces and is the source of the described APIs and workflows.
Compiler responsibilities deliver selected representations and collateral that hardware integration must consume under exact numerical and target contracts.
The group map separately assigns physical timing to Loop Timing; deployment-profile metadata is not a measured latency or energy result.
Simulation-to-fabric divergence is a separately named measurement tool scope, not a conclusion supplied by the hardware profile.

limits.title: Overflow trap is simulation-only in this source path
limits.text: The documented trap assertion is guarded by synthesis translate_off and stripped for synthesis. It does not become a runtime hardware protection mechanism merely because the profile selects trap.

limits.title: No implied board support or vendor qualification
limits.text: Profiles describe target settings; emulators describe selected dynamics. Genuine installed target/driver/measurement paths still need their own evidence.

limits.title: Safety and physical claims keep their scope
limits.text: Source evidence organisation and formal collateral do not certify a device or convert generated line counts into timing/power/energy.

external_roles.title: Physical implementation and measurement partners
external_roles.text: Target toolchains, real device/driver integration and matching raw measurement reports are separately required to support device conclusions. These are roles, not procurement commitments or settled quantities.

source_notes.title: Profile policy is not emitter availability
source_notes.text: The general profile vocabulary includes stochastic rounding, while the equation-to-Verilog API refuses it at its public emitter boundary. A consumer must resolve the selected backend rather than infer support from the enum.

purpose.text: Develop workload-specific benchmark suites and immutable run evidence so each neuromorphic result remains tied to the actual workload, numerical contract and execution environment.

scope.text: The named extraction destination is distinct from the current parent benchmark corpus and from the shared NEURO-EVIDENCE-BENCH plan/result protocol. This explanation reads existing report boundaries without executing or independently accepting any benchmark.

inputs.title: Workload and supported numerical contract
inputs.text: Selected neuron/network/codec/RTL workloads retain their actual precision, input size and comparison scope. Broad package names do not identify a reproducible experiment.

inputs.title: Execution environment
inputs.text: Source/release, Python/Rust/SIMD/backend, affinity, host load, governor and frequency context define the measurement. Historical GPU rows retain the named wheel/device environment.

inputs.title: Original run and tool artefacts
inputs.text: Committed JSON/CSV and named tool reports support public numbers. Local uncommitted observations remain exploratory and missing/skipped tool results remain explicit.

outputs.title: Immutable workload/run evidence
outputs.text: Raw measurements and environment/provenance records preserve the actual run, rather than an unattributed headline speedup.

outputs.title: Scoped regression or performance reports
outputs.text: Loaded-host medians and affinity-pinned runs remain under their documented qualification. Production claims require the stronger isolated-core and recorded-context boundary.

outputs.title: Distinct contract, synthesis and physical results
outputs.text: Formal proof/model-emitter observations, RTL synthesis and physical timing have different meanings. A timeout skip or unavailable runtime is retained rather than converted to a success or board measurement.

components.title: Workload-specific suite
components.text: Own the selected domain workloads and their numerical/comparison assumptions rather than duplicating every shared evidence tool.

components.title: Run capture and reproducibility
components.text: Keep original results with commands, source/environment identity and actual execution status.

components.title: Evidence interpretation
components.text: Separate Python/FFI overhead, native Criterion measurements, loaded-host regression and physical results before comparing numbers.

components.title: Shared consumer protocol
components.text: The separately named shared plan executor/result contract connects suites and Studio; workload ownership remains with this component scope.

model_layers.title: Numerical or contract experiment
model_layers.text: A comparison tests the selected workload and semantic boundary. It does not prove agreement with every source model or hardware target.

model_layers.title: Execution performance experiment
model_layers.text: Timing is tied to environment, affinity/load and FFI/native path. A smoke threshold or loaded run is not a production throughput result.

model_layers.title: Hardware observation
model_layers.text: Synthesis estimates and formal results stay separate from physical-device throughput, latency and energy.

connections.text: The current public workbench retains existing benchmark workloads/results until a qualified component transition establishes separate release interfaces.
The public group map assigns shared benchmark-plan execution and result protocol to this tool; SC-NC-BENCH owns workload suites and their run evidence.
Physical timing instrumentation is separately owned; software benchmark and synthesis timing cannot stand in for its measured device scope.
The source describes Studio as a consumer of shared plan/result contracts, not the owner of workload truth or raw evidence.

limits.title: Do not merge incompatible measurement contexts
limits.text: Different wheels, CPUs, SIMD, workloads, precision or load/affinity conditions require explicit comparison evidence. Historical rows remain historical.

limits.title: Tool completion and physical performance differ
limits.text: Synthesis success, timeout-limited skip, unavailable proof runtime and board measurements retain separate outcomes.

limits.title: Standalone extraction remains separately qualified
limits.text: This component identity does not imply an installed benchmark package, accepted independent consumer or settled commercial licence.

external_roles.title: Reproduction and measurement operators
external_roles.text: Reserved-core/environment capture, actual tool results and matching committed raw reports provide the basis for stronger performance or hardware claims; this guide makes no reservation or purchase.

purpose.text: Build a provenance-preserving record/replay container for ordered events and original source-native side streams, with chunked slog bytes, index, integrity chain and detached evidence.

scope.text: The actual source repository is under construction and declares architecture_only with empty implemented capabilities, claims and qualified schema inventories. The described runtime operations are target contracts, not available writer/replay commands.

inputs.title: Immutable pre-capture plan
inputs.text: The plan exists before source-owned capture. Completed run results reference the plan and container later; a container cannot hash itself or a future result.

inputs.title: Original event and stream identity
inputs.text: Signed integer ticks, geometry, polarity and stream identity retain original ordering, including explicitly unsorted sources. DVS event columns and original APS/IMU/trigger/external side bytes stay distinct.

inputs.title: Declared codecs and replay request
inputs.text: Exact source-native codec identity and complete source population are retained. A parser is required before accepting interpreted external semantics; native/scaled delivery timing is separately observed.

outputs.title: Complete chunked container identity
outputs.text: Header/chunks/index offsets/footer and the integrity chain must be checked against actual bytes, with detached seal and capture provenance.

outputs.title: Inspection, verification and located corruption
outputs.text: Whole-container verification preserves complete structure and identifies damaged regions. Partial recovery retains a new partial identity and visible gaps rather than becoming complete verification.

outputs.title: Logical replay and provenance-preserving slice
outputs.text: Replay preserves original values, ticks and ordering; a slice creates a new content identity with original provenance. Achieved wall-clock delivery is a separate observation.

components.title: Capture-plan and source boundary
components.text: Admit the original immutable plan and source-owned bytes without turning capture provenance into a future result hash.

components.title: Writer, chunks and index
components.text: Build bounded chunked storage with exact offsets, counts and tick bounds under the intended complete container contract.

components.title: Independent complete reader
components.text: Verify header/chunks/index/footer and integrity as one population, preserving located corruption and partial states.

components.title: Replay and slice consumers
components.text: Deliver logical content or a new sliced identity without hiding timing gaps, unknown semantics or changed provenance.

model_layers.title: Byte custody — original recording
model_layers.text: Archiving source bytes preserves identity and population but does not qualify an unknown neural codec. Neural state/spike/service bytes are not DVS pixels.

model_layers.title: Logical replay — content correspondence
model_layers.text: Original values/ticks/order form the logical contract; requested real-time or scaled delivery does not guarantee achieved wall-clock timing.

model_layers.title: Evidence — detached whole-container outcome
model_layers.text: Seals and verification reports refer to the actual complete or explicitly partial container. They do not judge event quality, ground truth or physical capture hardware.

connections.text: The neural workbench owns adapters and model outputs; the recording container retains their bytes/provenance without inventing their semantics.
Third-party event-format conversion and its permitted losses are outside SPIKE-LOG and belong to the separately named format bridge.
Capture instrumentation is separately owned; a recorded stream or replay is not a measurement instrument qualification.
Detached evidence signing is a consumed dependency under its actual class/qualification limits, not a private substitute signer or root.

limits.title: Unknown codec bytes remain uninterpreted
limits.text: An archive can retain exact unknown side-stream bytes while refusing claims about their interpreted neural meaning.

limits.title: Recovery and empty/missing streams differ
limits.text: Partial recovery carries visible gaps and a new partial identity; complete-empty and missing streams are different states.

limits.title: No conversion, quality or physical judgement
limits.text: Container custody/verification does not convert formats, judge event quality, generate ground truth or qualify capture/replay hardware timing.

external_roles.title: Capture and semantic source owners
external_roles.text: Original source/codec/parser and physical capture owners retain their own authority. The container preserves evidence rather than qualifying those owners by archiving their bytes.

source_notes.title: Parent group map and local repository scope differ
source_notes.text: The parent map lists supporting tools as planned, while this captured local SPIKE-LOG tree already contains architecture and repository validation work. Its empty domain inventory still makes no completed runtime claim. Naming, repository existence and qualified implementation remain separate.

purpose.text: Provide the numerical and network foundation that represents neurons, synapses, populations, connectivity, stimuli and ordered simulation steps, so experiments can retain their declared model and state meaning.

scope.text: The component is a named extraction destination under construction. This explanation describes current source surfaces owned by the SC-NeuroCore workbench; independent packaging, migration, supported installed consumers and licensing require their own evidence.

inputs.title: Model identity and configuration
inputs.text: A population supplies a model class or registered name, neuron count and explicit parameters. Distinct population objects retain distinct state even when their configurations match.

inputs.title: Connectivity and temporal contract
inputs.text: Projection CSR arrays, source/target populations, weights and delays determine how events become currents. Uniform and per-synapse delay storage are different contracts.

inputs.title: Stimulus and selected execution profile
inputs.text: Duration, timestep, stimuli, monitors and optional plasticity determine the reference simulation. Backend selection must preserve those semantics and the population configuration.

outputs.title: Events and readable simulation state
outputs.text: Spike monitors retain neuron/timestep events; state and rate monitors provide selected traces and binned firing rates. These observations describe the configured simulation.

outputs.title: Network continuation and reset surfaces
outputs.text: Population stepping, readable state, reset and externally supplied voltages have explicit roles. Matching a class name does not establish that a backend transports every configured or already-evolved state.

outputs.title: Numerical contracts for consumers
outputs.text: Fixed-point widths, fractional scaling, thresholds, reset and refractory conventions must be selected together when comparing Python, native and RTL forms.

components.title: Ordered simulation loop
components.text: The documented reference loop clears currents, applies stimuli and projections, steps neurons and records spikes, then updates plasticity. Optional feedback belongs to that selected model profile.

components.title: Population and sparse projection
components.text: Independent neurons and CSR connectivity retain event/state and temporal semantics; graph shape alone does not encode a scientifically validated connectome.

components.title: Synapse primitives
components.text: The source names static bitstream weighting, STDP, reward-modulated learning and selected stateful/plasticity models. Each named model retains its own update and state contract.

components.title: Monitor and input adapters
components.text: Timed arrays, Poisson inputs, step currents and spike/state/rate monitors define the selected stimulus and observable boundary.

model_layers.title: Neuron and synapse dynamics
model_layers.text: Published-source models and retained project recurrences must keep their own identities, parameter meanings, events and reset conventions.

model_layers.title: Network execution
model_layers.text: Ordered current propagation, delay handling, population stepping and observations define the configured network experiment.

model_layers.title: Native or hardware representation
model_layers.text: Backend dispatch and fixed-point/RTL forms require their exact supported profile. A generated representation does not independently qualify device operation.

connections.text: The public parent workbench integrates these foundational surfaces while the focused component boundary is being developed.
Named models and topology generators provide identities and connectivity used to build populations and projections.
The dispatcher selects an admitted native profile or the Python path; population parameters, seeds, state and required observables must cross that boundary faithfully.

Network and equation representations feed selected compilation paths. The documented legacy LIF exporter emits neuron arrays without projections/topology, so it cannot stand for a complete compiled network.

external_roles.title: Model and integration reviewers
external_roles.text: Consumers must select compatible numerical/state/event profiles and verify their actual producer-consumer boundary, including reset and unsupported execution semantics.

external_roles.title: Reference and measurement owners
external_roles.text: External simulator references and physical device observations remain separately owned evidence; simulation traces alone do not establish biological or physical equivalence.

limits.title: Backend capability is conditional
limits.text: Current Rust admission accounts for Python-only dynamics and population construction/state divergences. Forced Rust refuses incompatible semantics; automatic selection uses the Python path when the Rust admission conditions fail.

limits.title: Native width differs from Python width
limits.text: The documented native FixedPointLif accepts signed int16 state with data_width 1–16 and a valid fractional range. A wider Python configuration does not establish native support.

limits.title: Network export has a restricted meaning
limits.text: The documented LIF exporter produces arrays and fixed-point parameters, omits connectivity, and retains its own coverage limitations. Read the separate compiler path for a different emission scope.

source_notes.title: MPI support table differs from current code
source_notes.text: The network page lists stimuli and plasticity as MPI-supported and contains conflicting per-rank dispatch descriptions. Current Network._run_mpi explicitly refuses embedded stimuli, state monitors, plasticity, spike gating and positive FIM feedback. Treat the table as a dated description and bind support to the actual entry path.

purpose.text: Organise neuron/model identities, source references, model descriptors and topology generators so researchers and integrators can select an exact model and see its available evidence and limitations.

scope.text: The component is a named extraction destination under construction. This explanation describes current source surfaces owned by the SC-NeuroCore workbench; independent packaging, migration, supported installed consumers and licensing require their own evidence.

inputs.title: Exact model identity
inputs.text: The source distinguishes literature models, project-original designs, retained SC compatibility identities and aliases. These identities do not all increment the source-model count.

inputs.title: Descriptor and provenance fields
inputs.text: Model descriptors carry parameter/state/backend/reproducibility information together with science and silicon tier declarations, validation metrics and integration methods.

inputs.title: Evidence-bound qualification
inputs.text: Verified query floors require receipts whose subjects still match the repository; a declared tier alone does not satisfy a higher verified floor.

outputs.title: Browsable identity and health inventory
outputs.text: Every registered model remains visible, including unreadable metadata. Available, unavailable and invalid states distinguish committed descriptors, inferred entries and faults.

outputs.title: Model-specific descriptors and evidence pointers
outputs.text: The shared descriptor surface supplies browse/detail information and explicit curation fields. Missing legacy schemas and malformed curated schemas have different handling.

outputs.title: Filtered and revision-bound model selection
outputs.text: The documented query result supplies matching identities, totals, facets and corpus revision. Identity, family, behaviour, metadata and verified-tier filters retain their stated scope.

outputs.title: Connectivity structures for experiments
outputs.text: Topology generators return CSR tuples for selected network structures. A synthetic graph generator is not an experimentally reconstructed biological connectome.

components.title: Identity classification
components.text: A common identity registry drives catalogue identity kind and source-count membership; import aliases do not become additional scientific models.

components.title: Typed descriptor boundary
components.text: Public class identifiers are admitted before filesystem access; invalid paths/identifiers and malformed numeric/provenance/digest metadata are refused.

components.title: Corpus-health and query surfaces
components.text: Faulted entries stay in the corpus, revision reflects identity/state changes, and server-side filtering preserves the verified-evidence distinction.

components.title: Model and topology catalogue
components.text: The model reference and network topology catalogue expose selectable definitions and connectivity structures under their original source and backend scope.

model_layers.title: Declared model definition
model_layers.text: Source locator, parameters, numerical integration, dynamic state, events and retained compatibility identity describe which model is selected.

model_layers.title: Reference and runtime evidence
model_layers.text: Model-specific reference traces, engine binding coverage and full acceleration-language completion are separate evidence surfaces.

model_layers.title: Hardware and physical evidence
model_layers.text: Software polyglot completion does not by itself establish RTL, formal, synthesis, timing, PPA, device or silicon completion. Those rungs need their own executed evidence.

connections.text: Registered names and topology CSR tuples are consumed by population and projection construction.
Backend dispositions separate same-name constructors, mapped constructors, Python-only names and network-runner profiles. Binding presence is not model parity.
The workbench Studio uses shared descriptors, health facets and server-side verified filters; model links select identity without changing run settings.
Reference, reproducibility and evidence-bound readiness checks retain exact model/profile scope rather than a catalogue-wide qualification claim.

external_roles.title: Scientific source and curation reviewers
external_roles.text: Reviewers must examine a selected model’s source, reduction/integration choices, parameters, state and event conventions; a class inventory or reference-trace feature check is not universal external simulator parity.

external_roles.title: Backend and consumer integrators
external_roles.text: Integrators retain exact constructor mappings, compatibility identities and configured contracts when moving saved experiments between backends.

limits.title: Inventory counts measure different cohorts
limits.text: Registered identities, scientific/source catalogue models, static source classes and optional engine wrappers are different populations. Avoid using any one as a universal model or fidelity total.

limits.title: Verified readiness must remain current
limits.text: Declared descriptor tiers and still-fresh evidence-backed tiers are distinct. A stale or absent receipt cannot be replaced by a catalogue label.

limits.title: Finite trace-hash variants are explicit
limits.text: The descriptor’s golden-trace variants form a finite measured allowlist with a retained numerical envelope; this is not an unrestricted approximate golden comparison.

source_notes.title: Published summary counts require reconciliation
source_notes.text: The model-reference title says 180 Python classes, its opening says 183, its registry coverage says 185 names, and its polyglot summary says 60 models. The identity-aware fidelity page separately reports 57 source models within a 160-model source catalogue. Preserve the original passages and request cohort/date reconciliation rather than inventing a single headline total.

purpose.text: Execute supported stochastic, neural and related numerical workloads through maintained native interfaces, selected SIMD kernels and distributed paths while preserving each admitted numerical, state and resource contract.

scope.text: The component is a named extraction destination under construction. This explanation describes current source surfaces owned by the SC-NeuroCore workbench; independent packaging, migration, supported installed consumers and licensing require their own evidence.

inputs.title: Supported workload and model profile
inputs.text: Packed bitstreams, model/current arrays, dense weights or network populations enter their own selected kernel and wrapper boundary. A common exported name does not establish complete configured model support.

inputs.title: Array and numerical layout
inputs.text: The packed NumPy path admits contiguous one-dimensional uint8 input and returns owning uint64 words; fixed-point native models retain their separate width, fraction and refractory conventions.

inputs.title: Installed runtime and resource profile
inputs.text: Python/NumPy versions, engine features, actual extension origin and available worker/device/storage resources define the installation being used.

outputs.title: Numerical results and model state
outputs.text: Selected kernels produce packed words, dense results or events/state through documented owning or caller-buffer contracts. Output publication and recoverable refusal remain specific to each binding.

outputs.title: Installed interface evidence
outputs.text: A retained inventory records both facade and compiled-module names, aliases, signatures, identities and code hashes. Equal metadata still needs separate behavioural and numerical checks.

outputs.title: Execution and performance evidence
outputs.text: The benchmark component retains workload/environment-specific results. SIMD/native presence or an API list does not supply a universal speedup or production throughput claim.

components.title: SIMD and packed arithmetic
components.text: The source exposes bitstream operations and platform-adaptive SIMD paths. The packed interface specifies ordering, tail bits, ownership and exact output-buffer sizing.

components.title: Explicit maintained wrappers
components.text: Stable consumers use narrow network/Studio/world-model/photonics/DNA/quantum wrappers rather than treating the top-level compatibility namespace as a universal export contract.

components.title: Native worker and storage admission
components.text: Selected nonempty workloads share a Rayon pool. Resource refusal preserves stated inputs/state and allows retry; successful explicit thread configuration remains fixed. Fallible dense APIs differ from Rust convenience methods that retain documented panic behaviour.

components.title: Conditional network and GPU paths
components.text: Network dispatch admits exact supported semantics. GPU exports require a GPU-feature wheel and actual hardware/profile qualification; the default wheel omits those names.

model_layers.title: API and installed code identity
model_layers.text: Origin guards and interface captures identify the loaded facade/extension and runtime profile. This metadata layer is distinct from executable behaviour.

model_layers.title: Numerical and state behaviour
model_layers.text: Shape/layout, mutation/refusal atomicity, model equations, seeded events, reset and supported serialization require their own per-binding/model evidence.

model_layers.title: Performance and physical deployment
model_layers.text: Native workload timings, optional GPU execution, distributed semantics and actual device/board measurements retain separate evidence boundaries.

connections.text: Population/network contracts determine whether acceleration is semantically admitted; unsupported parameters, seeds, moved state or required observables must not be replaced silently.
The catalogue records exact model identities, constructor dispositions and retained project profiles; the engine consumes those meanings without inflating source-model totals.
Measured workload and environment records supply performance context; native engine and Python/FFI paths have distinct measurement overheads.
Installed interface metadata, per-binding runtime contracts and model numerical/parity evidence supply separate verification layers.

external_roles.title: Installed consumer and platform operators
external_roles.text: Operators retain source/wheel/module provenance, Python/NumPy/feature profile, actual executable hardware and recoverable worker/storage behaviour for the selected deployment.

external_roles.title: Distributed and numerical reviewers
external_roles.text: Real multi-rank ordering/datatype semantics and model/profile parity need their own exercised evidence. Mocked MPI coverage or matching class names do not establish these results.

limits.title: A native constructor is not universal model fidelity
limits.text: The binding map explicitly includes Python-only models and expected divergence, while stochastic models without shared RNG stay outside exact spike-train parity.

limits.title: GPU random streams have their own oracle
limits.text: The documented GPU shader uses Philox inputs distinct from CPU encoder streams. Equal seeds across those implementations are not an exact-output parity oracle.

limits.title: Resource and platform evidence is scoped
limits.text: Installed interface baselines qualify their stated platform/profile only; resource-refusal observations and optional exports do not transfer automatically across operating systems or feature sets.

limits.title: Distributed support has documented gaps
limits.text: The captured network page records mocked MPI coverage and an open real multi-rank requirement. Current MPI entry code refuses selected unsupported dynamics; no distributed execution was performed for this map.

source_notes.title: Current dispatch is more specific than the old feature matrix
source_notes.text: Rust admission also checks population configuration, derived seeds and moved state through network_divergences. MPI currently refuses embedded stimuli, state monitors and plasticity despite the older page’s broader feature table.

purpose.text: Prepare and preserve the datasets, event/spike representations, encoder declarations, codec and recorder boundaries that make a neuromorphic experiment reproducible from its actual inputs.

scope.text: This component is being developed as a focused destination within the group. The selected implementation and interfaces described here are owned by the SC-NeuroCore parent workbench; separate installation, migration, release and commercial decisions need their own evidence.

inputs.title: Declared dataset population
inputs.text: Selected files, labels, sensor geometry, source time units and published split are recorded with provenance. Real archives and deliberately selected synthetic fixtures are different input populations.

inputs.title: Encoding and time geometry
inputs.text: Timestep, observation window, polarity rule, dimensions, random seed and first-spike latency settings determine the tensor consumed by a network.

inputs.title: Codec or recorder contract
inputs.text: Binary rasters, event streams and electrode waveforms have different representations. Selected codecs require their dimensions/state; the waveform interface validates a finite nonempty time-by-channel matrix.

outputs.title: File and sample manifest
outputs.text: The dataset manifest binds file size/SHA, samples, labels/groups/splits and publisher metadata. Verification reports missing, altered and unlisted files; the manifest digest identifies the exact declared input.

outputs.title: Group-preserving split plan
outputs.text: The split plan binds its originating manifest and keeps complete groups on one side. Separate checks expose user-plan leakage and groups shared by the publisher’s original splits.

outputs.title: Rebuildable encoded network input
outputs.text: Frozen encoder declarations and digests retain exact binning/late-event/polarity/seed/latency rules; unknown schemas or changed rules are refused rather than reconstructed approximately.

outputs.title: Recorded or compressed representations
outputs.text: Selected recorder rasters and codec bytes/results retain their specific read/shape/state contracts. A stored representation does not itself establish link timing, physical telemetry or empirical compression benefit.

components.title: Dataset readers and precision
components.text: N-MNIST event timestamps retain float64 before binning and reject incomplete records. Selected indexed SHD readers retain their event/label and native ownership boundary.

components.title: Manifest and split management
components.text: Record actual on-disk files before selecting a manifest-bound group split; preserve the source split and user-converted dataset conventions.

components.title: Declared encoders and selection
components.text: Explicit event binning, Bernoulli-rate and first-spike-latency declarations feed experiments; the separate encoding zoo exposes encoder/optimizer selection interfaces.

components.title: Codecs and recorders
components.text: The source distinguishes shared codec calls, state-synchronised predictive coding, independent streaming frames, AER representation, waveform input and binary recording.

model_layers.title: Original event or sample population
model_layers.text: Sensor geometry, source time units, labels and source file identity describe the original population, including empty recordings and selected synthetic fixtures.

model_layers.title: Encoded numerical experiment
model_layers.text: Binning, truncated time windows, polarity merging/separation, single-event Bernoulli sampling and latency placement determine the transformed model input.

model_layers.title: Storage and transport representation
model_layers.text: Codec and recorder outputs preserve a declared representation; data conversion, compression and physical event-link performance require their own roundtrip/loss/measurement scope.

connections.text: Manifest-bound splits and declared encoded inputs define the actual population used by training and evaluation.
Recorded spike trains and time conventions feed rate, interval and other measurements; a recorder’s raw timestep/rate conventions must stay explicit.
The group assigns container integrity/replay to SPIKE-LOG; dataset/encoder/codec meaning remains a separate producer boundary.
The named conversion tool owns roundtrip and loss evidence rather than treating any changed representation as the same source.
The named codec benchmark owns measured ratio, distortion and computational cost; codec API documentation alone does not supply those workload results.

external_roles.title: Dataset custodians and experiment owners
external_roles.text: Supply the actual corpus, labels/grouping, citation/licence metadata and user version/split/conversion declaration so a result can be traced to its inputs.

external_roles.title: Encoding and conversion reviewers
external_roles.text: Check exact transform/window/polarity/seed rules, source precision and representation roundtrip/loss against the selected consumer.

external_roles.title: Native I/O and transport operators
external_roles.text: Selected native readers require operator-owned libraries, supervised lifetime and qualified platform behaviour. Returned-byte limits are distinct from total transient memory and physical link measurements.

limits.title: Synthetic input is an explicit choice
limits.text: Current loader code and common contracts select synthetic generation only through the explicit flag; missing requested real data refuses. A test fixture is not the real corpus.

limits.title: Poisson naming does not change the draw
limits.text: The documented poisson_encode path is one Bernoulli event per timestep, so it cannot emit multiple same-step events as a genuine Poisson count could.

limits.title: Manifest grouping is only as fine as supplied identity
limits.text: SHD uses speaker groups; the event datasets identify recordings. Group checks do not invent an unavailable subject identity or a publisher train/test split for user-converted CIFAR data.

limits.title: Codec scope is not a physical claim
limits.text: Header/input constraints and compression interfaces are source contracts; advertised ratios, Bluetooth feasibility and real-time latency need separate measured workload/device evidence.

source_notes.title: Loader introduction uses older fallback wording
source_notes.text: The dataset page’s introduction says loaders can fall back when an archive is absent. Its common-contract section and current loader branches instead require explicit synthetic mode and refuse missing real files. Bind the experiment to the selected real/synthetic path.

purpose.text: Develop training, plasticity and adaptation paths that update selected model parameters or bounded local synaptic state, with reproducible data, objective, numerical and export contracts.

scope.text: This component is being developed as a focused destination within the group. The selected implementation and interfaces described here are owned by the SC-NeuroCore parent workbench; separate installation, migration, release and commercial decisions need their own evidence.

inputs.title: Declared data and held-out population
inputs.text: The experiment selects manifest-bound groups, encoding, network tensors and labels before fitting/evaluation. The data and split contract accompanies any reported result.

inputs.title: Model, objective and learning profile
inputs.text: Choose a surrogate-gradient/Torch model, separate equilibrium-propagation research path or explicit local plasticity rule. Forward dynamics, gradient approximation and update state are different contracts.

inputs.title: Device, precision and optional runtime
inputs.text: Supported installed Torch/device features, fixed-point field widths, reward/decay parameters and actual native owners determine the selected numerical path.

outputs.title: Fitted model and scoped evaluation
outputs.text: Training returns its documented loss/accuracy observations; evaluation uses eval mode and no gradient. Report the exact data, model, timestep and device profile rather than inferring external generalisation.

outputs.title: Bounded local state and update contract
outputs.text: The hardware-facing reward-STDP contract retains weight, pre/post and eligibility traces plus exact field widths/saturation; selected Python/native/RTL forms require their own correspondence.

outputs.title: SC export and design-selection records
outputs.text: Selected trained weights are normalised per layer for SC probabilities, with optional declared export noise. Joint stochastic-backprop reports retain relaxed objective/design choices and export metadata.

outputs.title: Programme outputs under construction
outputs.text: The group also assigns quantisation-aware training and distillation to this component. These are component objectives; the selected passages here do not establish their complete independent interfaces or delivered results.

components.title: Surrogate-gradient network training
components.text: Selected feedforward/convolutional SNN cells produce spikes/state/readout, while a smooth backward surrogate approximates the threshold derivative.

components.title: Temporal and local learning families
components.text: The source names BPTT/truncated BPTT, carried membrane state, eligibility traces and reward-modulated learning; the bounded fixed-point local rule is a distinct selected contract.

components.title: Training support and native ownership
components.text: Schedulers retain local deterministic state; optional callbacks refuse unavailable packages. Native owners support close/context cleanup and validated atomic restore.

components.title: SC design and delay optimisation
components.text: Joint optimisation exposes length/encoding/correlation design variables; DelayLinear separately trains weights and continuous delay, retains history and exposes quantised export values.

model_layers.title: Learning objective and model dynamics
model_layers.text: Selected network dynamics, loss, surrogate derivative or two-phase settle/nudge protocol determine the training method; sharing a package does not make these interchangeable.

model_layers.title: Local fixed-point adaptation
model_layers.text: A four-field per-synapse state and saturating reward-STDP numerical contract bound this local learner independently of sequence length.

model_layers.title: Exported and physical implementation
model_layers.text: SC weights, numerical/SC-NIR reports and executable HDL parity are handoff evidence. Resource estimates and simulated adaptation do not supply measured board learning, power or timing.

connections.text: Dataset manifests, split provenance and declared encoders preserve what training and evaluation actually consumed.
Neuron/synapse state and delayed event/current semantics are consumed by the selected update or network model; the learner’s profile must retain those meanings.
Numerical/SC-NIR annotations, normalised weights and selected RTL update blocks form explicit compilation handoffs rather than device deployment proof.
Readouts, losses and held-out observations supply inputs for selected quantitative evaluation; their interpretation retains the original population/objective scope.
The group assigns measured physical rule updates against fixed-point oracles to this separate instrument; simulated reward pairing is not that measurement.

external_roles.title: Learning and data evaluation reviewers
external_roles.text: Review model/objective, sequence/window/state-reset, group split, encoder and held-out evaluation choices as one reproducible experiment.

external_roles.title: Compiler and physical measurement owners
external_roles.text: Qualify exported numerical/HDL semantics, actual synthesis/timing/learning updates and physical target measurements before promoting the selected handoff to deployment evidence.

limits.title: Local O(1) state has a specific scope
limits.text: The bounded state proof concerns four fields per synapse independent of sequence length. It does not assert constant total network, dataset, reporting or training-history memory.

limits.title: Automatic device selection is conditional
limits.text: The selector checks the installed Torch build’s GPU capability; an explicit CUDA request bypasses it. Installed hardware/feature support needs the selected runtime profile.

limits.title: Weight normalisation changes representation
limits.text: Per-layer min-max normalised probabilities and finite-bitstream noise are selected export semantics. Their source description does not establish unchanged trained-model accuracy after hardware conversion.

limits.title: Research training and board evidence remain separate
limits.text: EP is documented as a research NumPy path; local adaptation/RTL handoff and stochastic-backprop parity exclude physical board measurement and timing/power qualification.

source_notes.title: Training overview is narrower than the package’s full method set
source_notes.text: The opening Torch/module description applies to its surrogate-gradient pipeline; the same page explicitly documents a separate NumPy equilibrium-propagation research surface. Report the selected method, optional dependencies and state contract.

purpose.text: Turn declared spike/event populations and recorded model outputs into quantitative statistics, temporal patterns, latent trajectories and bounded explanations whose units, assumptions and backend evidence remain visible.

scope.text: This component is being developed as a focused destination within the group. The selected implementation and interfaces described here are owned by the SC-NeuroCore parent workbench; separate installation, migration, release and commercial decisions need their own evidence.

inputs.title: Spike representation and time convention
inputs.text: Binary timestep trains, continuous spike times, trial populations, waveforms or field signals are different inputs. Each metric’s timestep/bin/window and units are declared.

inputs.title: Estimator and comparison design
inputs.text: Select metric, bins/lags/model order, surrogate null, trial/group population and any conditioning signals before interpreting a result.

inputs.title: Latent model and installed backend
inputs.text: GPFA receives binned population counts and explicit latent/bin/iteration settings; deterministic initialisation and the selected available backend define that estimator.

outputs.title: Statistics and temporal comparisons
outputs.text: Rate/interval/variability, spike-train distances, correlation and significance/pattern outputs report the selected observable rather than a universal neural-system score.

outputs.title: Latent trajectories and fitted GPFA parameters
outputs.text: The documented EM contract returns trajectories, loading matrix, offset, diagonal noise and likelihood history; fixed timescales and consistent kernel jitter are retained estimator choices.

outputs.title: Scoped directed-connectivity diagnostics
outputs.text: Selected Granger/VAR, PDC and DTF outputs retain their input validation, short-history and singular-frequency fallback conventions; the maintained dispatched path here is Python.

outputs.title: Bounded integrated-information estimate
outputs.text: Phi* compares Gaussian past/future mutual information against contiguous bipartitions and returns a nonnegative reducibility estimate in nats. It is not a consciousness verdict or complete IIT partition search.

components.title: Basic, rate and comparison metrics
components.text: Time-aware spike extraction/binning, rate/interval variability and distance/correlation functions cover different quantitative views of the selected recording.

components.title: Surrogate significance and pattern analysis
components.text: Null generators preserve or alter specified train structure; bootstrap/pattern procedures must be interpreted with the chosen null and sampling population.

components.title: Structured latent estimation
components.text: GPFA uses reproducible PCA signs/initial fields, Cholesky E/M steps and a structured marginal likelihood; the public compatibility seed no longer changes its deterministic initialisation.

components.title: Directed and information diagnostics
components.text: The selected Python causality reference and Phi* Gaussian reducibility estimator have explicitly bounded model/interpretation domains.

model_layers.title: Recorded observation
model_layers.text: Source events, binary trains and binned population counts retain their units, windows and provenance before any estimator changes the representation.

model_layers.title: Statistical or latent model
model_layers.text: Metric/null/VAR or regularised Gaussian-process assumptions determine the numerical output; estimator choice is not the identity of the underlying biological mechanism.

model_layers.title: Runtime correspondence and measurement
model_layers.text: Backend-specific exposure, numerical parity and benchmark workload need separate evidence. Floating-point GPFA agreement is explicitly not bit-exact.

connections.text: Dataset provenance, grouping, transform and recorder conventions identify the population and time basis analysed.
Readout and evaluation results are interpreted with their original objective and held-out dataset; analysis does not replace the split or training contract.
Selected Rust/PyO3 analysis surfaces and GPFA backends accelerate their supported estimators. Closure-based functions and causality dispatch retain explicit exposure limits.
Named workloads measure estimator performance on documented data/backend/environment; historical GPFA timings are not a universal speed ranking.
The component programme assigns visualisation/explanations and the workbench integrates these results; this role does not independently qualify their scientific meaning.

external_roles.title: Statistical and scientific reviewers
external_roles.text: Review input/time semantics, null choice, population/split, estimator assumptions and the actual reference evidence before drawing a domain conclusion.

external_roles.title: Backend and reproduction operators
external_roles.text: Retain selected installed/runtime profile, parity tolerance and exact benchmark workload. Missing optional backend tests or interface exposure require separate qualification.

limits.title: Floating-point agreement has a declared workload
limits.text: GPFA reports measured absolute differences and conditional tests for built backends. Missing-backend skips and tight roundoff agreement do not establish universal or bit-exact parity.

limits.title: Causality names do not establish every backend
limits.text: The source explicitly keeps generated safety-note surfaces outside dispatched causality execution and owns the maintained estimator with Python/NumPy.

limits.title: Native analysis exposure is not uniform
limits.text: Selected callback/closure-based functions remain Rust-only or need Python wrappers. A module list cannot establish that every metric has the same PyO3 contract.

limits.title: Phi* retains its bounded meaning
limits.text: Small-window/coarse-grained Gaussian reducibility and contiguous partition comparison are diagnostic scope, not intrinsic causal power, consciousness or full IIT minimisation.

source_notes.title: Overview counts and dependency claims are source summaries
source_notes.text: The analysis title says 124 functions while its opening says 127 and claims pure NumPy/zero external dependencies. The dedicated GPFA page explicitly uses SciPy/LAPACK for the Python Cholesky path. Preserve exact function/profile scope rather than importing the overview as a universal installation guarantee.

source_notes.title: Dedicated GPFA and general overview describe different solvers
source_notes.text: The general Rust-analysis overview describes Gauss-Jordan/Gaussian-elimination GPFA primitives; the dedicated GPFA page describes structured Cholesky throughout. Keep both source passages and request solver/version reconciliation for an exact runtime.

purpose.text: Connect selected network representations and execution environments while exposing which parameters, timing, state and graph semantics are preserved, assumed, approximated or refused.

scope.text: The component is a developing destination within the group. The selected interfaces and workflows described here belong to the current SC-NeuroCore workbench sources; independent packaging, installed consumer support, migration and release require their own evidence.

inputs.title: Versioned graph and source conventions
inputs.text: NIR graphs or files supply node/edge structure and parameters; the importer still needs explicit timestep and reset conventions matched to the source framework.

inputs.title: Bounded declarative network
inputs.text: The Torch bridge takes a supported population/projection network and a time-by-batch-by-input current tensor. An input-facing population must provide a deterministic entry.

inputs.title: Hardware lowering contract
inputs.text: Selected parser graphs become NeuronGraph records with explicit scales, delays, thresholds, widths and hierarchy provenance before compiler consumption.

outputs.title: Executable selected graph plus interchange notes
outputs.text: The importer returns a network together with assumed/approximated/not-carried notes and file NIR version when present. Unsupported node types are refused.

outputs.title: Compatible exchange representation
outputs.text: NIR export retains its own omission notes for timestep, subtract-reset, dynamic node state and pooling input shapes. NeuroML and SONATA are documented as import-only on this surface.

outputs.title: Differentiable graph and weight writeback
outputs.text: The selected Torch module produces output-population spike counts and can write learned projection values back into the existing CSR connections.

outputs.title: Selected RTL handoff
outputs.text: The lowering/compiler path emits top interconnect, per-type neuron modules and weight ROM representation. These are compiler artefacts requiring target-specific validation.

outputs.title: Other bridge-family programme scope
outputs.text: The group also assigns quantum, hyperdimensional and neuro-symbolic bridges here. The selected NIR/Torch passages do not establish all of those families’ complete interfaces or independent results.

components.title: Graph import and validation
components.text: Names, endpoints, graph containers and supported primitives are checked before lowering; import assumptions and approximation notes accompany the result.

components.title: Hierarchy and hardware-graph conversion
components.text: Selected nested structure, scale/delay/threshold and recurrent provenance cross an explicit converter boundary; malformed or ambiguous graphs refuse incomplete emission.

components.title: Differentiable network adapter
components.text: The Torch path keeps graph structure, previous-spike projection semantics and trainable existing-edge weights under a narrow model/state support boundary.

components.title: Export and consumer handoff
components.text: A compatible NIR representation, selected compiler artefacts or Torch weight writeback have different retained metadata and execution meanings.

model_layers.title: Source graph and declared model
model_layers.text: Graph structure and parameter identity do not alone specify executable timestep, reset, recurrent scheduling or dynamic state.

model_layers.title: Realised execution semantics
model_layers.text: A recurrent back edge realised with a unit delay and a nonintegral delay approximation are explicit model choices; selected multi-port and metadata losses remain visible.

model_layers.title: Training or hardware consumer
model_layers.text: A supported differentiable cell mapping or hardware graph needs its own exact numerical/consumer qualification. Import success is not device deployment.

connections.text: Network/population/projection and declared update conventions supply source semantics that the bridge must preserve or explicitly refuse.
Supported Torch projection parameters provide a selected differentiable path and controlled writeback, without changing the existing NumPy/Rust execution paths.
NeuronGraph is consumed by the FPGA compiler and SC-NIR conversion; a validated selected graph is the handoff boundary.
The group assigns independent versioned import/export conformance to this tool; the producing bridge’s own roundtrip checks are not that independent judgement.
Studio’s NIR compile response exposes interchange notes and NIR version so users can inspect the selected conversion.

external_roles.title: Source-framework and interoperability reviewers
external_roles.text: Supply the source model, framework timestep/reset conventions and reference observations, then evaluate both graph/parameter correspondence and realised dynamics.

external_roles.title: Training and target integrators
external_roles.text: Qualify supported cell/state mappings, existing-edge weight updates and selected hardware graph/RTL under the intended consumer contract.

limits.title: Primitive coverage is not complete execution equivalence
limits.text: A list of supported NIR primitives and parameter-roundtrip wording does not remove the importer’s documented assumptions, approximations and export omissions.

limits.title: Torch support is deliberately narrow
limits.text: The guide admits selected Lapicque and constrained StochasticLIF profiles and refuses embedded stimuli, plastic/delayed projections and unmappable models. Closed graphs require an input-facing population.

limits.title: Export does not serialize every live experiment
limits.text: Timestep, some reset/state/shape information and graph metadata have explicitly recorded carriage limits; preserve notes rather than treating the exchange file as full runtime state.

limits.title: No physical or quantum advantage follows
limits.text: Selected graph/RTL generation needs target validation, and naming additional quantum-related programme bridges supplies no measured device or computational-advantage result.

source_notes.title: Roundtrip wording has a narrower executable boundary
source_notes.text: The integration guide claims full parameter fidelity across listed nodes; the API separately records assumed timestep/reset/recurrent delay, selected approximations and export losses. Read the conversion notes with the coverage table rather than making a lossless whole-experiment claim.

purpose.text: Make selected numerical, runtime, formal and evidence claims inspectable against an exact model/profile, reference, execution and set of source subjects, while keeping their proof and measurement limits explicit.

scope.text: The component is a developing destination within the group. The selected interfaces and workflows described here belong to the current SC-NeuroCore workbench sources; independent packaging, installed consumer support, migration and release require their own evidence.

inputs.title: Selected model/profile and subjects
inputs.text: Descriptors, model/schema/compiler/validator source, committed RTL/reports and required native source/binary subjects define the facet being evaluated.

inputs.title: Reference and proof configuration
inputs.text: DUT/reference interfaces, reset, observed/coupled state, proof mode, depth, assumptions and actual toolchain define a formal question.

inputs.title: Numerical/state and timing contracts
inputs.text: Declared state layouts/lane packets and real event-response signals identify what crosses a runtime boundary or satisfies a cycle-level obligation.

outputs.title: Scoped numerical or state correspondence
outputs.text: State conformance identifies carried, dropped and unnameable fields. Correct trajectories, supported installation and numerical parity remain separately exercised evidence.

outputs.title: Formal result or counterexample
outputs.text: Selected runners return verdict, mode/depth/engine and counterexample information; setup failure or unavailable tools are distinct from a proven property.

outputs.title: Profile-bound executed evidence receipt
outputs.text: A creditable receipt identifies actually executed checks and source subjects, including native binaries when required, and retains the selected class/facet/profile scope.

outputs.title: Declared and verified readiness views
outputs.text: The ledger distinguishes not-declared/declared/unavailable/located/bound/stale/invalid. Verified tiers climb only through declared facets with current bound evidence.

outputs.title: Broader verification programme
outputs.text: The group also names fault injection and resilience here; selected formal/state/receipt source passages do not establish complete fault campaigns or a safety certification.

components.title: State and numerical boundary checks
components.text: Name each declared state variable a lane can carry before evaluating whether its values and event/reset behaviour agree with the intended reference.

components.title: Equivalence and property flows
components.text: A sequential miter compares DUT/reference outputs, while a single-module property checker evaluates its own stated obligations. These are distinct claim classes.

components.title: Proof instrumentation and mathematical assumptions
components.text: State taps and opt-in shared-product abstraction support selected invariants; Lean theorems and outstanding axioms retain their explicit model hypotheses.

components.title: Receipt and freshness verification
components.text: Executed testcase identities, required source subjects, post-run checks and exclusive append-only publication bind a receipt to its selected claim.

components.title: Timing and CDC property templates
components.text: Cycle-level start/end/deadline/liveness and selected synchronizer structure are reusable consumer-bound properties; missing proof runtimes are reported.

model_layers.title: Mathematical specification
model_layers.text: A proof establishes a statement under its declared definitions and assumptions. Monotone scalar hypotheses or axioms do not demonstrate an actual controlled plant’s safety.

model_layers.title: Numerical and RTL correspondence
model_layers.text: Sampled co-simulation, bounded-depth equivalence and invariant-based induction cover different input/state domains and must retain that exact scope.

model_layers.title: Executed evidence and physical measurement
model_layers.text: A fresh subject-bound receipt records a selected execution, while post-route timing, metastability behaviour and physical board evidence require their own observations.

connections.text: Declared descriptor claims and exact model/profile identities feed subject-bound readiness views; a location or label alone is not execution evidence.
DUT/reference RTL, emitted numerical contracts and source/compiler digests define the selected equivalence or co-simulation claim.
Lane packets and native source/binary subjects separate available interface carriage, supported installation and executed numerical agreement.
Studio can present selected readiness/numerical/proof evidence while retaining the distinction between declarations, current receipts and sampled correspondence.
Cycle-accurate properties do not establish nanosecond latency, power or physical board response; these require the separately scoped measurement instrument.
The named harness owns cross-runtime comparisons against declared numerical oracles, separate from mere state-field carriage.

external_roles.title: Independent model and hardware verification reviewers
external_roles.text: Examine the reference, shared implementation assumptions, selected numerical/profile domain, formal invariant/abstraction and exact input/reset coverage.

external_roles.title: Native and physical measurement owners
external_roles.text: Supply actual tool/runtime/binary provenance and consumer signals; qualify measured timing/CDC/device conditions separately from reusable formal templates.

limits.title: BMC depth and induction remain distinct
limits.text: A bounded proof covers its depth from reset. An unbounded result needs the appropriate invariant over every coupled state; UNKNOWN is inconclusive.

limits.title: Abstraction retains proof assumptions
limits.text: Shared free-product lifting is an opt-in over-approximation with a sound PASS argument in the described construction; FAIL can be spurious and does not automatically disprove the real design.

limits.title: A seal is not independent scientific identity
limits.text: SHA seals detect content changes but are not signatures, recorder authentication or independent review. A receipt covers selected inputs/domain rather than arbitrary dependencies or operating points.

limits.title: Safety obligations do not equal equivalence
limits.text: Bounded safety belongs to its own facet and cannot credit formal equivalence. Likewise state-field carriage does not establish numerical correctness or installed support.

limits.title: Formal timing is not physical timing
limits.text: Cycle obligations and structural CDC checks do not provide post-route nanoseconds or physical metastability resolution. Missing proof executables never count as a pass.

source_notes.title: Lean’s declared proof boundary includes axioms
source_notes.text: The source distinguishes pure-core theorem declarations from two axiomatised bounds pending a different proof surface. Keep these assumptions visible rather than describing every stated invariant as independently closed.

purpose.text: Provide a visual workbench for selected model design, simulation, analysis, training, compilation and evidence workflows, with results bound to the experiment and input context that produced them.

scope.text: The component is a developing destination within the group. The selected interfaces and workflows described here belong to the current SC-NeuroCore workbench sources; independent packaging, installed consumer support, migration and release require their own evidence.

inputs.title: Resolved experiment
inputs.text: Model/profile, timestep, protocol, parameters, initial state and randomness travel with the resolved experiment rather than being reconstructed from a display plot.

inputs.title: Current workspace and capability context
inputs.text: Selected model/ODE inputs, supported backend and currently available prerequisites determine which workflow step is ready, failed, unsupported or complete.

inputs.title: Numerical and artifact identity
inputs.text: Requested parameter/step/integrator/Q-format values and source/RTL digests define the selected compilation and evidence context.

outputs.title: Current experiment observations and history
outputs.text: Simulation/analysis payloads retain raw traces and snapshots when supplied, display projections and omission markers. Historical visible results do not certify the latest requested run.

outputs.title: Reviewed compiler and numerical handoff
outputs.text: Selected IR/RTL views expose structural checks, source/RTL traceability, representability and accepted/refused Q-formats; these are distinct from synthesis or board evidence.

outputs.title: Reproduction script or replay pack
outputs.text: The standalone script guards the resolved experiment digest; a replay pack also carries events/state expectations and reports exact or allowed-tolerance reproduction and admitted runtime drift.

outputs.title: Evidence bundle and chain report
outputs.text: Receipts bind payload scope/dependencies and distinguish producer-written from exporter-assembled evidence. Chain verification and completeness remain separate outcomes.

outputs.title: Recoverable workspace revisions
outputs.text: Saving appends a revision and stale saves refuse; prior immutable state, conflict handling and restoration remain part of workspace custody.

components.title: Guided current-input workflow
components.text: Design/simulate/analyse/train/compile/parity/synthesis/export stages derive status from current evidence. Skipped optional work and unavailable steps are labelled separately.

components.title: Asynchronous result and evidence custody
components.text: Jobs capture their source context; late results from a changed experiment cannot qualify the current one. Cart exports compare captured content identity, not item count.

components.title: Numeric contract and compiler inspector
components.text: The workbench inspects fixed-point encodings/LUT grids and refuses unsupported or unrepresentable requests while retaining the emitted source/RTL identity.

components.title: Replay and external pack inspection
components.text: Resolved scripts, replay expectations, canonical cross-runtime seals and off-Studio dependency/digest checks support a reviewable handoff.

components.title: Revision and writer control
components.text: A workspace states its expected revision, serializes writers under a bounded single-host lock and keeps immutable revisions/recovery history.

model_layers.title: Display and interaction context
model_layers.text: A plot or historical trace is an observation, not proof of current success. The selected experiment and latest attempt determine completion state.

model_layers.title: Numerical and compiler evidence
model_layers.text: A representable Q-format and sampled RTL-versus-bittrue trace have scoped meanings; they do not establish float-model equivalence, all stimuli, LUT error or physical timing.

model_layers.title: Exported experiment and evidence custody
model_layers.text: A reproduction identity, payload seal and resolved dependency chain support exact review. They do not authenticate a producer or establish scientific correctness on their own.

connections.text: Model identities and descriptor/evidence views inform selection; declared readiness and current verified facets remain distinct.
Optional training is a selected workflow stage. Skipping it does not create training evidence, and later outcomes remain bound to the submitted experiment.
NIR compile responses carry conversion notes/version so the user can inspect import assumptions and omitted information.
Source/RTL traceability and accepted numeric contracts cross an explicit compilation boundary before downstream synthesis or validation.
Readiness receipts, structural/formal checks and sampled co-simulation expose their selected model/input/proof scope rather than a blanket success badge.
Current analysis jobs and their source experiment are captured together; historical/late plots cannot silently redefine a newer experiment.

external_roles.title: Experiment and integration reviewers
external_roles.text: Inspect the resolved model/profile/state/drive contract, conversion notes, exact selected numerical comparison and raw-data omissions before consuming an exported result.

external_roles.title: Workspace and deployment operators
external_roles.text: Use the declared single-host workspace root/locking boundary, preserve revisions/restore state, and qualify actual external compiler/board prerequisites.

external_roles.title: Independent evidence recipients
external_roles.text: Recompute exported file/payload/dependency checks and distinguish producer binding, exporter receipt, internal consistency, completeness and scientific interpretation.

limits.title: Development preview remains the stated maturity
limits.text: Selected workflows are available for evaluation while API/UI and production hardening continue; a visual workflow is not a stable release or physical deployment guarantee.

limits.title: Representability has a bounded meaning
limits.text: The numeric contract does not establish reached-state range, LUT approximation error, timing closure, place/route or board behaviour.

limits.title: Co-simulation is a selected stimulus comparison
limits.text: Catalogue RTL-versus-bittrue comparison excludes the float model, model-specific exact-threshold stimuli and untested schedules; supported integrators and RNG/substep paths remain limited.

limits.title: Workspace locks have a deployment boundary
limits.text: The documented exclusion applies to writers sharing appropriate single-host filesystem locking. It does not promise two-host consistency over a network share.

limits.title: Export integrity is not producer authentication
limits.text: A producer-written receipt and an exporter-assembled one attest different things; internal seals do not sign identity or validate the underlying scientific result.

source_notes.title: Keep the two co-simulation comparisons separate
source_notes.text: The Inspector page labels its IR endpoint float-versus-Q8.8; the catalogue numeric-contract page defines RTL-versus-bittrue with no floating model. State the route/model/profile instead of merging these into one equivalence claim.

purpose.text: Provide generic problem foundations, configuration, logging and resource-budget boundaries so oscillator and quantum workflows can share explicit numerical inputs without importing paper-specific assumptions.

scope.text: This component is in progress within the group’s separation programme. The selected executable interfaces are documented in the SCPN-QUANTUM-CONTROL workbench; a focused name, reserved directory or roadmap boundary does not establish an independently qualified component release.

inputs.title: Coupling and natural frequencies
inputs.text: The typed Kuramoto facade accepts a nonempty square symmetric real coupling matrix and a matching frequency vector. It rejects nonfinite values and implicit string, boolean, object or complex coercion.

inputs.title: Domain mapping and provenance
inputs.text: A domain consumer supplies its own mapping from source data to coupling/frequency arrays and JSON-serialisable metadata. Naming EEG, plasma or a grid does not supply that scientific model.

inputs.title: Declared experiment and resource request
inputs.text: A problem/backend/objective, seed, shot policy and metadata describe an experiment; compile or dense requests additionally specify dimensions, ranks, object counts and an active memory cap.

outputs.title: Copied immutable problem
outputs.text: Validated input arrays are copied and made read-only, with the coupling diagonal zeroed. Later caller mutation cannot silently replace the retained problem.

outputs.title: Hamiltonian and evolution handoff
outputs.text: The live facade constructs sparse Pauli or dense Hamiltonians and Trotter circuits, and exposes analog/hybrid programme and selected trajectory entry points.

outputs.title: Structured resource decision
outputs.text: Budget checks return explicit requirements and allowed/refused outcomes; enforcement raises a typed error for an over-budget request.

outputs.title: Declared contract and backend view
outputs.text: Stable Problem, Backend, Experiment and Result records and capability profiles describe an integration boundary. Their construction does not execute a simulator or hardware job.

components.title: Generic problem validation
components.text: Shape, symmetry, numeric domain, finiteness and provenance are checked before the typed facade accepts a KuramotoProblem.

components.title: Contract-to-facade adapters
components.text: Problem adapters connect the smaller stable contract layer to the live Hamiltonian/circuit/trajectory facade without making the contract itself a compiler.

components.title: Budget admission
components.text: Compile-Pauli and dense-Hilbert estimators compose low-level guards; sparse fallback and full-basis construction also have declared allocation boundaries.

components.title: Configuration and integration foundations
components.text: Configuration and logging belong to this component’s assigned responsibility; the selected passages detail problem and budget interfaces rather than a complete standalone configuration API.

model_layers.title: Source-domain model
model_layers.text: The consumer owns source meaning, units and the conversion into coupling and frequency arrays; generic XY compilation does not validate the source-domain hypothesis.

model_layers.title: Validated mathematical representation
model_layers.text: The typed problem has symmetric coupling and explicit numerical data. Hamiltonian, circuit and trajectory objects are different downstream representations.

model_layers.title: Execution and observed evidence
model_layers.text: Capability declarations and admitted allocations precede an actual backend run, provenance, observables and any independent review.

connections.text: Shared parameter/result/evidence contracts describe component interchange; CORE supplies generic problem foundations and budget admission.
Validated problems feed Hamiltonian and circuit construction; model/circuit frontends and code generation retain the compiler’s assigned ownership.
Simulation consumes the selected mathematical representation and numerical budget, then produces route-specific states, trajectories or observables.
Differentiation needs explicit parameter identity, objective and supported route; sharing a problem object does not make every simulator differentiable.
The integrated workbench hosts these selected interfaces while focused components are developed and independently qualified.

external_roles.title: Domain-model and numerical integrators
external_roles.text: Proposed contribution: supply traceable source-to-array mappings and reference cases, including an explicit treatment of directed coupling before a symmetric XY problem is constructed.

external_roles.title: Consumer and resource reviewers
external_roles.text: Proposed contribution: verify the selected contract/adapter, allocation model and actual target behaviour; a within-budget estimate is not a host-capacity guarantee.

limits.title: Contract records do not compute results
limits.text: The stable core does not by itself run circuits, solve Lindblad dynamics, optimise control or submit hardware jobs.

limits.title: Symmetry belongs to the named entry point
