limits.text: The typed facade refuses asymmetric coupling. A consumer with directed interactions needs an explicit modelling decision before passing that facade.

limits.title: Memory estimates have a bounded meaning
limits.text: Declared compile/dense estimates and caps do not establish production immunity to memory exhaustion or available host RAM.

limits.title: Package and licensing decisions remain separate
limits.text: The facade source describes an in-repository boundary and a possible later lightweight package; its own AGPL/commercial distribution boundary remains explicit.

source_notes.title: Compiler summary and typed validation describe different boundaries
source_notes.text: The architecture summary mentions symmetrisation inside a compiler, while the facade documents rejection of asymmetric input before compilation. This guide scopes its input promise to the typed facade; directed-model semantics must not be inferred from the summary alone.

purpose.text: Make optimisation objectives trainable and inspectable through declared derivative methods, transforms, batching and supported-path contracts, with evidence that distinguishes analytic, numerical, stochastic and unsupported routes.

scope.text: This component is in progress within the group’s separation programme. The selected executable interfaces are documented in the SCPN-QUANTUM-CONTROL workbench; a focused name, reserved directory or roadmap boundary does not establish an independently qualified component release.

inputs.title: Objective and parameter identity
inputs.text: A selected objective, parameters, trainability and requested derivative method define the computation; method dispatch rejects unknown names rather than guessing.

inputs.title: Supported operation and route
inputs.text: Gate, observable, backend, transform, adapter, shape and effect contracts must match a supported route. Registry metadata and a planner decision have narrower meanings than numerical execution.

inputs.title: Source and captured-state context
inputs.text: Whole-program numerical admission checks source correspondence, callable bindings, captured coefficients and effects before running the objective.

inputs.title: Estimator and resource policy
inputs.text: Finite-shot requests need sample/variance provenance; whole-program adjoint access carries memory, deadline and cancellation controls.

outputs.title: Value and declared derivative
outputs.text: Supported routes return a value/gradient or requested transform with an explicit method; finite-difference artefacts retain diagnostic-only classification.

outputs.title: Support or refusal diagnostic
outputs.text: Unsupported gates, observables, transforms, effects and hardware requests stay visible instead of silently becoming a different derivative algorithm.

outputs.title: Bound runtime and adjoint content
outputs.text: A whole-program runtime result retains its primal, gradient, parameter identity, captured nodes, effect IR and adjoint correspondence; changed retained content can invalidate access.

outputs.title: Inspectable dry-run journey
outputs.text: The product catalogue returns acknowledged steps or blockers for frontend/IR/adjoint journeys. This decision is a plan and does not execute those steps.

outputs.title: Bounded verification and training evidence
outputs.text: Selected tutorials pair registered-gate derivatives, confidence envelopes, small QNN training and numerical checks with explicit local/nonisolated evidence limits.

components.title: Canonical transform namespace
components.text: scpn_quantum_control.diff and scpn.diff expose gradient/Jacobian/Hessian, JVP/VJP, batching and JIT explanation entry points with supported-route diagnostics.

components.title: Derivative method selection
components.text: Parameter-shift, finite differences, complex step, forward mode, reverse mode and whole-program tracing answer different questions; choose and retain the declared method.

components.title: Program frontend and effect admission
components.text: Source-visible helper/capture checks precede execution; external callbacks, ambient randomness and captured mutation have explicit refusal boundaries.

components.title: Runtime correspondence and adjoint controls
components.text: Result/IR/tape correspondence and captured-state inspection share active resource and cancellation limits before derivative access or replay.

components.title: Evidence and product journey layer
components.text: Registry/planner rows describe support metadata, while the experimental product map organises dry-run steps; neither alone certifies native compilation or a device.

model_layers.title: Declared objective and derivative
model_layers.text: Fix the mathematical objective, parameter order, primitive contracts and analytic/numerical/stochastic method before comparing gradients.

model_layers.title: Executed local route
model_layers.text: A supported trace or registered quantum gradient can be checked against a declared reference. A functional tutorial or host bridge does not establish arbitrary native-framework autodiff.

model_layers.title: Retained result and independent qualification
model_layers.text: Live captured-state correspondence is distinct from persistent-record authentication; independent comparison, hardware policy and performance evidence need their own artefacts.

connections.text: Validated problems, parameter identity and resource admission support a selected differentiable objective without making all core/facade operations differentiable.
Quantum tapes, selected gradient execution and framework bridges belong to QNODE; AD supplies transforms and supported derivative contracts across those boundaries.
The frontend/IR/adjoint journey and registered-primitive compiler reports expose a compiler boundary; an allowed dry-run is not completed lowering.
Selected oscillator and local quantum objectives can supply derivatives; simulator choice, estimator policy and each supported kernel still require explicit qualification.
The group assigns independent software-derivative comparison against analytic, shifted and numerical references to this developing tool; producer diagnostics are not its completed verdict.

external_roles.title: Derivative and framework reviewers
external_roles.text: Proposed contribution: compare exact primitive/backend/shape/transform cases against an independent declared reference, retaining stochastic variance and sample identities.

external_roles.title: Compiler and consumer integrators
external_roles.text: Proposed contribution: qualify source/effect admission, actual lowering/replay and captured-state handling separately from a catalogue or support-plan result.

limits.title: No universal Python or transform promise
limits.text: Arbitrary Python/NumPy AD, every compiler/JIT path, arbitrary neural architectures and unsupported transform nesting remain outside the documented bounded support.

limits.title: Numerical checking is its own evidence class
limits.text: Finite differences can verify a selected derivative but do not become analytic, whole-program, native-framework or hardware-gradient evidence.

limits.title: Live binding is not persistent authentication
limits.text: In-memory source/capture correspondence observes current state, does not lock caller storage or detect fully reverted mutations, and is omitted from historical serialisation.

limits.title: Resource accounting is component scoped
limits.text: Declared buffers, capture inspection and adjoint storage share the active allowance; general allocator overhead and undeclared third-party allocations remain outside that accounting.

limits.title: No provider or performance promotion from a plan
limits.text: Supported registry/planner metadata, tutorial integration and dry-run decisions do not establish live hardware gradients, universal transforms or production benchmark performance.

source_notes.title: Whole-program dry-run is different from the numerical runtime
source_notes.text: The product journey acknowledges declared steps without executing an objective, compiling or replaying an adjoint. Numerical runtime documentation separately specifies effect admission and live result/capture correspondence.

purpose.text: Develop classical and quantum oscillator simulation, XY/Kuramoto solvers, open-system and tensor-network paths and co-simulation. The selected parent sources detail quantum evolution and approximation boundaries rather than qualifying every family named in that programme.

scope.text: This component is in progress within the group’s separation programme. The selected executable interfaces are documented in the SCPN-QUANTUM-CONTROL workbench; a focused name, reserved directory or roadmap boundary does not establish an independently qualified component release.

inputs.title: Model, preparation and evolution request
inputs.text: A validated coupling/frequency problem or Hamiltonian, an initial state and a time grid define the selected evolution. Explicit preparation matters when comparing routes.

inputs.title: Numerical and approximation policy
inputs.text: Tensor runs declare bond cap, SVD cutoff, timestep/order, sweep limit, long-range truncation policy and memory ceiling.

inputs.title: Open-system and ensemble assumptions
inputs.text: The selected open-system paths describe density dynamics, jump trajectories, seeded ensembles and simulation-only noise-rate interchange; uncertainty must retain its ensemble/seed meaning.

outputs.title: State, trajectory and observable handoff
outputs.text: Selected evolution paths produce circuits, statevectors, trajectories and route-specific observables for analysis and later evidence retention.

outputs.title: Variational ground-state result
outputs.text: DMRG returns energy, an MPS, energy-convergence status, actual bonds and diagnostics. Energy convergence does not guarantee global ground-state fidelity.

outputs.title: Compressed time-evolution result
outputs.text: TEBD returns requested times, R values, final MPS/bonds and diagnostics, including local losses and actual observations.

outputs.title: Seeded open-system evidence
outputs.text: The open-system product describes trajectory and ensemble mean/std surfaces, reproducibility certificates and simulation-noise I/O, with broader evidence breadth still residual.

outputs.title: Explicit approximation record
outputs.text: Tensor diagnostics retain runtime version, cutoff, timestep/order, contraction strategy, actual bonds/bytes, norm and local Pauli-Z observations; omitted coupling remains visible.

components.title: Gate-model and variational evolution
components.text: The workbench documents Lie/Suzuki Trotter and variational lanes. Its ADAPT-VQE label denotes layered VQE, and AVQDS denotes fixed-ansatz McLachlan evolution without operator-pool growth.

components.title: Open-system density and jump routes
components.text: Lindblad density and seeded MCWF paths provide different numerical representations. A tensor_jump module name does not make its exponential statevector storage an MPS algorithm.

components.title: MPS ground state and dynamics
components.text: Optional quimb-backed DMRG/TEBD operate on nearest-neighbour spin-half models with explicit preparation, truncation and memory admission.

components.title: Contraction and approximation inspection
components.text: The tensor family also includes cotengra contraction planning; actual storage, observations and local discarded-weight diagnostics remain part of the selected run.

components.title: Classical and native sibling integration
components.text: Classical oscillator tools and optional Rust/PyO3 acceleration are separate sibling packages in the parent workbench. They are not automatically absorbed into SIM or AD.

model_layers.title: Mathematical dynamics and preparation
model_layers.text: Specify classical/quantum model, operator normalisation, initial state and open-system assumptions before interpreting an evolution result.

model_layers.title: Numerical solver and approximation
model_layers.text: Trotter order, variational ansatz, nearest-neighbour truncation and finite bond cap alter the represented computation and need separate diagnostics.

model_layers.title: Observed convergence and uncertainty
model_layers.text: Energy convergence, local SVD losses, a Trotter estimate and seeded ensemble spread answer different questions; none alone is a global fidelity or hardware-noise bound.

model_layers.title: Scientific or engineering interpretation
model_layers.text: Cross-method parity needs the same Hamiltonian and preparation. State compression or a large qubit label does not establish accuracy, speed, physical calibration or quantum advantage.

connections.text: Problem/facade and allocation boundaries supply selected Hamiltonians, preparation handoffs and resource admission before a simulator is run.
Only explicitly supported simulator objectives and derivative methods cross the AD boundary; Lindblad adjoints are a named gap in the selected open-system product.
Simulation produces route-specific states and observables for the group’s analysis/evidence pipeline; the downstream claim must retain the actual numerical model and approximation record.
Bounded small-system references, bond refinement and timestep refinement provide comparison inputs. A tensor-network baseline design is not a measured large-system benchmark.
The workbench integrates these numerical paths and optional sibling packages while component separation and supported public consumer interfaces develop.

external_roles.title: Numerical and tensor-network reviewers
external_roles.text: Proposed contribution: match Hamiltonian coefficients and initial preparation, inspect coupling truncation, refine timestep/bond caps and compare bounded references with retained diagnostics.

external_roles.title: Noise-model and experiment contributors
external_roles.text: Proposed contribution: provide declared noise assumptions and seeded/reference observations, then qualify model fidelity separately from simulation reproducibility.

limits.title: Same arrays can represent different Hamiltonians
limits.text: The MPS spin-half convention uses Pauli coefficients K/4 and omega/2. Matching a Pauli-normalised XY route also requires explicit initial-state preparation; rescaling omega alone changes its default preparation.

limits.title: Long-range coupling is not silently complete
limits.text: Direct DMRG/TEBD rejects longer-range terms unless explicit truncation is enabled; truncated runs expose omitted-coupling magnitude and their nearest-neighbour scope.

limits.title: Local losses are not a global error certificate
limits.text: Summed discarded singular-value losses and the separate Trotter estimate do not establish a global state, observable or fidelity error bound.

limits.title: Compression still needs admitted storage
limits.text: Entanglement can exceed the retained bond cap. Declared tensor/SVD/input/observation accounting is not a total-RSS guarantee; dense export needs explicit separate admission.

limits.title: Open-system and resource-estimator gaps remain explicit
limits.text: The selected product refuses unsupported non-CP/non-Markovian, adjoint-Lindblad and hardware-noise claims; QSVT is described as a resource estimator with phase synthesis refused.

source_notes.title: Cross-solver equality requires a matched estimand
source_notes.text: The detailed tensor guide specifies spin versus Pauli normalisation and preparation dependence. Use those conventions when reading the architecture’s broad XY-family label.

source_notes.title: Large-size plans and qualitative tables are not run results
source_notes.text: The tensor guide explicitly identifies N=30–40 baseline work as a CPU-first design, and says compressed states need actual accuracy/storage/cost qualification. This guide makes no measured large-system performance claim.

purpose.text: Coordinate the chamber-side kinematic, pulse-admission and trigger-software workflow for magneto-inertial field-reversed-configuration research. MIF connects a declared merge scenario to inspectable fire/hold/abort decisions, separately owned controller/physics services and explicit software/RTL evidence.

scope.text: This explanation follows inspected source and its documented software demonstration. MIF owns kinematic merging, pulse/lifecycle and trigger/evidence responsibilities; FUSION owns the plasma physics. A model decision, a software actuator call, local RTL cosimulation and physical timing/plant acceptance retain different meanings. No demonstration, proof, backend, model or hardware was executed for this map update.

inputs.title: Typed merge scenario
inputs.text: Initial phases in radians, axial positions in metres, velocities in metres per second, integration step/time horizon, phase/spatial lock tolerances and the sampled safety envelope accompany the bank specification, initial voltage and requested compression pulse.

inputs.title: Prescribed physics channels and optional recovery
inputs.text: Recovery requires both its coil/load specification and an expansion trajectory: time, radius, radial velocity, magnetic field and field rate. The simple MIF decision consumes those supplied channels; it does not evolve the self-consistent compression physics itself.

inputs.title: Diagnostic events with explicit origin
inputs.text: The inspected full-chain diagnostic generates a deterministic ADC-reference stream, preserves address/polarity/clock/sequence meaning and projects admitted events into a separately bound CONTROL exact-current path. Its calibration statement is a normalised simulation profile, not a calibrated facility measurement.

inputs.title: Actual sibling and RTL tool bindings
inputs.text: The full-chain entry point selects actual MIF/CONTROL/FUSION/NeuroCore source checkouts, requires the selected Rust stochastic backend and builds the tracked trigger fabric with Verilator. Source availability and installed dependency/tool compatibility must be checked in the actual run.

outputs.title: Merge-trigger report and intermediate traces
outputs.text: The simple entry point returns fire, abort unsafe, hold no lock or abort bank infeasible, plus reasons, lock time, kinematic/merge traces, a sampled safety certificate, bank feasibility/energy and optional prescribed-trajectory recovery. These are model outputs, not a physical trigger or measured energy recovery.

outputs.title: Causal nominal and veto case records
outputs.text: When run successfully, the full-chain demonstration records MIF decisions, the CONTROL permit and scheduler, diagnostic event provenance and actual local RTL cycles. It requires exactly one nominal RTL pulse before calling the FUSION model; the injected unsafe case must suppress the pulse and avoid that model call.

outputs.title: FUSION trajectory and recovery accounting
outputs.text: The admitted model call produces radius, radial velocity, magnetic-field and time channels. The field-rate channel is explicitly derived with numpy.gradient, then used for Faraday recovery; the runtime checks flux-budget diagnostics. This remains a source-described software-model output with its own physics evidence requirements.

outputs.title: Separate exact-current diagnostic record
outputs.text: A stateful diagnostic result carries canonical event/address-map/projection/control-execution identities and ingress telemetry. Its actuation_authority field is false; it does not replace the stateless permit, scheduler or independent veto.

outputs.title: Digest-bound replay and timing evidence
outputs.text: The documented bundle contains nominal.json, safety_veto.json, fusion_trajectory.npz, summary.md and chain_manifest.json. The runtime reruns both cases and compares canonical payloads and trajectory channels before writing provenance/artifact digests. A separate timing package keeps cycle proofs, post-route reports and calibrated end-to-end measurements in distinct classes.

components.title: Kinematic approach and sustained merge window
components.text: Moving-frame phase/axial evolution supplies a trajectory to a phase-and-spatial lock monitor. The selected consecutive-sample requirement is part of the scenario; kinematic phase coupling is a control-lane model rather than an automatically validated plasma solution.

components.title: Sampled safety, bank feasibility and pulse lifecycle
components.text: The decision checks the sampled envelope and bank feasibility, while separately described lifecycle/scheduler surfaces control pulse-state progression. A mathematical envelope certificate or transition check does not certify the physical facility.

components.title: Observation/event representation
components.text: Diagnostic normalisation, ADC-reference generation, AER buffering/address mapping and source-clock/sequence handling retain their own representations. The selected exact-current branch records a normalised simulation calibration and fails before CONTROL execution on event loss.

components.title: Permit, RTL fabric and dominant veto
components.text: The full-chain software composes the stateless CONTROL permit and scheduler with a deterministic sensor-reference stimulus. Verilator executes the trigger fabric and its cycles are compared with the reference. Only the explicit combination of a MIF fire outcome, CONTROL admission and exactly one observed RTL trigger allows the FUSION model call.

components.title: Replay, provenance and consumer-facing boundaries
components.text: Case payloads retain the selected execution modes and non-actuating diagnostic branch. Replay and exact source/artifact bindings support review; source symbol readiness, numerical/physical evidence and timing measurements remain separately owned qualifications.

implementation.title: One scenario produces a decision and its intermediate evidence
implementation.text: evaluate_merge_trigger composes moving-frame evolution, merge-window evaluation, sampled safety, bank feasibility and optional prescribed-expansion recovery. Its decision precedence is safety first, then lock, then bank feasibility. Recovery is calculated from supplied channels before the final decision, so an estimate is not evidence that a pulse physically occurred.

implementation.title: A stateless transition gate supplies the stochastic permit
implementation.text: The full-chain CONTROL path compiles a Petri net for lock, kinematic safety and bank feasibility, compares floating and stochastic dense permits using the required SC-NeuroCore Rust backend, and checks bounded explicit-state marking/reachability results. The lif_fire API name here denotes a reset-before-one-evaluation threshold permit; no membrane state is preserved by this path.

implementation.title: A distinct stateful diagnostic preserves a different model contract
implementation.text: evaluate_exact_current_aer_diagnostic builds clocked ADC-reference events and address mapping, checks buffer admission, constructs a source-bound stream/projection and invokes the installed CONTROL exact-current bridge. Its recorded execution mode is stateful_exact_current_diagnostic and actuation_authority is false. The event source is simulated and the selected calibration is explicitly normalised.

implementation.title: The scheduler and actual RTL simulation gate the next model call
implementation.text: The full-chain case drives the CONTROL pulsed scheduler, produces trigger-fabric stimulus, runs the built Verilator binary and requires bit-true reference agreement. The nominal case requires one unanimous fire admission; the unsafe injection must abort, veto every RTL cycle, produce no pulse and avoid the FUSION call. The stateful diagnostic is recorded separately from those admission inputs.

implementation.title: FUSION retains the compression physics
implementation.text: After admission, the runtime invokes FUSION equilibrium and supplied-current pulsed-compression APIs, checks trajectory flux budgets and passes the resulting fields to MIF Faraday accounting. Its reported field rate is a finite-difference derivative of the FUSION field samples. The simple merge-trigger entry point instead accepts a prescribed expansion; these are distinct invocation paths.

implementation.title: Actual runs must pass replay before emitting their bundle
implementation.text: run_full_chain_demo verifies selected package source origins, builds the tracked fabric, runs nominal/veto cases twice, compares canonical JSON and each trajectory channel, then emits the documented bundle and digests. Source-described simulation/cosimulation labels do not become fresh execution evidence when this atlas reads the code.

model_layers.title: Kinematic state versus plasma-physics evolution
model_layers.text: Phase/position trajectories, lock windows and sampled separation envelopes model the approach and decision problem. Equilibrium, Hall-MHD, instability and self-consistent compression remain FUSION-owned. The MIF trajectory and report do not by themselves constitute a three-dimensional plasma or complete reactor simulation.

model_layers.title: A decision and a model actuator are separate steps
model_layers.text: The simple merge-trigger report has safety/lock/bank precedence. The full-chain demonstration additionally requires CONTROL and local RTL admission before invoking a software FUSION actuator. Neither a fire label nor an actuator_invoked field establishes a physical coil command or machine-protection approval.

model_layers.title: Stateless permit versus temporal exact-current diagnostic
model_layers.text: The transition permit resets before a threshold evaluation and carries no membrane history. The separate event-to-exact-current diagnostic preserves its selected temporal model but has no actuation authority. They coexist in the case record and must not be substituted for one another or reported as the same neuron experiment.

model_layers.title: Numerical, RTL-cycle and physical timing evidence
model_layers.text: Software-model trajectories, local bit-true Verilator results, formal clock-cycle relations, named-device post-route timing and calibrated sensor-to-driver measurements concern different claims. The sub-50-nanosecond figure is an engineering target: the documented timing package explicitly prohibits promoting its cycle proof into a wall-clock claim.

connections.text: Owns the FRC/plasma physics. MIF inspects public contract/readiness surfaces, consumes prescribed physics channels in its simple decision and invokes a supplied-current compression model in the separately bound full-chain demonstration. Symbol availability and full physics evidence remain distinct.

Supplies the full-chain Petri/stochastic permit and pulse scheduler, plus the separately bound exact-current diagnostic bridge. Those actual source APIs have different execution modes and admission responsibilities; no current installed compatibility is inferred from this diagram.

The proposed scientific scope includes PHWR's own coupled spatial/thermal/network solver, source-supported fuel history and refuelling, separate field/history prediction, and geometry/material inspection for 3D/CAD and teaching. [Architecture detail](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) distinguishes these future components and their data/evidence boundaries. None is implemented by the current scaffold.

Reusable mathematical primitives belong to SCPN-REACTOR-KERNELS; PHWR owns its source-specific model and solver/prediction choices. Registry semantics belong to SCPN-PHASE-ORCHESTRATOR. Studio/workbench interfaces, supervisory control and final machine-protection veto retain their external owners.

The current implementation validates repository source and metadata. [project-boundary.json](../project-boundary.json) is a checked PHWR identity, not an active reactor-domain capability or SPO registry record. Its validator refuses any capability, claim, runtime dependency, active configuration or registration at this stage. All scientific components and interfaces described here are proposed and unimplemented.

## Scientific profiles

The source-faithful benchmark profile retains an exact case edition, geometry, material/library state, boundary conditions and source assumptions. Its reference quantities and numerical support belong to that case.

The full fuel-history/refuelling profile additionally needs its own complete nuclear chain, reaction and decay data, composition-dependent properties, energy accounting and source-supported event dynamics. Benchmark reproduction cannot qualify those additional subjects.

Separate prediction profiles would forecast named channel/bundle fields or per-bundle inventory and burnup at requested future times. Each forecast remains conditional on an exact adopted model, current physical state and declared future boundary/history schedule. Scenario outputs retain every submitted scenario identity; their spread does not establish a calibrated probability or confidence interval.

## Proposed component boundaries

| PHWR-owned component | Input meaning | Intended output meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Source and profile contract | Original edition, rights, quantities, material/library and supported physical domain | An explicit source/model profile with consistent units, coordinates and support |
| Geometry and material state | Pressure-tube/channel geometry, physical bundle occurrences, computational cells and material instances | A source-supported 3D geometry and occurrence map with explicit volumes and physical identities |
| Own coupled solver | Spatial neutron/poison state, solid temperatures, coolant network and boundary history | Coupled fields and observations for the exact supported model |
| Own fuel-history evolution | Per-bundle nuclide inventory, irradiation lineage, energy history and scheduled refuelling | Evolved inventory and committed incoming, retained and discharged bundle states |
| Separate own predictor | Adopted physical state/profile, target, horizon and future schedule | Model-conditional field or inventory/burnup forecasts with their own evidence |
| Result and inspection contract | Source/profile identities, actual state, geometry and quantity mappings | Evidence-bearing observations and qualified 3D/CAD, workbench and teaching inputs |

Physical bundles, computational cells and thermal groups are separate identity spaces. Refining a mesh cannot duplicate a bundle's atom inventory. A field projection must retain its source units, physical support, averaging and conservation mappings. A 3D/CAD view must preserve geometry and material identity rather than imply a new solved physical model.

The proposed PHWR world model comprises that source-bound physical state, geometry/material occurrence graph and permitted model evolution. Spatial resolution and any dimensional reduction belong to the adopted scientific profile. Observation, prediction and presentation consume the same identified physical subject while retaining separate evidence scopes.

The own coupled formulation retains spatial neutronics and source-supported delayed/poison feedback, conservative solid heat, and the complete supported two-phase/network model. Full equation, property, closure, discretisation, native precision, event and error choices need scientific acceptance before implementation. Numerical primitives do not select these PHWR-specific choices.

## Proposed data flow

This diagram describes the target research system. It does not represent current runtime dependencies or implemented interfaces.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S[Source editions and physical profiles] --> G[Geometry materials and history]
    G --> N[Own spatial neutronics and poisons]
    G --> T[Own solid heat and coolant network]
    N <--> T
    N --> H[Own fuel-history evolution]
    T --> H
    H --> E[Committed refuelling transitions]
    E --> G
    N --> R[Model state and source-bound observations]
    T --> R
    H --> R
    G --> R
    R --> P[Separate model-conditional forecasts]
    Q[Forecast target and future schedule] --> P
    R --> U[Qualified inspection 3D CAD and teaching]
    P --> U
```

Refuelling moves the physical bundle's inventory, provenance, geometry/material association and stored history together. Incoming and discharged bundles remain explicit. A failed or cancelled attempt cannot commit the same event again on restart. Exact source-supported transition laws and their conservation/error evidence remain required.

## Producer and consumer boundary

A future request must identify the exact physical profile, consumed source/data, geometry/material state, initial/boundary/history schedule and observation or prediction question. A future result must identify the actual effective inputs, method/native build, supported quantities and applicable reference/evidence. These are semantic requirements; the public API, wire schema and installed interfaces are not yet accepted.

Missing source data, inconsistent material or occurrence maps, an unsupported regime, or an unsupported forecast target/horizon require explicit refusal. Predictions and visualisations keep their own evidence scope. They do not confer solver, physical or control acceptance.

Reusable primitives, registry semantics, Studio presentation and common workbench execution retain their own project owners. PHWR-specific producer contracts must be accepted jointly with their actual consumers. No runtime dependency, hardware actuation or safety-service capability is declared. [ADR 0001](adr/0001-repository-boundary.md) fixes ownership; [validation](../VALIDATION.md) explains the checks that exist today.

## 1. Ecosystem role

`scpn-fusion-core` is one repository in a multi-repository SCPN ecosystem. Each repository owns
a distinct surface; the boundaries are explicit contracts rather than copied code.

| Repository | Role | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| **`scpn-fusion-core`** (this repo) | **Physics-solver laboratory** | Broad physics kernels, numerical formulation, external-code validation campaigns, facility-data integration, Rust + GPU solver paths, 3D / stellarator / VMEC / free-boundary internals, neural-physics training, and the Petri→SNN control-compiler internals. |
| `scpn-control` | Control-grade integration + facade | Bounded public control APIs, NMPC / controller-loop integration, replay/campaign metadata, HIL / CODAC / EPICS / WebSocket safety boundaries, traceable claim surfaces. Ports/wraps the control-loop subset of FUSION's physics. |
| `scpn-quantum-control` | Quantum + phase-dynamics research | Quantum disruption classifiers, Qiskit/PennyLane execution, quantum Kuramoto/UPDE variants. |
| `scpn-mif-core` | FRC / magneto-inertial fusion | Consumes FUSION's FRC equilibrium / Faraday / compression seams (see [§11](#11-cross-repository-contracts)). |
| `scpn-studio` | Ecosystem hub / verb registry | Consumes per-repo "verbs" + evidence; FUSION is a physics-verb provider. |

A physics model matures **in `scpn-fusion-core` first**; downstream repos wrap the subset that
has a clear control-loop or research contract. FUSION is the canonical owner of the solver-level
mathematics, so the same model is not re-implemented elsewhere.

### 6.1 Equilibrium
- **`fusion_kernel.py` — `FusionKernel`**: non-linear **free-boundary Grad-Shafranov** solver,
  Picard iteration with under-relaxation; inner elliptic solves via Jacobi / SOR / **geometric
  multigrid V-cycle** (`fusion_kernel_iterative_solver` + `multigrid_solve`, Rust-parity).
  Newton-Kantorovich path (`fusion_kernel_newton_solver`, GMRES + Anderson) and free-boundary
  mixin. Rust tier via `RustAcceleratedKernel`; vacuum field via Green's function (elliptic
  integrals). **Input:** grid, coil set, pressure/current profiles. **Output:** ψ(R,Z), magnetic
  axis, X-point, B-field.
- **JAX equilibrium** (`jax_gs_solver`, `jax_equilibrium_solver`): differentiable fixed-boundary
  GS for sensitivity/coil optimisation.
- **`kinetic_efit.py`**: kinetic reconstruction with anisotropic fast-ion pressure + synthetic MSE.
- **`force_balance.py`**: public 2D free-boundary post-solve utility that adjusts paired PF3/PF4
  currents with a Newton radial-force residual loop and writes a balanced equilibrium config. It is
  consumed by validation workflows and documented as a config-balancing utility, not as the quasi-3D
  reduced-order force residual model in `quasi_3d_contracts.py`.
- **`amr_patch.py`**: validation/offline two-level patch AMR utility for X-point and pedestal
  refinement studies. It provides finite-input validation, gradient-threshold patch detection,
  prolongation/restriction, and cylindrical Jacobi patch smoothing; it is not wired into the
  production Grad-Shafranov solve or Rust dispatcher until a parity-backed AMR production lane
  exists. **`eqdsk.py`** handles I/O.
- **3D:** `geometry_3d` (LCFS→toroidal mesh), `equilibrium_3d` (VMEC-style Fourier),
  `fieldline_3d` (tracing/Poincaré), `vmec_lite` (reduced-order spectral), `stellarator_geometry`.

### 6.2 Transport
- **`integrated_transport_solver.py` — `IntegratedTransportSolver`**: 1.5-D transport orchestration;
  Rust tier (`PyTransportSolver`) with Python mixin fallback. Closures: TGLF (external),
  **QLKNN / neural** (`neural_transport`, MLP surrogate) with **out-of-distribution escalation**
  to TGLF, and `neoclassical` (Chang-Hinton χ, Sauter bootstrap). **Input:** Te/Ti/ne profiles +
  geometry. **Output:** evolved profiles, χ_e/χ_i/D, bootstrap current.

### 6.4 Control (`control/`)
- **Classical / optimal**: H-infinity (`h_infinity_controller`), μ-synthesis (`mu_synthesis`),
  constrained NMPC (`nmpc_controller`, `fusion_nmpc_jax`), super-twisting sliding-mode
  (`sliding_mode_vertical`), gain-scheduled PID (`gain_scheduled_controller`), fault-tolerant
  reconfiguration (`fault_tolerant_control`), SVD/MPC trajectory control (`fusion_optimal_control`,
  `neural_surrogate_mpc`), RWM feedback, shape control, density control (with EKF estimator),
  burn control (Bosch-Hale alpha heating). `controller_tuning.py` is an offline/library tuning
  helper for PID gains and reduced H-infinity search parameters; it validates Gym/Gymnasium-style
  PID environments and H-infinity target dictionaries, then returns bounded parameter dictionaries.
  It is not a live controller-loop mutator or deployment path.
- **Disruption**: Transformer predictor (`disruption_predictor`, torch, with checkpoint-trust
  policy + analytical fallback), deterministic linear-risk + tearing physics
  (`disruption_risk_runtime`), contracts, federated learning, Fokker-Planck RE, SPI ablation/mitigation.
- **Free-boundary tracking** (`_free_boundary_*` + `free_boundary_tracking`): kernel-in-the-loop
  isoflux/gap/X-point control with a supervisory safety policy; modular mixin architecture.
- **Flight sim / digital twin**: `tokamak_flight_sim` (actuator lag + delay + noise),
  `rust_flight_sim_wrapper` (Rust 10 kHz), `tokamak_digital_twin`, GDEP digital-twin ingest with
  SNN scenario planning, HIL harness, TORAX hybrid loop.
- **RL / neuro-symbolic**: Gymnasium env (`gym_tokamak_env`), constrained RL with Lagrangian
  multipliers (`safe_rl_controller`), spiking neuro-cybernetic controller (`neuro_cybernetic_controller`,
  embedded LIF), CODAC/EPICS interface (`codac_interface`), state estimator (EKF), RZIP vertical model.

### 6.5 Diagnostics, nuclear, engineering
- **`diagnostics/`**: forward models (interferometer, neutron, Thomson, ECE, soft X-ray,
  bolometer, CXRS), `synthetic_sensors` (magnetics/bolometer/interferometer), `tomography`
  (lsq_linear / SART / ridge inversion).
- **`nuclear/`**: 1-D breeding-blanket neutronics (TBR), neutron wall loading + ash poisoning,
  sputtering/erosion (PWI), TEMHD divertor stabiliser — reduced-order, deterministic, tested.
- **`engineering/`**: balance-of-plant (Rankine + parasitics), CAD ray-trace surface loading,
  thermal-hydraulics (coolant pumping power).

## 10. Symmetric ecosystem architecture

The SCPN repositories are intentionally asymmetric in implementation depth but symmetric in
contract responsibility: each repository owns one public boundary and consumes the others through
documented seams. `scpn-fusion-core` owns physics-solver development and evidence generation; it
does not own downstream deployment posture, facility interlock policy, quantum execution, MIF
system integration, or Studio routing. Those boundaries keep a solver improvement from becoming an
unreviewed deployment claim in another repository.

### 10.1 Responsibility matrix

| Boundary | FUSION owns | Sibling owns | Shared contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| Solver-to-control | Physics kernels, solver configuration, accepted/blocked validation reports, backend dispatch telemetry | Control facade, replay campaign shape, controller safety envelope, HIL/CODAC/EPICS/WebSocket integration | Imported solver subset, deterministic replay metadata, report status, and claim boundary |
| Solver-to-MIF | FRC equilibrium, Faraday recovery, pulsed-compression solver seams, and their evidence gates | Magneto-inertial workflow orchestration, pulsed-system kinematics, RTL/hardware-adjacent paths | FRC public symbols and validation status without duplicated solver mathematics |
| Classical-to-quantum | Classical phase/disruption feature contracts and local evidence | Quantum circuit/model execution, quantum-specific benchmarks, hardware-provider metadata | Feature schemas, phase/replay inputs, and bounded comparison reports |
| Solver-to-Studio | Physics verbs, capability manifest, evidence schemas, architecture-map metadata | Hub registry, user-facing routing, Studio workbench UX, cross-repo aggregation | Generated Studio manifest, schema-A verbs, content digests, and evidence links |

The symmetric rule is operational: if a change alters a shared contract, this repository updates
the FUSION side of the contract, evidence references, and public docs in the same commit. The
sibling repository remains responsible for its facade, runtime adapter, or user workflow. Where a
contract has not been reconciled, public docs must say that the row is blocked or diagnostic rather
than implying downstream readiness.

## 11. Cross-repository contracts

What `scpn-fusion-core` provides to siblings:

- **To `scpn-control`**: the equilibrium/transport/free-boundary solver subset,
  the deterministic TORAX review envelope, and the Petri→SNN compiler
  internals; CONTROL wraps the control-loop subset behind bounded public APIs
  and the Studio control vertical. TORAX runtime outcomes are provenance, not
  actuation commands.
- **To `scpn-mif-core`**: FRC rigid-rotor equilibrium, Faraday induction recovery, and pulsed-compression
  seams; the canonical FRC physics lives here.
- **To `scpn-quantum-control`**: the classical Kuramoto/UPDE phase engine and disruption-feature
  contracts; quantum variants live in QUANTUM.
- **To `scpn-studio`**: physics "verbs" (solve / diagnose / validate) and their evidence, consumed
  via the studio platform package.

Consumers should treat the **dispatched kernels** ([§3.1](#31-the-fastest-first-dispatcher-core_multi_compatpy))
and the **IO seam** ([§4](#4-inputs-ingest-seam--io--coreeqdsk)–[§5](#5-outputs-emit-seam)) as the stable
integration surface, and the **public CLI modes** ([§8](#8-entry-points-and-public-api)) as the stable

## Public Development Workbench and the 4.0.0 Roadmap

**SC-NeuroCore will remain a public, open-source development workbench** for the
**SC Neuromorphic Computing Systems** group. It brings together a connected
engineering workflow: model neural behaviour, encode and process events, train
and simulate networks, compile selected computations for hardware, and inspect
the resulting evidence. Its breadth lets researchers and engineers develop and
test the interfaces between those stages in one place.

The workbench supports experimentation, comparisons across runtimes and
integration of the complete workflow. Focused repositories give teams clearer
entry points and smaller dependency boundaries when they need one part of it.
SC-NeuroCore continues as the place to bring those parts together.

The split architecture is prepared for the **unpublished 4.0.0 roadmap**.
Repository names and responsibilities are established; implementation and release
status are described separately in the map. The current public package remains
at the version shown above, with its existing installation instructions.

| Part of the map | Repositories and purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Foundation and execution | **SC-NC-CORE**, **SC-NC-CATALOGUE**, **SC-NC-ENGINE** and **SC-NC-BRIDGES**: numerical primitives, models, accelerated execution and interchange. |
| Learning and data | **SC-NC-LEARN**, **SC-NC-DATA** and **SC-NC-ANALYSIS**: training and adaptation, datasets and encodings, spike analysis and visualisation. |
| Silicon and verification | **SC-NC-COMPILER**, **SC-NC-HARDWARE** and **SC-NC-VERIFY**: RTL generation, target integration, formal checks and fault analysis. |
| Workspace and research | **SC-NC-STUDIO**, **SC-NC-RESEARCH** and **SC-NC-BENCH**: visual workflows, experimental work and workload-specific benchmarks. |
| Supporting tools and instrumentation | **LOOP-TIMING-WITNESS** and **25 tools**: timing measurements, data quality, numerical conformance, provenance, deployment and assurance evidence. |

Future components may be open-source or proprietary products. Their boundaries
and licensing remain under discussion with investors and IP partners, and will
be announced per project. **Several supporting tools will remain public.** This
roadmap does not change the current repository's open-source license or its
continuing public workbench role.

The [group and project map](docs/ecosystem.md) presents all 13 specialized
repositories, 25 supporting tools and LOOP-TIMING-WITNESS, with their functions
and current status. Read it as a map of responsibilities and implementation
status; future licensing decisions will be announced separately. Migration
guides will accompany component releases.

# SC-NeuroCore — System Architecture Map

> Canonical architecture map. Package version `3.16.0`; refreshed against the
> current tree on 2026-07-14. Supersedes the earlier `architecture.md` and
> `COMPONENT_INVENTORY.md` in this directory, which are stale (see *Provenance*).
>
> Purpose: a single, factual reference to SC-NeuroCore's capabilities, data flow,
> inputs/outputs, processing models, backends and their wiring — for sibling
> repositories and for the STUDIO integration layer. Every structural claim is
> anchored to the source tree; quantitative or model claims carry a file
> reference. No marketing language, no speculative naming.

---

## 1. What SC-NeuroCore is

A three-tier stochastic-computing (SC) spiking-neural-network framework that takes
a network defined in Python down to bit-true RTL on FPGA/ASIC silicon:

| Tier | Location | Substance |
|------|----------|-----------|
| **Software simulation** | `src/sc_neurocore/` (121 subpackages, ~57k LoC Python) | Neuron/synapse models, SC arithmetic, network engine, learning, analysis |
| **Compiled engine** | `engine/` (Rust + PyO3 → `sc_neurocore_engine`), `crates/` (7 research crates), `src/sc_neurocore/accel/` (Julia/Go/Mojo/JAX kernels) | SIMD SC inference, fixed-point integrators, spike-train analysis, IR emit |
| **Hardware** | `hdl/` (Verilog RTL, 43 top-level non-testbench modules), `hdl_gen/`, `compiler/`, `asic_flow/` | Synthesisable RTL, FPGA bitstreams, ASIC flow |

The defining design choice is **stochastic computing**: values are encoded as
Bernoulli/quasi-random bitstreams, so arithmetic becomes single-gate logic
(multiply = AND/XNOR, scaled-add = MUX) — directly mappable to extremely small,
low-power digital hardware. The SHD pipeline is proven end-to-end on a Zynq
XC7Z020 (`ARCHITECTURE.md` §SHD; 1 317 LUT / 2.5 %).

### Module tiers (from `pyproject.toml` + `__init__.py`)

- **Core (ships in the wheel)** — imported by default; the production surface:
  `neurons`, `synapses`, `layers`, `sources`, `recorders`, `core`, `utils`,
  `accel`, `network`, `learning`, `compiler`, `ir`, `hdl_gen`, `hardware`,
  `nir_bridge`, `math`, `solvers`, `scpn`, `adapters`, `spike_codec`, and more.
- **Research (source-available, excluded from the built wheel)** — explicitly
  excluded in `[tool.setuptools.packages.find] exclude`: `audio`, `generative`,
  `world_model`, `dashboard`, `viz`, `analysis`, `experiments`, `drivers`,
  `interfaces`, `swarm`, `sleep`, `optics`, `chaos`, `bio`, `robotics`,
  `physics`. Functional but not part of the supported binary distribution.
- **Contrib (not a package)** — speculative material lives under the repo-root
  `research/` tree (`eschaton/`, `speculative/`, `meta/`, `transcendent/`,
  `exotic/`, `post_silicon/`); it is **not** importable as `sc_neurocore.*` and
  is out of scope for this map.

## 3. The spine: end-to-end data flow

```
 float input
    │  BitstreamEncoder (LFSR x^16+x^14+x^13+x^11+1, or Sobol/Halton quasi-random)
    ▼
 bitstream  (uint8 0/1, or packed uint64 words)
    │  ── multiply = AND (unipolar) / XNOR (bipolar [-1,1]);  scaled-add = MUX
    ▼
 SC primitives ── neurons (fixed-point LIF, Q8.8) · synapses · SC layers
    │              (packed 64-bit AND + popcount in VectorizedSCLayer)
    ▼
 Network engine  (network.Network: clock-driven step loop)
    │  per timestep: apply stimuli → CSR projection matvec → population.step_all
    │               → record → STDP plasticity update → optional FIM sync
    ▼
 outputs ── spikes / membrane voltages / firing rates / packed bitstreams
    │
    ▼
 analysis & decode (spike-train statistics, decoders) · spike codecs (BCI) · export
```

Bipolar `[-1, 1]` SC (XNOR multiply) is the fundamental signed primitive — it is
what allows signed-weight networks on SC hardware (`core/bipolar.py`).

### Network engine step loop (verified)

`network.Network` (`network/network.py:59`) is the central simulation entry point.
`run(...)` (`:102`) routes to one of three backends; the Python loop
`_run_python` (`:203`) per timestep:

1. zero the per-population current accumulator;
2. `_apply_stimuli()` (`:220`) — inject configured input currents;
3. `_apply_projections()` (`:221`) — CSR sparse weight matvec across projections;
4. `population.step_all(currents, spike_gating)` (`:225`) — advance every neuron;
5. `_record(...)` (`:227`) — spike/voltage recorders;
6. `_update_plasticity()` (`:229`) — STDP weight updates;
7. optional `_apply_fim()` (`:231`) — Fisher-Information-Metric synchronisation.

Backends: **Rust engine** (high throughput), **MPI** (`network/mpi_runner.py`,
distributed), **pure NumPy** (full feature parity: plasticity, FIM, spike-gating).
Per the source, plasticity / FIM / spike-gating run on the Python path; the Rust
and MPI paths cover a subset (see Audit for the exact gap).

## What this repository is for

`scpn-quantum-control` is an evidence-governed workbench for turning
coupled-oscillator models into quantum-control experiments, simulator studies,
gradient-bearing optimisation loops, and auditable hardware-result packages.
It is for teams that need a repeatable path from a physical model to a result
that can be reviewed, reproduced, cited, or used in an application pilot.

If your team needs reproducible research or product-grade experimentation, the
repository provides:

- a stable route from `K_nm`/`omega` problem definitions to simulators;
- deterministic artefact-led evidence for method claims;
- bounded optimisation and differentiable-programming surfaces for training,
  verification, and convergence analysis;
- hardware campaign management that separates committed raw-count rows from
  simulator and scoped-failure classes.

It is positioned for use-cases where decision quality depends on evidence:
engineering teams that need a consistent pathway from model specification to
observable contracts, and research teams that need explicit failure modes rather
than implied coverage.

## Scientific problem inputs and parameter schemas

`KuramotoProblem` remains the original symmetric coupling/frequency owner.
Its existing constructors, compilers and raw metadata codec retain their
contracts. `ScientificDesign` supplies an immutable declaration;
`ScientificProblemParameters(problem, design)` validates that declaration
against the actual problem and produces a separate `scientific_problem.v1`
companion. The original `oscillatools` numerical kernels remain independent
of Studio and Atlas. The scientific companion adapter
consumes the existing workspace `ParameterSpec`, typed float64 payloads and
canonical codec instead of defining another workspace format or solver.

The companion identity includes the declared model and coupling convention,
logical/physical coordinates, explicit graph, units, initial/history state,
observable, design objective and trainable parameter names. Arrays own immutable
byte buffers; caller edits and mutations of exported dictionaries cannot rebind
an existing identity. Topology contains sorted unique undirected index pairs,
covers every nonzero coupling, and retains declared zero-weight edges.

| Declaration | Phase dynamics | Quantum XY spin model |
|---|---|---|
| Model | `phase_kuramoto` | `quantum_xy` |
| Coupling convention | `pairwise_sum` or `population_mean` | Original `pairwise_sum` |
| Initial state | `float64 (N,)` phase angles | Normalized `complex128 (2**N,)` amplitudes |
| State unit | `rad` | `1` |
| Observable | `phase_order_parameter`, nonnegative weights with positive total | `spin_z`, finite per-qubit weights |
| History | Optional strictly increasing times ending at zero; final state equals initial state | Phase history refused |
| Objective | Simulation, synchronisation target in `[0,1]`, observable maximisation | Simulation, observable maximisation, gate-count minimisation |

Rates and coupling must declare `rad/s` with time `s`, or explicitly declare
dimensionless rates/coupling/time as `1`. Both observables use unit `1`;
gate-count targets use `gate`. A `Hz` label, mixed dimensional regime, invalid
observable/state shape, nonfinite input or incompatible model refuses before
export or compilation. Units are checked exactly and never converted by labels.
Physical indices are a declaration, without placement or calibration evidence.

`effective_problem()` returns an independent original-owner problem. Phase
`population_mean` explicitly projects the supplied weights to `K/N`; pairwise
sum preserves them. The frequency vector and units retain their meaning.
The companion's `compile_hamiltonian()` only accepts a declared quantum XY
model and calls the original compiler. A phase declaration cannot silently
become a quantum-spin model. Initial state, history, observable and objectives
are design inputs; the companion does not execute a trajectory or optimise them.

## Circuit transformations and measurement preservation

`scpn_quantum_control.compiler.compile_circuit_to_mlir` accepts a bound native
Qiskit circuit or a bounded static OpenQASM 2 source. It lowers the unitary body
through the original native transpiler to `rx`, `ry`, `rz` and `cx`, then attaches
the original trailing measurement/barrier block at its original bit indices.
Optimising the unitary body separately preserves phase-sensitive semantics that
an optimisation conditioned on final measurement could otherwise discard.
The transpiler receives no assumption that input qubits are zero. Its virtual
output permutations are materialised through native permutation synthesis before
readout is attached, preserving both arbitrary input states and original bit indices.

`qualify_circuit_pass` also qualifies an existing transformation, including the
original global unitary folding output. Its immutable `CircuitPassRecord` stores
both instruction IRs, exact source text and digests, real statement spans, register
indices, logical-to-physical layouts, observable correspondence, the explicit
global-phase policy and the measured reference error. Source offsets count Python
Unicode characters; line and column are one-based. Generated rotation source uses
round-trip decimal parameters instead of approximate multiples of pi.

## Classical-to-Quantum Mapping

Each module maps a classical SCPN computation to its quantum analog:

These are declared encoding or modelling choices. The phase Kuramoto ODE and
quantum XY spin dynamics have different state spaces and observables; matching
coupling/frequency coefficients does not establish dynamical equivalence.
Scientific problem companions keep the two models distinct.

| Classical (SCPN) | Quantum (this repo) | Mapping |
|-------------------|---------------------|---------|
| Stochastic LIF membrane potential | Ry(theta) rotation angle | theta = pi * (v - v_rest) / (v_threshold - v_rest) |
| Bitstream AND-gate synapse | CRy(theta_w) controlled rotation | P(out) = P(pre) * sin^2(theta_w/2) |
| STDP correlation learning | Parameter-shift gradient rule | dw = lr * pre * d<Z>/d(theta) |
| Kuramoto ODE (dtheta/dt) | XY Hamiltonian Trotter evolution | H = -K_ij(XX + YY) - omega_i Z_i |
| 16-layer UPDE coupling | 16-qubit spin chain | Knm -> J_ij entangling gates |
| MPC quadratic cost | QAOA Ising Hamiltonian | ||state - target||^2 -> ZZ + Z terms |
| Grad-Shafranov PDE | VQLS linear system | Laplacian A, source b -> A|x> ~ |b> |
| SPN token probability | Qubit amplitude | p -> amplitude encoding |
| Disruption feature vector | Amplitude-encoded state | 11-D -> 16-D zero-padded |

# Evidence and numerical boundary

A completed-job producer supplies original observations and separate custody facts. Import preserves foreign bytes, original representations and field origin. A count total, requested resource, calibration label and observed timestamp are distinct assertions.

Derivation binds the actual installed programme, environment lock, ordered inputs, output schema, full scalar inventory, precision, units, comparison and optional seed. Earlier raw output is validated before later execution/output wrappers. Failure, cancellation and resource refusal retain actual diagnostics without producing a successful output.

The shared runtime owns content addressing, canonicalisation, signing and Common evaluation. The pack owns domain comparison and policy conjunction. Common success does not certify physical measurement or current domain eligibility. Verification creates a separate immutable report for the explicit policy and time.

Caller-owned unsigned and protected trust contexts have different fields. Selected source versions and installed types must agree with the whole request and evaluation inputs. Historical intervals need genuine event sources; an operational evaluation witness is not their replacement.

Inspection retains complete claims, reasons, quantities, references and unavailable states without executing programmes or granting eligibility. Rendering escapes foreign text and preserves full scope. Assurance resolves actual class information rather than relabelling a declared validation token.

## Purpose and evidence state

`SCPN-REACTOR-KERNELS` is the shared kernel library of the SCPN Reactor
Systems Research Group. It owns three implemented kernel groups at
`computational_prototype` in `src/scpn_reactor_kernels/`: the geometry
kernels (design records ADR 0002 and ADR 0007, evidence record
`VALIDATION.md#geometry-kernels`; owned domain `shared_geometry_kernels`)
and the numerics kernels (design record ADR 0003, evidence record
`VALIDATION.md#numerics-kernels`; the numerical substrate of the owned
domain `shared_physics_kernels`) and the optional CAD adapters on pinned
third-party C++ kernels (ADR 0006, `VALIDATION.md#cad-kernels`, owned domain
`shared_cad_and_meshing_adapters`).
Every other section below describes boundaries and contracts. The claim
inventory is empty; the kernel inventory is generated and drift-checked.

## Why a library

Twenty device-family repositories each need the same published closed
forms (reactivities, radiation, collisions, confinement criteria, fields,
inductances, circuit elements), the same integrators and the same
tessellation and export substrate. Copying them twenty times would create
twenty sources of truth; leaving them inside the tokamak solver would tie
eighteen non-tokamak families to a solver they do not consume. The library
is the single implementation, versioned and pinned by digest, with one
evidence record per kernel.

## The kernel contract

Every kernel satisfies all of the following before it enters the manifest:

1. A published form or a standard method, cited in the module docstring
   with the exact equation and its validity range; the source is on file
   in the private ledger where legally obtainable, otherwise the record
   says so.
2. A pure-Python floor as the public API with zero runtime dependencies,
   strict typing, NumPy-convention docstrings, fail-closed input
   validation (non-finite and out-of-range inputs are refused, never
   clamped).
3. A native kernel in `rust/` with the identical operation order, using
   only correctly rounded operations (`+ - * /`, `sqrt`) and vendored
   deterministic implementations of anything else (polynomial
   trigonometry, cube roots), so results agree with the floor bit for bit.
4. Parity tests comparing float64 bit patterns, never tolerances.
5. Statement- and branch-complete tests with analytic anchors (published
   reference values, closed-form identities, convergence orders).
6. A benchmark row per backend following the ecosystem benchmark standard.
7. An entry in `kernels-domain.json` (identifier, module, sources, maturity,
   evidence pointer, native parity flag, benchmark pointer).

For the CAD group, ADR 0006 records the third-party backend boundary:
`native_parity=false`, with physical measures checked against analytic
references rather than an independent Rust floor. B-rep values and native
STEP exports use metres. The volume-mesh adapter explicitly converts
declared STEP units to metres before meshing and reports cubic metres.

## Contract surfaces and versioning

- `kernels-domain.json` follows schema `scpn.reactor-kernels-domain.v1`;

- The distribution `scpn-reactor-kernels` follows semantic versioning; a
  kernel whose output changes for any input is a breaking change
  of that kernel and bumps the major version.
- Consumers record `{distribution, version, inventory_sha256}` in their own
  manifests; the `consumers` list here is updated when a consumer lands.

A kernel promoted beyond `computational_prototype` (documented accepted
cases with thresholds), a consumer's first pin, publication of the
distribution, or a FUSION seam migration that retires an overlapping
helper — each recorded as a versioned change in a new ADR.

**SCPN Control** is a research-grade control and validation package for fusion
plasma control loops. It turns stochastic Petri-net logic into executable
neuro-symbolic controllers, surrounds those controllers with runtime
pre/post-condition contracts, and connects them to equilibrium, transport,
disruption, digital-twin, and hardware-in-the-loop evidence gates.

The practical purpose is simple: help fusion teams decide whether a controller
idea is safe enough, fast enough, reproducible enough, and well-evidenced enough
to move from notebook experiments toward a facility control-system review.

## Who it is for

- Fusion control researchers prototyping PCS logic, NMPC, SNN, disruption, and
  mitigation controllers.
- Tokamak and stellarator programmes that need replayable validation artefacts
  before promoting algorithms toward hardware tests.
- Fusion startups that need a compact control package rather than a broad solver
  laboratory.
- Universities teaching plasma control, formal methods, differentiable physics,
  and control-system safety cases.
- Investors, grant reviewers, and collaborators who need to understand which
  claims are already evidenced and which claims are still blocked by external
  data, external codes, target hardware, or facility access.

## What the package does

- Compiles stochastic Petri nets into spiking-neural control artefacts with
  bounded marking, transition, and temporal-logic evidence.
- Runs control-facing equilibrium and transport facades for controller tuning,
  replay, and validation admission.
- Provides NMPC, robust control, phase-dynamics, reinforcement-learning,
  digital-twin, WebSocket, CODAC/EPICS-facing, and hardware evidence surfaces.
- Captures validation results as checksum-bound JSON/Markdown reports instead
  of unverifiable claims.
- Keeps facility-grade promotion fail-closed until the required measured-shot,
  public-reference, external-code, hardware, or independent-review artefacts
  are supplied and admitted.

- **Formal verification is bounded, model-level evidence**: The repository
  includes Petri-net reachability, temporal-logic, Z3-backed, certificate-bundle,

## Executive overview (What SPO Is and What It Is Not)

SPO is a synchronisation-analysis toolkit for systems that can be expressed as coupled oscillatory processes, with a review-only control-proposal surface. It gives teams a single interface for turning telemetry into phase variables, evaluating coherence, and *proposing* bounded control updates with replay evidence for human review — it does not close a control loop on hardware.

In practical terms, SPO is useful when:

- A domain has reusable cycle structure (time-of-day shifts, wave timing, phase-locked loops, rhythm-driven events, spatially propagating oscillations).
- Operational teams need explainable interventions before actuation, not black-box controller outputs.
- Governance requires deterministic evidence trails, policy guardrails, and cross-language consistency checks.

SPO is not a universal AI controller, a live PLC hardening platform, or a ready-made certified hardware stack. It is a synchrony-aware simulation and control framework that can be embedded in those ecosystems after domain validation and adapter-specific evidence are attached.

The immediate commercial value is the reduction of uncertainty in phase-control projects: instead of asking whether a system is "stable" from a single metric, teams get shared, auditable artefacts for **what was measured, what was proposed, what was bounded, and what was replayed**.

For a compact business, operator, and technical orientation, read the
[Executive Overview](docs/getting-started/executive_overview.md). It explains
where SPO creates value, how the pieces fit together, which surfaces are
execution-ready, and which frontier tracks remain review-only until external
evidence is attached.

An open measurement instrument, in design, that timestamps the events of a real-time control
loop in FPGA fabric and reports latency, jitter, deadline misses, fault response and energy per

**Evidence maturity: `architecture_only`.** No board instrument has been built or measured. The

command that reports simulation provenance separately from

validator.

## The measurement problem

Real-time control on embedded systems-on-chip is usually characterised by software that times
itself on the processor under test: a timer wake-up benchmark, or timestamps logged by the
control task. Those numbers share clock, scheduler and interrupts with the system being
measured, often describe a proxy task rather than the control loop, and rarely come with energy
per cycle or with the effect of latency on control quality. Moving a controller between a Linux
task, a bare-metal core and FPGA logic therefore changes the measurement method along with the
placement.

## What the instrument is designed to do

For one closed control loop on one PolarFire SoC Icicle Kit, the planned instrument:

1. timestamps every sample-ready, sample-read, actuator-write and deadline event in FPGA fabric
   on a 64-bit counter clocked at 100 MHz (10 ns resolution);
2. reports latency and jitter as distributions (median, 95th, 99th and 99.9th percentile,
   maximum) and counts deadline misses in hardware;
3. compares three controller placements under identical plant and controller definitions: Linux
   user space on the U54 application cores, a bare-metal loop on one U54 core in asymmetric
   multiprocessing, and fixed-point logic in fabric;
4. relates latency to the tracking error of an emulated plant in the same run;
5. estimates energy per control cycle from the board's PAC1934 power monitor, with the limits
   stated in [`docs/MEASUREMENT_PROTOCOL.md`](https://github.com/anulum/loop-timing-witness/blob/main/docs/MEASUREMENT_PROTOCOL.md);
6. injects faults and measures detection and time to a defined safe actuator state;
7. writes every run as raw event records plus a hashed manifest, so a run can be repeated and
   audited.

## Evidence boundary and non-claims

- No board latency, jitter, deadline, energy or control-quality number has been measured.
  Functional simulation results and native regression timings are separately labelled.
- No physical board is currently available; development and verification use simulation.
- No statement about PolarFire SoC performance is made before a measured run with its manifest
  and hashes exists.
- No comparison with other vendors or platforms is part of the project.
- The target board has not been used yet; the platform facts in the manifest come from the board
  user guide and are marked `verified_on_hardware: false`.
- Hardware timing measurement from FPGA fabric is established prior work (see below). The
  planned contribution is its application to complete control-loop events across three
  placements with control quality, energy and fault response in the same run, published as
  reproducible run records — not the idea of measuring from fabric.

## Relation to SC-NeuroCore

Loop Timing Witness is developed as hardware-validation tooling for
[SC-NeuroCore](https://github.com/anulum/sc-neurocore), an open neuromorphic computing library.
The `COMPUTE` profile is designed to measure the memory-mapped write, compute, read and interrupt

### Event witness and buffer

`rtl/event_witness.sv` connects `rtl/event_record_capture.sv` to a Gray-pointer dual-clock
FIFO and separate reset-release synchronisers. It accepts one event-code/cycle tuple per
capture-clock edge without stalling the measured source. The original timestamp is retained
through the capture pipeline and drain. Event codes are declared in `measurement-domain.json`
and `rtl/event_codes_pkg.sv`. Public ports and reset/overflow behaviour are specified in
[`FABRIC_WITNESS.md`](FABRIC_WITNESS.md). The integrated plant entry point uses `control_event_capture.sv` to preserve simultaneous
strobes before serialization; its ports are in [`PLANT_WITNESS.md`](PLANT_WITNESS.md). The AXI
board interface remains planned.

The default buffer holds 16 384 records. A full buffer drops the newest record, pulses
`event_dropped`, latches `overflowed` and increments a saturating 32-bit count. Reset starts a
new run and flushes both clock domains; there is no independent-domain reset. Capture-domain
status is not a coherent processor snapshot. A nonzero overflow count invalidates the host run.

Linux is planned to drain at least 20 times per second. At 20 kHz with four periodic events per
cycle the buffer fills in about 205 ms, longer than the 50 ms slowest drain interval; the
validator checks that inequality and the declared Gray-pointer capacity. Drain frequency alone
cannot establish sustained throughput or prevent loss during software stalls; board RAM sizing,
drain bandwidth and physical CDC constraints still require qualification.

Derived intervals per cycle:

| Interval | Definition |
|---|---|
| scheduling latency | `SAMPLE_READ − SAMPLE_READY` |
| compute time | `ACT_WRITE − SAMPLE_READ` |
| loop latency | `ACT_WRITE − SAMPLE_READY` |
| time to safe state | `SAFE_STATE −` first missed `DEADLINE` |

A cycle misses its deadline when `ACT_WRITE` does not arrive before `DEADLINE`.

### Deadline and safe-state monitor

The monitor counts misses in hardware. After a configurable number of consecutive misses it drives
the actuator to a defined safe value, raises a latched fault flag and interrupt, and records
`SAFE_STATE`.

## Power and energy

The selected Microchip [`pac1934` driver](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/linux4microchip/linux/linux-6.18-mchp/drivers/iio/adc/pac1934.c)
uses the Linux IIO interface. The logger must bind the selected BSP/driver revision, channel-to-rail
mapping, shunts, sampling configuration and accumulator units. An assumed `hwmon` interface or
automatic direct-I²C fallback cannot establish that acquisition contract.

The native UIO entry accepts `--power-config file --power-journal file` together. Its separate
normal-policy worker validates the actual IIO node, kernel release, driver, enabled accumulators,
labels, sample rate and unsigned shunt scales. It preserves each raw/scale attribute with its own
host and fabric read brackets. The journal is acquisition evidence; it is not the analyzer's
qualified `power.csv`. The current host has no PAC1934 device, so successful physical acquisition
and energy-window qualification remain unverified. See [`HOST_ANALYSIS.md`](HOST_ANALYSIS.md)
for the explicit configuration and units.

Fabric counter brackets around acquisition and the driver's cache/refresh timing must be retained.
Sequential channel reads do not establish an atomic four-rail snapshot or an exact common fabric
tick. Energy-window alignment remains unqualified until the acquisition timing contract is
validated on the board. The reported metric is mean energy per control cycle over windows of many
cycles, per rail and for the four rails together, with the limits stated in
[`MEASUREMENT_PROTOCOL.md`](MEASUREMENT_PROTOCOL.md).

The source module exports canonicalization, byte references, inspection, difference, seal and verification operations, with four offline command grammars. Installed packaging and operational root, signer, clock and domain qualification are not supplied by this checkout. Common report eligibility and command completion do not establish scientific acceptance.

The implemented infrastructure checks local metadata, attribution, workflows, dependency alignment, documentation and inventory. The preflight command combines those gates with the complete development-tool checks. A successful report covers only the requested local repository operation.
