## Polyglot backend architecture

Compute kernels follow a **fastest-measured-first dispatch chain** ([ADR 0002](../adr/0002-multi-language-acceleration-and-dispatch.md)):
the runtime selects the fastest available in-process backend per kernel; CLI surfaces
(Julia, Mojo) are measured/parity surfaces, not the in-process hot path. The ordering
is regenerated from `bench/results/` into `bench/dispatch.toml`; `scpn_mif_core._dispatch`
reads it. Python is the guaranteed floor.

## Cross-repository ownership boundaries

MIF stays strictly inside its lane ([ADR 0001](../adr/0001-repository-scope-and-ownership-boundaries.md)):

| Owned by a sibling — consumed, never duplicated | Sibling |
|---|---|
| Hall-MHD / FRC equilibrium / MRTI / tilt / self-consistent compression | SCPN-FUSION-CORE |
| Petri-net runtime, NMPC, replay, neuro-symbolic controller | SCPN-CONTROL |
| SNN→Verilog, Q8.8 SNN encoder, AER router HDL | SC-NEUROCORE |
| Reusable Swarmalator / coherence-monitor primitives | SCPN-PHASE-ORCHESTRATOR |

MIF owns: FRC kinematic merging, the pulsed-shot lifecycle, the capacitor bank, the AER
sensor bridge, the sub-50 ns target trigger fabric, the timing-aware formal tier, the Lean
kinematic-safety invariant, and Faraday recovery. Several kinematic surfaces are
`SYNC-STATE: upstream-pending` — implemented locally until the reusable surface lands in
the owning sibling.

## Evidence state

The full board instrument remains planned and no measured result exists. Synthesizable
timestamp capture, a dual-clock record buffer, numeric event codes, a run-manifest schema and
host analysis exist. Both sampled plants, references, deadline/safe-state monitor, fault injector
and simultaneous-event capture feed the drain stream and host CLI in simulation. C, Rust and
RTL PID/LQR kernels have bit-exact parity, with an integrated fabric feedback loop and native
command replay through simulated actuator transactions. Native AXI simulation and Linux UIO run
software are implemented; physical I/O, power acquisition and processor timing remain unqualified.
No physical board is available. The
machine-readable design contract is `measurement-domain.json`, validated by
`tools/validate_measurement_domain.py`; changes to that contract also update its schema, this
document and the measurement protocol.

## Target platform

PolarFire SoC Icicle Kit, device MPFS250T-FCVG484E, as described in the board user guide
(Microchip DS60001679E). Facts used by the design:

| Item | Use in the design |
|---|---|
| SiFive E51 monitor core and four U54 application cores | E51 boots the system; U54 cores run Linux or a bare-metal controller |
| On-board 50 MHz oscillator | reference for the fabric clock conditioning circuit |
| PAC1934 power monitor on the processor subsystem I²C bus, four rails (VDD, VDD25, VDDA25, VDDA) | energy windows |
| Two Gigabit Ethernet ports | run control and data transfer to the host |
| Raspberry Pi 4 compatible header | optional mirror of the event strobes for an external logic analyser |

Not yet checked on hardware, and therefore not relied on: the asymmetric-multiprocessing
reference release for the current board support package, the PAC1934 sampling configuration of
the reference Linux image, and the fabric RAM budget used to freeze the event buffer size.

The board-facing `rtl/icicle_witness.sv` presents a 38-bit AXI4-Lite address port to a fabric
interconnect that selects the planned 256-byte register range at `0x60020000` through
`0x600200ff`. It passes the low eight address bits to `axi_control_witness` and exposes its
retained interrupt level. This boundary is exercised in simulation; the Libero interconnect,
capture clock, interrupt route and physical timing are not yet qualified.
The pinned Icicle reference source configures the FIC0 bus clock at 125 MHz from CCC GL0_0
and the witness capture clock at 100 MHz from CCC GL0_1. Those source settings do not
establish implemented clock rates or CDC timing closure.

### Plant emulator

A discrete-time second-order plant (mass, spring, damper) and a first-order thermal plant, in
signed fixed point with a documented Q format per plant. The plant updates once per sample period
(100 Hz to 20 kHz, 1 kHz by default) with the most recent actuator value that arrived before the
update; a late command is applied one period later and counted. A reference generator (step,
ramp, sine) provides the tracking target. Implemented Q8.24 equations, coefficients and ports
are specified in [`PLANT_WITNESS.md`](PLANT_WITNESS.md).

### Controller input/output register and strobes

An AXI4-Lite peripheral on a fabric interface controller holds the sample register, the actuator
register and the cycle counter. It raises the `CONTROL` profile strobes:

| Event | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SAMPLE_READY` | plant update complete |
| `SAMPLE_READ` | first bus read of the sample register in the cycle |
| `ACT_WRITE` | first timely actuator command in the cycle |
| `ACT_LATE` | first accepted out-of-cycle or deadline-edge command, tagged with its observation cycle |
| `DEADLINE` | next sample instant |
| `SAFE_STATE` | safe actuator value applied by the monitor |
| `FAULT_INJECTED` | fault injector action |
| `FAULT_DETECTED` | monitor detects the injected fault |

### Event witness and buffer

`rtl/event_witness.sv` connects `rtl/event_record_capture.sv` to a Gray-pointer dual-clock
FIFO and separate reset-release synchronisers. It accepts one event-code/cycle tuple per
capture-clock edge without stalling the measured source. The original timestamp is retained
through the capture pipeline and drain. Event codes are declared in `measurement-domain.json`
and `rtl/event_codes_pkg.sv`. Public ports and reset/overflow behaviour are specified in
[`FABRIC_WITNESS.md`](FABRIC_WITNESS.md). The integrated plant entry point uses `control_event_capture.sv` to preserve simultaneous
strobes before serialization; its ports are in [`PLANT_WITNESS.md`](PLANT_WITNESS.md). The AXI
board interface remains planned.

The default buffer holds 16 384 records. A full buffer drops the newest record, pulses
`event_dropped`, latches `overflowed` and increments a saturating 32-bit count. Reset starts a
new run and flushes both clock domains; there is no independent-domain reset. Capture-domain
status is not a coherent processor snapshot. A nonzero overflow count invalidates the host run.

Linux is planned to drain at least 20 times per second. At 20 kHz with four periodic events per
cycle the buffer fills in about 205 ms, longer than the 50 ms slowest drain interval; the
validator checks that inequality and the declared Gray-pointer capacity. Drain frequency alone
cannot establish sustained throughput or prevent loss during software stalls; board RAM sizing,
drain bandwidth and physical CDC constraints still require qualification.

Derived intervals per cycle:

| Interval | Definition |
|---|---|
| scheduling latency | `SAMPLE_READ − SAMPLE_READY` |
| compute time | `ACT_WRITE − SAMPLE_READ` |
| loop latency | `ACT_WRITE − SAMPLE_READY` |
| time to safe state | `SAFE_STATE −` first missed `DEADLINE` |

A cycle misses its deadline when `ACT_WRITE` does not arrive before `DEADLINE`.

### Deadline and safe-state monitor

The monitor counts misses in hardware. After a configurable number of consecutive misses it drives
the actuator to a defined safe value, raises a latched fault flag and interrupt, and records
`SAFE_STATE`.

### Fault injector

Drops a sample-ready interrupt, delays it by a number of periods, freezes the actuator register,
or requests a processor overload scenario from the software load generator. Every injection is an
event on the same timebase, so detection latency comes from the same clock as everything else.

### Fabric controller

`fixed_point_controller.sv` implements PID with conditional integration and discrete LQR.
`fabric_control_witness.sv` connects it to the sampled plant and existing independent monitor,
record capture and drain. In simulation the first read follows sample-ready by one tick and
the timely actuator write follows by another tick. This is a registered RTL schedule, not
physical timing closure. Arithmetic, reset, coefficients and native counterparts are specified
in [`CONTROLLERS.md`](CONTROLLERS.md). A board placement register remains planned.

### Device-under-test slot and the `COMPUTE` profile

The register, strobes and witness are built around a generic slot: an AXI4-Lite peripheral with

## Verification of the instrument

1. **Simulation** before hardware: witness, buffer, plant, monitor and fabric controller with a
   vendor-neutral simulator, directed and randomised tests, bit-exact parity of fabric, C and
   Rust controllers, including complete 64,000-sample trajectories per plant/controller.
2. **Known-period test:** a period generated from the same timebase must appear as an exact
   interval; any deviation is a witness defect.
3. **Injected-delay test:** a delay of k periods must measure as k periods within one tick.
4. **Bus-offset calibration:** the fabric placement, with no processor involvement, gives the
   minimum read and write path latency, recorded as the instrument floor.
5. **External cross-check (optional):** mirrored strobes on a logic analyser agree within the
   analyser's resolution.
6. **Overflow test:** an undrained buffer must be counted as overflow and invalidate the run.

`rtl/event_witness.sv` connects the timestamp capture to a dual-clock FIFO. This is a
simulation-tested stream component. Peripheral event arbitration, AXI/UIO access, coherent
processor status snapshots, physical clock constraints and board qualification remain planned.
The domain maturity is `architecture_only`; the capability inventory remains empty.

## Event input and record output

| Port | Clock domain | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `event_valid`, `event_code[7:0]`, `cycle_number[31:0]` | capture | One tuple per rising edge when `capture_active` is high. No backpressure. |
| `capture_active` | capture | Local run reset has released. |
| `counter_ticks[63:0]` | capture | Free-running counter, cleared by run reset; record samples the pre-increment value. |
| `buffer_full` | capture | No new record can be accepted at the current write edge. |
| `event_dropped` | capture | High for each edge rejecting a pending captured record. Consecutive drops keep it high. |
| `overflowed` | capture | Sticky loss flag until run reset. |
| `overflow_count` | capture | Saturating count of rejected records; a lower bound after saturation. |
| `drain_request` | drain | Request the next record; empty requests do not advance the pointer. |
| `drain_valid`, `drain_record[127:0]` | drain | Registered result of the request at this rising edge; consume only when valid. |
| `drain_empty` | drain | No record currently visible to the read domain. |

A source tuple is captured at an edge, then offered to the FIFO at the next capture edge.
It retains the original timestamp even if it later crosses into the drain domain. The write
status and overflow pulse therefore refer to the pending captured record. The source must
supply event codes from `rtl/event_codes_pkg.sv` and the hash-bound domain snapshot. The host
rejects unknown codes, nonzero reserved fields, regressing ticks/cycles and duplicate events.
Arbitrate simultaneous source strobes before this input; this module cannot represent two
events at one capture edge. Clock crossing of asynchronous source strobes is also upstream.

The 128-bit output is `{timebase_ticks[63:0], cycle[31:0], 16'd0, 8'd0, event_code[7:0]}`.
Write its least significant byte first for the published 16-byte little-endian host format.
The record payload is unspecified when `drain_valid` is low, including during reset.

### Shared-counter channels

`rtl/shared_event_witness.sv` gives independent event FIFOs one common 64-bit capture
counter. Each channel supplies its own pre-edge valid bit, eight-bit code and 32-bit
identity. Channel buses are flat: channel `i` occupies bits `i*width +: width`,
with widths 8 for code, 32 for identity, 64 for run counts and 128 for a record.
Simultaneous tuples receive the same pre-increment timestamp, with zero
reserved fields in the existing 128-bit record layout. Codes and identities are supplied
by the caller's declared profile; the instrument does not interpret a neural state or
encode it in reserved bits.

The shared capture reset and counter release together. Each registered tuple enters its
channel FIFO on the next capture edge. `attempt_count` counts those FIFO write attempts;
`accepted_count` counts accepted writes. A full channel drops its newest record and
updates its own sticky flag, drop pulse and saturating overflow count. Other channels
continue independently. Attempt and acceptance counts are 64-bit run counters; the
admitted run must end before their wrap. Capture-domain status needs a coherent snapshot
before crossing to a processor or drain clock domain.

`CHANNEL_COUNT` accepts 1 through 32; `ADDRESS_BITS` and `OVERFLOW_COUNTER_BITS` retain
the FIFO and single-channel witness limits. Every channel has its own drain request,
valid record and empty flag. An unused channel remains empty. Common reset flushes all
channels and clears the shared timebase and counts. Reset release, conservative FIFO
flags, physical CDC constraints and RAM qualification follow the same rules below.

The dedicated simulation exports simultaneous known-edge records, continuously captures
1,000 records plus two markers per channel at 1,024-record capacity before drain, and
exercises isolated full-buffer loss, saturation, an empty channel and queued-data reset.
These are instrument-port controls. Neural wrapper, complete export/report integration
and board qualification have separate acceptance requirements.

## Clock crossing and reset

`event_record_fifo.sv` uses binary pointers with an extra wrap bit, Gray-coded pointers,
two destination-clock synchroniser stages, registered full/empty flags and a dual-clock
128-bit memory. Full compares the next write Gray pointer to the synchronised read pointer
with its top two bits inverted. Empty compares the next read Gray pointer to the synchronised
write pointer. Synchronisation makes flags conservative: newly written data or newly freed
space becomes visible after destination-clock edges, rather than immediately. Synchroniser
registers carry `ASYNC_REG` attributes. This follows FIFO style 1 in Clifford E. Cummings,
[Simulation and Synthesis Techniques for Asynchronous FIFO Design, SNUG 2002](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252160343_Simulation_and_Synthesis_Techniques_for_Asynchronous_FIFO_Design).

Both clocks share `run_reset_n`. Assertion is asynchronous; each `clock_reset_release.sv`
instance waits for two local rising edges before release. A stopped clock remains in reset.
Assertion flushes the run, clears the timebase and loss state and prevents old records from
becoming valid. RAM contents and the invalid read payload are not cleared, preserving memory
inference. Independent reset of one pointer domain is unsupported. Hold the common reset low
for the device's required minimum pulse width and meet reset-recovery/removal constraints.

Capturing and draining need no coherent shared clock. Reading capture-domain status from
processor logic does require a separate coherent CDC snapshot; synchronising each counter
bit separately is insufficient. Gray-bus skew/max-delay constraints, placement of synchroniser
stages and RAM inference must be supplied and reviewed in the vendor integration. RTL simulation
and generic synthesis do not establish metastability rates, timing closure or physical RAM fit.

## Configuration space

One configuration is one combination of:

- controller placement: `linux_user_space`, `bare_metal_amp` or `fabric_logic`;
- load case: idle, CPU stress, memory and cache stress, network stress, storage stress;
- sample rate: from 100 Hz to 20 kHz, 1 kHz by default;
- controller (PID with anti-windup or discrete LQR) with its coefficients, and plant
  (second-order mechanical or first-order thermal) with its fixed-point format;
- fault schedule, empty for timing runs.

## Procedure

1. The board is powered from its own supply only. Room temperature is recorded.
2. The same bitstream serves every placement; the placement changes through a register only.
3. Each repeat starts after a reboot.
4. A fixed warm-up period is discarded; its length is recorded in the run manifest.
5. Each repeat runs 1 000 000 control cycles (about 17 minutes at 1 kHz).
6. Each configuration is repeated five times.
7. Every repeat writes its event file, power file, measurement-domain snapshot and run manifest
   with SHA-256 of each referenced file, the bitstream, firmware, operating-system images and
   controller binary, and the tool versions.
8. A repeat with any event-buffer overflow is invalid and is reported as invalid, not dropped.

The buffered RTL witness produces event files for host-tool verification through its actual
drain stream, including known-period and overflow simulations. Its drop-newest buffer retains
accepted records, latches overflow and counts drops with a saturating 32-bit counter. The count
is a lower bound after saturation, and `overflowed` remains set until common run reset. Record
status before reset: reset flushes both domains and clears all run counters. A processor logger
must implement a coherent capture-domain status snapshot before using it in a manifest; raw CDC
sampling is insufficient. RTL ports and reset timing are specified in
[`FABRIC_WITNESS.md`](FABRIC_WITNESS.md). Those runs declare
`source.kind: rtl_simulation` and remain simulation evidence even when the input series are
internally valid. A board run declares the source, all input and build artefact paths and their
SHA-256 values; the host checks the referenced bytes. The board acceptance flags in the run
manifest are operator declarations, not a replacement for the separate same-bitstream acceptance
records required below.

## Reporting

- Latency and jitter are reported as distributions — median, 95th, 99th and 99.9th percentile and
  maximum — per repeat and pooled, with the spread between repeats.
- Every statistic states its sample count and run duration. No single-run number is presented
  without its distribution.
- Per-run latency jitter means the absolute change in the same periodic event interval
  between adjacent post-warm-up cycles. Both intervals must be complete; missing cycles
  are never bridged. Pair counts, expected pairs and missing-pair coverage accompany the
  distribution, with peak-to-peak latency spread reported separately. Fault and safe-state
  intervals remain latency-only. The exact definition, null/zero semantics and auditable
  pair outputs are specified in [host analysis](HOST_ANALYSIS.md#latency-jitter).
  This derived software metric changes no capture or input-manifest parameter; pooled
  repeats and physical jitter qualification still require their separate campaign evidence.
- Deadline misses are reported as counts and rates from the hardware monitor.
- Control quality is the tracking error of the emulated plant, RMS and peak.
- Energy is reported as mean energy per control cycle over windows of many cycles, per rail and
  for the four rails together.
- Fault runs report detection latency and time to safe state per injected fault.
- The instrument floor from the bus-offset calibration is reported with every latency table.
- The host report retains the observation duration in timebase ticks and the contributing sample
  count for each metric. Missing tracking or power input is reported as unavailable, not filled
  with a simulation substitute.

## Native simulation observations

The native capture path binds the executed source snapshot, configuration, executable, original
event stream, raw tracking and completion metadata to the run manifest. It declares
`source.kind: rtl_simulation`; its reports remain `simulation_only`, with physical acceptance
flags false and no power series. These captures verify software and RTL behaviour; they do not
satisfy the board procedure or instrument acceptance below.
The frozen source includes the production Makefile and its included Spike plugin make fragment,
even when the selected target builds only the native simulator.
The run also binds `producer_context.json` and the actual parent project package,
packaged contracts and loaded tools. The context records source origins and hashes,
interpreter, platform and dependency versions. Source or context drift during
capture refuses producer acceptance while retaining the original native artifacts.

`tracking_sampling: observed` permits only the cycles actually read by the controller. Their
tracking rows must match the captured `SAMPLE_READ` cycles exactly. After warm-up exclusion,
the report states the expected cycle count, observed sample count, missing cycles and coverage
fraction. RMS and peak describe observed samples only. Incomplete coverage is `partial` and
invalidates the run; zero post-warm-up observations are `unavailable`. Neither missing samples
nor their errors are interpolated. Omitting this option or selecting `complete` retains the
complete-series contract in [`HOST_ANALYSIS.md`](HOST_ANALYSIS.md).

Optional hash-bound `native_metadata` preserves the final live miss, overflow, sample and record
counts and safe-state status. Its fault kind, cycle and delay duration must agree with
the declared schedule even when the metadata and manifest hashes are updated together.
Without FIFO loss, those counts must agree with the complete
captured event stream. With loss, the report retains live counts separately: missing actuator
records cannot establish controller deadline misses, and the completion receipt cannot repair
lost events or make the run valid. Finalisation waits for the configured final deadline,
capture quiescence and receiver drain, including events after safe state first latches.

Dedicated-hart ISA capture uses a separate hash-bound `amp_capture` receipt, reconciled with
original firmware inputs, original pre-generation/pre-compilation plugin inputs and captured
native plugin build/source snapshot, raw observations
and actual logger completion. It declares
`bare_metal_amp` with `rtl_simulation`; neither parked companion harts nor the functional clock
map qualifies Linux coexistence or physical U54 latency. See [the AMP capture contract](AMP_SIMULATION.md).

Optional hash-bound `host_load` identifies the idle, CPU, memory/cache, private loopback UDP or
owned-file storage/fsync profile. Its worker interval must enclose the actual native interval;
policy readback and complete operation counters describe the whole worker interval. Host
monotonic time is separate from fabric event time. CPU affinity does not reserve a core,
loopback traffic does not establish NIC load, and fsync does not establish uncached storage
load. These receipts do not qualify board processor timing or energy.

The Linux PAC1934 journal retains raw accumulator attributes, units and individual host/fabric
read brackets. It is not a qualified `power.csv`: physical acquisition, rail calibration and
energy-window alignment remain unverified. The journal cannot substitute for the power series
required by the board procedure. Formats and validation are in
[`HOST_ANALYSIS.md`](HOST_ANALYSIS.md); register snapshots, reset custody and final drain are in
[`PLANT_WITNESS.md`](PLANT_WITNESS.md).

## Stated limits

These limits are part of every report:

- The PAC1934 rails do not separate processor cores from fabric: the core rail supplies both.
  Placement energy is whole-rail energy, not per-core energy.
- The power monitor samples far more slowly than a control cycle. Energy per cycle is a window
  mean, not a per-cycle measurement.
- Timestamps resolve 10 ns. Bus access inside the interconnect adds a fixed offset that is
  calibrated and reported.
- The plant is emulated. Results describe controller timing and its effect on the emulated plant,
  not a physical machine.
- A PREEMPT_RT comparison is included only if a matching kernel builds for the board support
  package.

## Acceptance of the instrument before any result

A result may be reported only after the instrument has passed, on the same bitstream, the
known-period test, the injected-delay test, the overflow test and the bus-offset calibration
described in [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md). Their records are kept with the run records.

[`PLANT_WITNESS.md`](PLANT_WITNESS.md) specifies the implemented Q8.24 models, reference
quantisation, strict deadline and safe-state priority, simultaneous event capture and fault
injection. `ACT_WRITE` denotes the first timely command; `ACT_LATE` is the first accepted
late command in its observation cycle and does not satisfy a deadline. Late-command counts

flags with sample output and include all coefficient values in source/configuration provenance.
The injected-delay simulation checks an exact k-period fabric delay; processor execution,
power-monitor energy and physical safe-state behaviour need separate board acceptance.

| `diff` | `left_json`, `right_json`, keyword `limits`, optional ordered `left_envelopes` and `right_envelopes` | `Difference` with content identities, changed pointers and receipt identities. |
| `seal` | `content_json`, keywords `schema_id`, `registry`, `resolver`, `limits`, optional `signing`, `signer`, `trust` | `SealResult` with canonical content, its reference and an optional detached envelope. |
| `verify` | `content_json`, keywords `schema_id`, `envelopes`, `registry`, `resolver`, `limits`, `policy`, `trust` | Complete fifteen-field `VerificationReport`. |

All six limit fields are explicit positive integers: `max_json_bytes`, `max_blob_bytes`, `max_total_reference_bytes`, `max_reference_count`, `max_graph_depth` and `max_json_depth`. `Limits.validate()` checks the declaration; operations independently check it before acquisition. Construction supplies no defaults or unlimited mode.

Native parser or canonical writer recursion exhaustion raises `InputRefused` with
`Reason.code="limit_exceeded"`, even when `max_json_depth` permits the document's
container depth.

`BlobRef` retains `digest`, decimal-string `byte_length`, `media_type`, `digest_basis` and optional `schema_id`. Its constructor retains the supplied declaration. `BlobRef.from_mapping()` and `to_mapping()` validate the complete wire shape; the returned mapping is detached and read-only. Neither method retrieves bytes or establishes their identity. The wire representation omits an absent `schema_id`; an explicitly received null is invalid.

`reference_bytes` requires `digest_basis="raw_bytes"` or `"jcs_content"`. Raw identity binds the original bytes; canonical identity binds the complete strict canonical document. The helper does not rewrite or store the input. A declared schema ID does not register that schema.

## Sources and authority

The caller selects a complete `SchemaRegistry`, including its snapshot reference and all fourteen fields of every `RegistryEntry`. Static schema bytes, dependencies, reference paths and common semantics are independently checked. An artifact cannot choose a Python implementation or network schema resolver.

The caller's `Resolver` implements both methods:

```python
resolve(reference: BlobRef, *, max_bytes: int) -> bytes
resolve_digest(digest: str, *, max_bytes: int) -> bytes
```

Each read returns actual bounded bytes. A missing target raises `ReferenceUnavailable` with the exact original argument in `.reference`. A digest-only lookup retains the original digest string; it does not fabricate a missing length or schema declaration. Operations check returned identities and share cumulative reference budgets across the whole selected graph.

An uncached full-reference read receives the smaller of `max_blob_bytes` and the
remaining cumulative allowance. An exhausted allowance refuses before calling
the resolver. Cached bytes retain their metadata checks and require no new read.

`TrustContext` selects an independently accepted bootstrap policy, current snapshot, accepted sequence floor, evaluation mode and time, explicit control envelopes, and an optional archived snapshot. Historical mode requires the selected archive and retains current floor and revocation checks. Verification does not install a snapshot, advance a floor, issue a certificate or derive trusted time from a producer timestamp.

`VerificationPolicy` supplies the policy reference, exact required claim and purpose populations, and any declared reference requirements. The referenced policy and caller selections must agree. Selecting a narrower claim population preserves the full content and reference observations; it does not rewrite the inventory or supply a domain verdict.

Unsigned `seal` uses `signing=None`, `signer=None` and `trust=None`. Signed construction requires all three together and current authority. The actual caller-owned `Signer` exposes raw public-key bytes and `sign(message: bytes) -> bytes`. The signature covers the complete context-specific message and is checked before an envelope is returned. A signer failure does not trigger unsigned construction. Initial root issuance and adapter qualification are outside these functions.

## UTC values

`Utc(raw)` validates an original string using the Gregorian calendar, the selected leap-second history and the complete fractional token. It is an immutable string subtype. It preserves the original spelling, including the distinction between `T` and `t`, and uses ordinary string equality for wire identity.

`value.compare(other)` accepts `Utc` or a string, revalidates both operands and returns `-1`, `0` or `1` by exact instant order. It does not round through a floating-point epoch. Malformed scalar input raises `InputRefused` with the original located reason.

The caller's independently qualified `Clock.now()` supplies the time token. `Utc(clock.now())` validates that token; it does not qualify the clock's source, controller, capture, freshness or uncertainty. The existing clock precondition remains with its owner. Required unavailable clock qualification retains the policy refusal in the complete verification report.

## Reports and failures

`VerificationReport` retains all fifteen fields: `content_ref`, `policy_ref`, `registry_ref`, `evaluation_mode`, `evaluation_time`, `evaluated_claim_ids`, `structure`, `integrity`, `authenticity`, `availability`, `common_eligibility`, `domain_verdict`, `current_eligibility`, `reference_observations` and `reasons`.

Common eligibility reports the applicable common gates. `domain_verdict` remains `not_evaluated`; the separately owned domain consumer supplies scientific acceptance. Historical common eligibility does not establish current eligibility. Inspection and difference results do not authenticate receipts or accept evidence.

Thrown `EmtError` subclasses carry one complete `.reason`: `InputRefused`, `ConfigurationError`, `ReferenceUnavailable`, `SignerUnavailable` or `StorageError`. A `Reason` has `code`, `subject_digest`, `claim_id`, `pointer` and fixed `detail`. Unknown identities retain their null values. Returned verification refusals remain complete reports rather than being replaced with a successful Boolean.

After an eligible signing adapter is called, response failure uses the fixed
`SignerUnavailable` reason and known content digest. Other typed operation errors
retain their classification. Internal verifier errors are separate from adapter
response failures.

The source checkout runs the commands through `python -m evidence_manifest_toolkit` from the `src/` directory, using explicit absolute input and output paths. Installed `emt` packaging remains under development. The grammar below uses the executable's design name.

```text
emt seal --content FILE --schema-id ID --registry FILE --objects DIR --limits FILE --output NEW_DIR [--signing-request FILE --signer-config FILE --trust FILE]
emt verify --content FILE --schema-id ID --registry FILE --objects DIR --limits FILE --policy FILE --trust FILE --report NEW_FILE [--signature FILE]...
emt inspect --content FILE --limits FILE --report NEW_FILE
emt diff --left FILE --right FILE --limits FILE --report NEW_FILE [--left-signature FILE]... [--right-signature FILE]...
```

Every configuration is an explicit closed local JSON value. `--limits` supplies all six positive integer bounds described in the [Python API](api.md). Its initial read is bounded by the size measured on the same opened regular-file handle. Once decoded, its bounds control subsequent inputs. A small `max_json_bytes` does not impose that future bound on the limits file itself.

Native parser or canonical writer recursion exhaustion produces `limit_exceeded`
and exit `2` before successful output publication, including when the configured
`max_json_depth` permits the document's container depth.

Registry, policy and trust files encode the complete corresponding public value types. Bytes in configurations use canonical unpadded Base64URL. Decimal lengths, digests and UTC strings retain their original spelling. Repeated detached-signature flags preserve caller order; the command does not discover signatures in the object store.

Signed `seal` requires all three signing flags together. `SignerConfig` contains only `adapter_ref`, `signer_key_id`, `public_key` and `profile_id`. The reference names an owner-controlled, locally enrolled signing adapter. The current checkout supplies no qualified CLI adapter; selecting an unavailable adapter refuses signing. No private key or executable is loaded from these configuration fields, and a failed signed request does not become an unsigned result.

Trusted installation code holds the read-only association between an exact descriptor and an already existing signer. Caller configuration must match that descriptor; it cannot enroll or replace the object. A mismatch is a located configuration failure. An empty installation produces `signer_unavailable` with null subject, claim and pointer before signing or publication. Once an eligible signer is invoked, a failed response retains the known content digest in the original signer-response refusal.

A missing local verification provider produces `configuration_error` and exit `4`
before authentication, with null subject, claim and pointer. It creates no requested
report. Restoring the provider permits evaluation of the complete original input;
the command retains every verification gate and requires a fresh report destination.

## Read-only object store

`--objects` selects an existing directory. A digest `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` maps to the immediate file `<objects>/<64 lowercase hex>`. The store adds no extension, basis suffix or index. Captured bytes must satisfy every applicable declaration, including declarations sharing a digest under different bases.

The resolver anchors the directory descriptor and refuses symlinks and nonregular targets. It reads within the original per-object and remaining cumulative allowance. Input and store files remain unchanged. Artifact URLs and labels are not filesystem paths or network lookup instructions.

## Complete output publication

Unsigned `seal` creates a fresh directory containing exactly `content.json` and `refs.json`. Content is the bare canonical library result. The unregistered reference index contains exactly `content_ref`. Signed transport additionally carries the detached envelope and its reference when an eligible adapter supplies a verified signature.

Seal stdout preserves all three `SealResult` field names. `canonical_content` is represented by `{content_ref, output_file}`, where `output_file` is the selected directory joined with `content.json`. The root `content_ref` is that same complete reference. `envelope_json` is null for unsigned construction, or unpadded Base64URL of the exact detached-envelope file bytes for signed transport.

`verify`, `inspect` and `diff` exclusively create the selected report file. Stdout and that file contain the same complete report bytes. All transport JSON is strict UTF-8 RFC 8785 JCS without a BOM, padding or trailing newline. Serialization adds no accepted flag or registered evidence schema.

Output parents must already exist. The current directory publisher uses Linux `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` with an anchored parent, sibling staging, actual absent/occupied capability checks and complete file/directory synchronization. It never substitutes a check followed by an overwriting rename. Existing files, directories and symlinks are preserved. Support on other hosts and filesystems requires equivalent native validation.

Before publication, failures remove only the transaction's unchanged owned staging entries. After publication, a stdout or durability failure leaves the complete immutable output and returns an I/O failure. A retry uses a distinct fresh destination; the command does not delete or overwrite the previous result.

## Exits

| Exit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Construction or diagnostic transport completed, or verification's requested common mode is eligible. |
| `2` | Input or verification gate refused without a higher-priority failure. |
| `3` | Required reference or signer unavailable, or actual storage, cleanup, stdout or durability failure. |
| `4` | Invalid invocation/configuration or unsupported implementation capability. |

Observed failures use precedence `4 > 3 > 2 > 0`. A report's successful publication clears no gate. Common or historical exit `0` does not establish scientific or current acceptance; read the complete report.

Thrown failures produce stdout `{"operation": ..., "reasons": [...]}` with the full located reasons and no success field. They create no requested successful report or seal destination. A well-formed returned refusal report can be published in full. Malformed invocations name a recognized command when available and otherwise use `operation="emt"`. Caller diagnostics use fixed authored details rather than interpreter messages or local paths.

def verify(
    content_json: bytes,
    *,
    schema_id: str,
    envelopes: tuple[bytes, ...],
    registry: SchemaRegistry,
    resolver: Resolver,
    limits: Limits,
    policy: VerificationPolicy,
    trust: TrustContext,
) -> VerificationReport:
    """Evaluate whole common content, required closure and independently selected authority.

    Parameters
    ----------
    content_json : bytes
        Entire original strict JSON source; no claim projection or byte identity is invented.
    schema_id : str
        Explicit independently selected content schema, not an artifact code selector.
    envelopes : tuple of bytes
        All actual explicitly supplied detached receipts in original order.
    registry : SchemaRegistry
        Complete independently selected raw schema catalogue, selectors and native roles.
    resolver : Resolver
        Actual bounded offline source; no URL, executable or hidden receipt discovery.
    limits : Limits
        All six original positive bounds shared by every source and control acquisition.
    policy : VerificationPolicy
        Whole independently selected policy and complete exact claim/purpose/selector scope.
    trust : TrustContext
        Independent accepted bootstrap/current/floor/time and optional selected archive.
        Prior owner or fixture approval is an explicit trusted-caller premise, not a parsed bit.

    Returns
    -------
    VerificationReport
        All fifteen original fields with separate common/domain/current results, complete
        observations and actual reasons. No snapshot, floor, key or source record is changed.

    Raises
    ------
    ConfigurationError
        Caller/local policy/registry or the maintained local verifier cannot be configured.
    InputRefused
        Strict source, native envelope or an explicit operation bound is violated.
    ReferenceUnavailable
        Required bootstrap/current/archive source cannot be acquired, retaining its exact

original full reference. Missing selected graph/control links remain report observations.
    """
    inputs = acquire_verification_inputs(
        content_json,
        schema_id=schema_id,
        envelopes=envelopes,
        registry=registry,
        resolver=resolver,
        limits=limits,
        policy=policy,
        trust=trust,
    )
    state = select_trust_state(
        trust,
        registry=registry,
        schemas=inputs.schemas,
        resolver=resolver,
        budget=inputs.budget,
        verifier=inputs.verifier,
    )
    actual_claims = tuple(claim.claim_id for claim in inputs.content.content_claim_obligations)
    receipts = tuple(
        receipt_authority(
            envelope,
            content_reference=inputs.content.content_ref,
            actual_claim_ids=actual_claims,
            state=state,
            trust=trust,
            policy=inputs.policy_declaration,
            resolver=resolver,
            budget=inputs.budget,
            verifier=inputs.verifier,
        )
        for envelope in inputs.envelopes
    )
    return compose_verification_report(
        inputs,
        state=state,
        receipts=receipts,
        policy=policy,
        trust=trust,
        registry=registry,
    )

## Interpretation

QCEC's probabilistic and phase-dependent outcomes retain their original
vocabulary. PyZX returning `False` means an unsuccessful reduction. Layout
checks establish structural mapping facts; additional ancilla and measurement
semantics remain explicit requirements. Matching replay bytes establish that
comparison under its observed settings.

The affected PyZX QASM2 parser route can lose global phase, including with
`up_to_global_phase=False`. That route cannot establish `unitary_exact`.
The MQT QPY route carries finite global phase in explicit derived scalar gates.
Its derived native operations retain original finite parameter bits through
public typed fields, avoiding constructor simplification and overflow.
The observed native checker ignores its IR global-phase field on this route.
Original QPY bytes stay unchanged, and shared gate validation with the PyZX
converter remains a correlated dependency of both observations.
The controller's caller-side preparation and validation have retrospective
elapsed checks; hard whole-caller memory and lifetime containment remain
unqualified.

The library operates offline. It does not submit circuits to a QPU.

Conversion admits thirty-two explicit standard SDK gate families. Unsupported
classes, changed definitions, control states, nonunitary instructions and
unbound parameters refuse. Finite binary64 radian values retain their exact
rational coefficient with an explicit continuous symbol for `1/pi`.
The separate numerical graph supports consistency observations; it supplies no
equivalence verdict.

## Controller custody retention

`transpile_witness.execution.controller_storage.retain_controller_custody`
retains every original file from a completed controlled-engine observation in a
separate immutable object store. It returns the actual raw parent-measurement
reference and sorted file inventory. Links, missing required files, source/output
overlap and exceeded acquisition bounds refuse before storage. Original controller
files stay unchanged. Retention grants no engine, native, Clock or current verdict.

Controlled typed engine observations also preserve their full original controller
record in `result.controller`, including PID and interval for custody retention.
The typed wrapper keeps its distinct entry/end interval. Archiving checks the
selected engine against the original request before writing output.

The original controller record now includes its observed process group and the
complete per-child kernel resource result. Immutable custody preserves CPU float
bits and every original integer counter. Native precision and containment
qualification remain separate requirements.

A source-bound CPU reader recovers only uniquely encoded integer microseconds
from retained kernel values, then expresses their sum in nanoseconds. The full
original encoding definition is required under the caller's same source budget.
This supplies numeric consistency without admitting clock accuracy or profiles.

The controller duration constructor binds these counters to complete original
invocation, start, end and Clock records before retaining all twelve duration
fields. Missing sources or changed original acquisition bounds refuse before
output storage. Successful construction with genuine full Clock inputs and native
qualification remain unverified.

`VerificationContext` now retains the complete twenty-seven-field caller layout
with immutable typed nested declarations. Its request method uses the genuine
Common stage and preserves the original shared acquisition budget. Root `verify`
and the complete evaluator flow remain under development.

The context's execution-source preparation continues genuine Common/request work
into full binding inventory and release-source custody under the same read budget.
It preserves original unqualified states and dispatches no received code.

The controller process-record constructor now prepares complete audit and run
receipt records from the original parent sources before either is stored. Actual
failed-process measurements cannot be promoted to completed audit state. Full
qualified process/Clock construction remains unverified.


The supervised raw-engine constructor now prepares the full original record from
the actual typed capture and whole selected request/profile/pair sources. It keeps
native availability, both timing scopes, original streams and declared UTC/context
limitations. Complete successful construction with genuine selected sources and
qualification remain unverified. Custody preserves previously acquired original
media metadata when the same programme bytes occur in the capture tree.


Pair rendering checks its full recorded evaluation-source correspondence and keeps
requested policy scope distinct from an actually evaluated refused singleton.
Common and native current eligibility remain separate recorded values. Existing
whole verification read budgets continue through rendering without restarting.
Full successful qualified rendering remains unverified.


Recorded case coverage is checked against the complete original case ledger and
inventory. Unavailable and unattempted cases retain their distinct states, while
counts and actually evaluated IDs must correspond. This source check does not
qualify case execution or replace the remaining full evaluator/runtime gates.


Caller runner bindings retain explicit workspace and complete process controls for
each exact purpose/domain selection. Their fixed engine adapters preserve actual
process custody; missing selections refuse before capture. Full evaluator and
qualified native execution remain unfinished.


Verification callers can prepare one actual Common/source session before bounded
engine candidates. Request-selected profiles, original pair inputs, conversion
ancestry and explicit process limits are checked before fixed adapter dispatch.
The complete qualified evaluator and native verification result remain unfinished.

Engine replay preparation checks the full original profile/core/qualification
source chain and complete case/process custody before fixed dispatch. Missing
assessment evidence or unsupported passed promotion refuses; source consistency
still requires separate runtime and scientific qualification for native acceptance.


Complete engine configurations can be constructed and matched from actual public
SDK settings. QCEC keeps all thirty getters, including differences from its JSON
display; PyZX retains both flags and its selected parser. Numeric sources have an
explicit whole encoding definition and preserve original bits. These source
operations do not execute circuits or establish qualified native verification.


Actual QCEC workers retain all thirty typed configuration getters before parsing
and after the real checker call in the original bounded diagnostic stream. QASM
and QPY observations keep their complete programme and mapped dependency hashes.
Successful capture requires both stages; raw construction also matches them to
the selected complete configuration. A parse failure retains its genuine
before-only observation. These source joins do not grant runtime, profile,
physical Clock or scientific qualification.

A prepared EvaluationExecution can retain an engine replay directly from its
actual supervised capture. Run, request and source identities come from the
prepared session; applied configuration comes from original controller custody.
The result is a raw source record. Complete evaluator, parent process, physical
Clock and native eligibility checks remain required.

Whole replay preflight preserves original pair-policy bindings, profile order and
unique pair/engine identities. The prepared evaluation shares one original
monotonic interval across its four controlled replay routes. Expiry prevents a
later replay from restarting that budget; native and controller limits remain
unchanged. These timing samples do not establish qualified physical Clock or
complete evaluator containment.

An explicit MemoryPolicy on RunnerSelection also enables an owned cgroupv2
charged-memory subtree for the four controlled adapters. It requires an existing
caller-selected delegation and preserves original kernel counters, membership
and cleanup journals in full raw custody. Per-process AS and native/controller
limits remain separate. Complete evaluator accounting and qualification remain
required.

`engine_capture_plan.capture_engine_plan` preflights every immutable candidate
request before its first dispatch, then retains actual observations in order.
An operational error or timeout preserves that capture and leaves the remaining
suffix unattempted. `EvaluationExecution.observe_engine_replays` first checks
the complete original native plan and source/qualification bindings, then uses
this path with the same earlier interval. Native negative and unknown values
remain observations for the owning scientific policy evaluator. Full evaluator
parent, scientific decisions, report construction and qualification remain open.

Execution preparation now compares the full original C0 claim content with its
native pair or batch certificate after actual Common succeeds and before later
binding sources are read. Same claim IDs cannot hide changed statements, scope,
source order or limitations. The public `bound_subject.read_bound_subject`
source reader preserves the whole native certificate and shared acquisition;
it supplies no authenticity, scientific or current-eligibility verdict.

The supervised raw producer now accepts the original `witness_request.v4` for
first engine observations as well as `evaluation_request.v4` for later replay.
First observations bind the whole prior pair, selected profiles, semantics,
policy, resource bounds and actual conversion ancestry. They need no future
certificate or Common report. QCEC/PyZX QASM/QPY paths retain their native values
and genuine failure custody; complete witness orchestration and qualification
remain required.

## Boundary

TRANSPILE-WITNESS is an offline source library in its own assigned repository
scope. It owns its circuit input interpretation, converter and engine
observations, compiler provenance, layout and replay observations, and domain
verification requirements. It preserves original programme and result custody.

The common evidence runtime owns common references, canonicalisation,
reference closure, registry, sealing, signature purpose and trust. A domain
certificate must use the actual common interfaces and exact native subject;
a project-local replacement signer, resolver or manifest cannot stand in for
that runtime.

The owning consumer receives complete subject, policy, claims, source and
member identities. It must preserve negative, failed and unavailable results
and the distinction between historical common success and current domain
eligibility. Presentation does not recompute or upgrade an engine observation.

## Consequences

The source library performs no QPU submission or provider job management.
Qiskit, MQT QCEC and PyZX remain genuine external suppliers with their own
licences and source provenance. Their installed versions, numerical domain and
integration need qualification for each claimed profile.

The five certificate operations and complete common/consumer integration are
under development. Existing observations supply no positive certificate,
registered engine profile or current trust claim. Local source, publication
and release remain distinct states. See
[the actual execution architecture](../ARCHITECTURE.md) and
[validation](../../VALIDATION.md).

The caller supplies circuit programmes, dependencies, compiler output, engine
settings, resource policy and an owned workspace. Those data can be malformed,
misleading or costly to parse. The caller, operating system, Python runtime,
owned source and installed supplier code form the execution base. A separate
process or a matching digest does not establish their authenticity.

The assets are original programme bytes and declarations, private circuit data,
captured supplier results, compiler observations, the caller's files and the
host's available resources. An input author can try to alter include resolution,
substitute an artifact or result, hide changed semantics behind metadata,
overwrite runtime code, or exhaust time, memory, streams and storage.

## Boundaries and controls

| Input or boundary | Current control | Limit of that control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Engine and compiler selection | Fixed owned `WorkerKind` and `CompilerCase` values select source modules; the process command has no shell interpreter | Installed source and executable integrity still depend on their custody |
| Original programmes and dependencies | Linux sealed memory descriptors are mounted read-only at exact virtual filenames | Original bytes can still exercise defects in the SDK or native parser |
| Include and cost-profile resolution | Complete declared dependency bytes, normalised POSIX names, collision and cycle checks, lexical include inventory and explicit supplier built-ins | Lexical resolution records declarations; it does not prove each native file read |
| Runtime overlays | Data cannot replace protected runtime roots, device paths or fixed worker modules | The selected runtime roots are available to the worker; they must be appropriate for that execution |
| Supplier process environment | Bubblewrap separates PID and network namespaces, clears the inherited environment and mounts runtime roots read-only | Namespace containment is dependent on the host kernel and Bubblewrap, and is not an admitted platform profile |
| Native preparation and execution | Six explicit engine limits bound time, represented qubits, static operations, original input occurrences, captured output and per-process address space; startup memory is separate | Address space is not whole-job resident memory; caller-side allocation remains outside this cap |
| Controller and export | Separate controller limits cover its address space, namespace data, lifetime, request size, export bytes and file count | Caller preparation and validation use elapsed checks, without qualified hard whole-caller lifetime or memory containment |
| Returned archive | Every member is checked before extraction; only unique regular relative files are admitted, with no traversal or conflicting paths and with finite count and byte quotas | Imported artifacts are local custody; this does not authenticate a remote producer |
| Result decoding | Bounded unique-key JSON, original input/dependency/configuration joins, prior and terminal consumption records, and agreement with the typed native result | Agreement among these records does not prove the supplier's mathematics or an independent conversion |
| Worker cancellation | The owned process session is killed when still live and reaped, with a second cleanup guard | Arbitrary repeated asynchronous interruption and creation before process assignment remain unqualified |

The controlled QASM and QPY observation adapters use the controller route.
Direct converter functions and SDK metadata readers run in the calling process;
they do not acquire containment through their module names. QPY inventory checks
occur after the genuine SDK loader has parsed the bytes. Run these direct APIs
within an appropriately controlled caller when inputs are untrusted.

The fixed compiler observation uses sealed input and an owned worker deadline.
It currently captures compiler streams directly to files and uses the legacy
namespace without the controller's finite storage and exchange quotas. Its
deadline and process separation do not establish complete resource admission.
See the [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the two routes.

## Result integrity and semantic attacks

Gate names, matching layouts or equal global-phase metadata can accompany
different operators. Conversion checks supported standard classes, definitions,
controls, operand order and finite parameters. Unsupported scope refuses.
Complete SDK maps distinguish original logical wires from added physical wires;
ancillary and garbage flags describe native roles rather than proving initial
states, disposal or isometry.

The MQT and PyZX converters share gate validation. Running their suppliers in
different processes does not remove this correlated dependency. QCEC's
phase-weaker and probabilistic outcomes retain their native meanings; PyZX's
unsuccessful reduction is not a definite difference. Numerical observations
retain their precision limits and unresolved discrepancies. None of these
observations alone establishes scientific equivalence.

Exact byte replay compares retained output files. Repeated SDK QPY dumps can
differ while observed circuit and layout state agrees. Byte differences must
remain visible; replacing them with normalised files would change the claimed
observation. A native schema resource's pinned digest checks the resource
bytes, not reference traversal, trust, signing, current verification or
certificate eligibility. Common evidence and domain admission are separate
requirements.

## Data custody and disclosure

Capture directories contain complete original circuit bytes, dependencies,
settings and raw supplier diagnostics. Retain them in a caller-controlled
workspace with appropriate access permissions. The capture APIs do not encrypt
these artifacts or select their retention period. Read-only mounts do not
prevent readable runtime material from appearing in diagnostics, so inspect
the chosen runtime roots and retained data before sharing a capture.

The library does not submit circuits to a QPU. It does not provide provider
credential management, a hosted account boundary or hardware-result admission.
Windows execution, hard whole-caller confinement, complete supplier integrity
and certificate operations require their own actual qualification.

Report a suspected boundary failure through the
[private security route](../SECURITY.md). The [validation record](../VALIDATION.md)
describes exercised source contracts and remaining qualification; this model
does not substitute for their runtime evidence.

class ReplayBytes:
    """Describe exact observed bytes independently of replay scope qualification.

    Attributes
    ----------
    status : str
        Equal bytes, different bytes, or unavailable output on either side.
    original_length : int or None
        Actual original output length, absent only if the output is unavailable.
    replay_length : int or None
        Actual repeated output length, absent only if unavailable.
    first_difference : int or None
        Zero-based differing byte or the end of the shorter matching prefix.

    Equal bytes alone do not admit source/configuration/seed/target/environment/
    resource/serialization scope or a compiler-wide determinism claim.

    """

    status: Literal["equal", "different", "unavailable"]
    original_length: int | None
    replay_length: int | None
    first_difference: int | None

class MappingAssessment:
    """Report structural mapping facts separately from domain qualification.

    Attributes
    ----------
    status : str
        Valid total injection, invalid supplied map, or unavailable map.
    complete : bool or None
        Exactly one supplied entry per declared source slot.
    in_range : bool or None
        Every supplied index is a plain integer in the target index space.
    injective : bool or None
        No supplied source slots share a target slot.
    surjective : bool or None
        All target slots occur, independently of source completeness/injectivity.
    reason : str
        Local observation description, not a native acceptance/reason code.

    A valid injection can have unequal widths. It does not qualify an isometry,
    ancilla state, measurement order, phase, or unitary equivalence.

    """

    status: Literal["valid", "invalid", "unavailable"]
    complete: bool | None
    in_range: bool | None
    injective: bool | None
    surjective: bool | None
    reason: str

def assess_mapping(
    mapping: tuple[int, ...] | None, *, source_width: int, target_width: int
) -> MappingAssessment:
    """Assess the complete supplied map without coercion or inferred entries.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mapping : tuple[int, ...] or None
        Exact ordered target indices; None means the mapping is unavailable.
    source_width : int
        Positive declared count of source slots, including explicit ancillas.
    target_width : int
        Positive declared target-space width.

    Returns
    -------
    MappingAssessment
        Independent structural facts with explicit unknowns when not assessable.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If counts are not positive plain integers or the container is not a tuple.

    """
    if (
        type(source_width) is not int
        or type(target_width) is not int
        or source_width <= 0
        or target_width <= 0
    ):
        raise ValueError("Layout widths must be positive plain integers.")
    if mapping is None:
        return MappingAssessment(
            "unavailable", None, None, None, None, "No mapping was supplied."
        )
    if type(mapping) is not tuple:
        raise ValueError("A supplied layout map must be an immutable tuple.")
    complete = len(mapping) == source_width
    if any(type(index) is not int for index in mapping):
        return MappingAssessment(
            "invalid", complete, None, None, None, "Indices must be plain integers."
        )
    in_range = all(0 <= index < target_width for index in mapping)
    distinct = len(set(mapping))
    injective = distinct == len(mapping)
    surjective = in_range and distinct == target_width
    valid = complete and in_range and injective
    return MappingAssessment(
        "valid" if valid else "invalid",
        complete,
        in_range,
        injective,
        surjective,
        "Complete injective mapping." if valid else "Supplied mapping is invalid.",
    )

def routing_permutation(
    initial: tuple[int, ...] | None,
    final: tuple[int, ...] | None,
    *,
    width: int,
) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    """Derive physical routing from two explicit bijective index maps.

    Parameters
    ----------
    initial : tuple[int, ...] or None
        Original declared slot to initial physical slot mapping.
    final : tuple[int, ...] or None
        Same declared slot to final physical slot mapping, in the same order.
    width : int
        Full source/target width, including every explicitly declared ancilla.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[int, ...]
        Initial physical slot to final physical slot permutation.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If either map is missing, incomplete, nonbijective or differently scoped.

    """
    if initial is None or final is None:
        raise ValueError("An unavailable mapping cannot become identity routing.")
    left = assess_mapping(initial, source_width=width, target_width=width)
    right = assess_mapping(final, source_width=width, target_width=width)
    if left.status != "valid" or right.status != "valid":
        raise ValueError("Routing requires both complete explicit bijections.")
    source_position = {physical: slot for slot, physical in enumerate(initial)}
    return tuple(final[source_position[physical]] for physical in range(width))

from evidence_manifest_toolkit import BlobRef

from transpile_witness._audit_custody import _record
from transpile_witness._value_wire import array, blob, closed
from transpile_witness.engine_replay import EngineReplaySelection
from transpile_witness.execution._raw_engine_read import _read_raw_engine_source
from transpile_witness.execution.raw_engine import RAW_ENGINE_SCHEMA
from transpile_witness.input_wire import _availability_wire
from transpile_witness.inputs import (
    AvailableReference,
    ReferenceAvailability,
    UnavailableReference,
)
from transpile_witness.value_fields import reference, text
from transpile_witness.verification_reads import VerificationReads

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class EngineReplayRecord:
    """Retain exactly the original six native replay-row fields.

    Attributes
    ----------
    pair_id, engine_id : str
        Original pair and fixed engine identity; never an executable selector.
    original_observation_ref, replay_observation_ref : ReferenceAvailability
        Whole available or unavailable facts, preserving source and assurance.
    state : ReplayState
        Actual match/divergence/unavailability or a dispatch left unattempted.
    reason : str
        Nonempty original explanation, without a fabricated qualification.

    Notes
    -----
    A matching negative result is still negative. This immutable row is source
    comparison, not a native gate, scientific profile, Clock or current approval.

    """

    pair_id: str
    engine_id: EngineId
    original_observation_ref: ReferenceAvailability
    replay_observation_ref: ReferenceAvailability
    state: ReplayState
    reason: str

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Keep complete original row types and raw-source availability branches."""
        text(self.pair_id)
        text(self.reason)
        if self.engine_id not in ("qcec", "pyzx") or self.state not in (
            "matches",
            "diverged",
            "unavailable",
            "not_evaluated",
        ):
            raise ValueError("Engine replay row has an unsupported original identity.")
        for fact in (self.original_observation_ref, self.replay_observation_ref):
            if type(fact) is AvailableReference:
                AvailableReference.__post_init__(fact)
                reference(fact.value, schema=RAW_ENGINE_SCHEMA)
            elif type(fact) is UnavailableReference:
                UnavailableReference.__post_init__(fact)
            else:
                raise ValueError("Engine replay row loses its complete availability.")
        if self.state in ("matches", "diverged") and (
            type(self.original_observation_ref) is not AvailableReference
            or type(self.replay_observation_ref) is not AvailableReference
        ):
            raise ValueError("Engine replay comparison lacks original observations.")
        if (
            self.state == "not_evaluated"
            and type(self.replay_observation_ref) is not UnavailableReference
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "Unattempted engine replay cannot claim a captured result."
            )

    def to_mapping(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Return all six original fields as a detached complete native row.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, object]
            Exact original row vocabulary with both complete availability facts.

        """
        EngineReplayRecord.__post_init__(self)
        return {
            "pair_id": self.pair_id,
            "engine_id": self.engine_id,
            "original_observation_ref": _availability_wire(
                self.original_observation_ref
            ),
            "replay_observation_ref": _availability_wire(self.replay_observation_ref),
            "state": self.state,
            "reason": self.reason,
        }

def compare_engine_replay(
    original: AvailableReference,
    replay_ref: BlobRef,
    *,
    selection: EngineReplaySelection,
    request_ref: BlobRef,
    reads: VerificationReads,
) -> EngineReplayRecord:
    """Compare complete first-observation and actual independent replay sources.

    Parameters
    ----------
    original : AvailableReference
        Entire original raw observation fact, including its source and assurance.
    replay_ref : BlobRef
        Actual newly retained complete raw_engine.v4 from a separate replay.
    selection : EngineReplaySelection
        Full independently selected pair/profile/semantics/inputs/conversion scope.
    request_ref : BlobRef
        This replay's original complete evaluation_request.v4 identity.
    reads : VerificationReads
        Same original acquisition and six bounds, without a new comparison budget.

    Returns
    -------
    EngineReplayRecord
        Complete native replay row. Unknown and failed observations never match.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Whole selected bindings, request stages or actual native source disagree.
    EmtError
        Original grammar, source integrity, acquisition or unchanged bounds refuse.

    Notes
    -----
    Stored normalization is recomputed from retained native files and options.
    This source comparison supplies no original execution/runner/Clock/profile
    qualification. Native claim policy and every other current gate still apply.

    """
    if (
        type(original) is not AvailableReference
        or type(selection) is not EngineReplaySelection
        or type(reads) is not VerificationReads
    ):
        raise ValueError("Engine replay comparison requires whole original values.")
    AvailableReference.__post_init__(original)
    EngineReplaySelection.__post_init__(selection)
    reference(
        request_ref,
        schema="urn:gotm:design:transpile_witness.closure.evaluation_request.v4",
    )
    reads.resolve(original.source_ref, max_bytes=reads.limits.max_blob_bytes)
    first = _read_raw_engine_source(original.value, reads)
    replay = _read_raw_engine_source(replay_ref, reads)
    expected = {
        "pair_id": selection.pair_id,
        "profile_ref": dict(selection.profile_ref.to_mapping()),
        "semantics_ref": dict(selection.semantics_ref.to_mapping()),
        "environment_ref": dict(selection.domain_ref.to_mapping()),
        "source_input_ref": dict(selection.source_input_ref.to_mapping()),
        "compiled_input_ref": dict(selection.compiled_input_ref.to_mapping()),
        "conversion_refs": [
            dict(ref.to_mapping()) for ref in selection.conversion_refs
        ],
    }
    if any(replay[name] != value for name, value in expected.items()):
        raise ValueError(
            "Engine replay sources substitute the full original selection."
        )
    if (
        first["pair_id"] != selection.pair_id
        or first["semantics_ref"] != replay["semantics_ref"]
        or _problem(first, reads) != _problem(replay, reads)
    ):
        raise ValueError("Engine replay substitutes its original problem or semantics.")
    if (
        blob(first["request_ref"]).schema_id
        != "urn:gotm:design:transpile_witness.closure.witness_request.v4"
        or blob(replay["request_ref"]) != request_ref
        or original.value == replay_ref
        or first["same_run_id"] == replay["same_run_id"]
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            "Engine replay does not retain separate original request stages."
        )
    if first["engine_id"] != replay["engine_id"]:
        raise ValueError("Engine replay changes its original engine identity.")
    engine: EngineId = "qcec" if first["engine_id"] == "qcec" else "pyzx"

Heavy-water pressure-tube design and on-power refuelling interfaces; graphite channel physics belongs to SCPN-CHANNEL-CORE.

This is a local **architecture-only** fission device repository in the SCPN Reactor Systems group. It contains a declared project boundary and working validation infrastructure. The machine-readable [boundary](project-boundary.json) is validated by `python tools/validate_boundary.py project-boundary.json`. Start local source admission with `make scope` and enforce immutable workflow references with `make workflow-sources`; `python tools/preflight.py --gate boundary` runs the real boundary gate with a deadline. Use dedicated tests and strict checks for changed code. The default preflight remains exhaustive and belongs on an authorised runner before a requested push. The current implementation validates repository source and metadata. [project-boundary.json](../project-boundary.json) is a checked PHWR identity, not an active reactor-domain capability or SPO registry record. Its validator refuses any capability, claim, runtime dependency, active configuration or registration at this stage. All scientific components and interfaces described here are proposed and unimplemented.

The source-faithful benchmark profile retains an exact case edition, geometry, material/library state, boundary conditions and source assumptions. Its reference quantities and numerical support belong to that case.

The full fuel-history/refuelling profile additionally needs its own complete nuclear chain, reaction and decay data, composition-dependent properties, energy accounting and source-supported event dynamics. Benchmark reproduction cannot qualify those additional subjects.

Separate prediction profiles would forecast named channel/bundle fields or per-bundle inventory and burnup at requested future times. Each forecast remains conditional on an exact adopted model, current physical state and declared future boundary/history schedule. Scenario outputs retain every submitted scenario identity; their spread does not establish a calibrated probability or confidence interval.
| PHWR-owned component | Input meaning | Intended output meaning |

| Source and profile contract | Original edition, rights, quantities, material/library and supported physical domain | An explicit source/model profile with consistent units, coordinates and support |

| Geometry and material state | Pressure-tube/channel geometry, physical bundle occurrences, computational cells and material instances | A source-supported 3D geometry and occurrence map with explicit volumes and physical identities |
| Own coupled solver | Spatial neutron/poison state, solid temperatures, coolant network and boundary history | Coupled fields and observations for the exact supported model |

| Own fuel-history evolution | Per-bundle nuclide inventory, irradiation lineage, energy history and scheduled refuelling | Evolved inventory and committed incoming, retained and discharged bundle states |
| Separate own predictor | Adopted physical state/profile, target, horizon and future schedule | Model-conditional field or inventory/burnup forecasts with their own evidence |
| Result and inspection contract | Source/profile identities, actual state, geometry and quantity mappings | Evidence-bearing observations and qualified 3D/CAD, workbench and teaching inputs |

Physical bundles, computational cells and thermal groups are separate identity spaces. Refining a mesh cannot duplicate a bundle's atom inventory. A field projection must retain its source units, physical support, averaging and conservation mappings. A 3D/CAD view must preserve geometry and material identity rather than imply a new solved physical model.

The proposed PHWR world model comprises that source-bound physical state, geometry/material occurrence graph and permitted model evolution. Spatial resolution and any dimensional reduction belong to the adopted scientific profile. Observation, prediction and presentation consume the same identified physical subject while retaining separate evidence scopes.

The own coupled formulation retains spatial neutronics and source-supported delayed/poison feedback, conservative solid heat, and the complete supported two-phase/network model. Full equation, property, closure, discretisation, native precision, event and error choices need scientific acceptance before implementation. Numerical primitives do not select these PHWR-specific choices.

On timeout or keyboard interruption, it signals its owned process group with SIGTERM and gives Make two seconds to reap cooperative jobs. This document is the structural map of `scpn-fusion-core`: what the package contains, how
the pieces are wired, what it consumes (inputs) and produces (outputs), the processing
models behind each subsystem, and the multi-backend acceleration layer. It is written for
**SCPN STUDIO** verb/contract design that consume this repository's surfaces. For the
reasoning behind the durable design choices, see
Every claim here is grounded in the source tree. Capability *maturity* (production-grade
positioning, fidelity, what is reduced-order vs full-fidelity, and what is fail-closed) is
governed by the dedicated evidence artifacts — see [Evidence and validation](#evidence-and-validation)
— not by this map. Where a model is reduced-order or a path is dormant, this document says so.
`scpn-fusion-core` is one repository in a multi-repository SCPN ecosystem. Each repository owns
a distinct surface; the boundaries are explicit contracts rather than copied code.

| **`scpn-fusion-core`** (this repo) | **Physics-solver laboratory** | Broad physics kernels, numerical formulation, external-code validation campaigns, facility-data integration, Rust + GPU solver paths, 3D / stellarator / VMEC / free-boundary internals, neural-physics training, and the Petri→SNN control-compiler internals. |

| `scpn-control` | Control-grade integration + facade | Bounded public control APIs, NMPC / controller-loop integration, replay/campaign metadata, HIL / CODAC / EPICS / WebSocket safety boundaries, traceable claim surfaces. Ports/wraps the control-loop subset of FUSION's physics. |
| `scpn-quantum-control` | Quantum + phase-dynamics research | Quantum disruption classifiers, Qiskit/PennyLane execution, quantum Kuramoto/UPDE variants. |
| `scpn-mif-core` | FRC / magneto-inertial fusion | Consumes FUSION's FRC equilibrium / Faraday / compression seams (see [§11](#11-cross-repository-contracts)). |
| `scpn-studio` | Ecosystem hub / verb registry | Consumes per-repo "verbs" + evidence; FUSION is a physics-verb provider. |
A physics model matures **in `scpn-fusion-core` first**; downstream repos wrap the subset that
has a clear control-loop or research contract. FUSION is the canonical owner of the solver-level
mathematics, so the same model is not re-implemented elsewhere.
The package is `src/scpn_fusion/` plus a Rust workspace `scpn-fusion-rs/`
and a validation/evidence tree. It is organised as **physics/control lanes over a
multi-backend dispatch floor**, with a self-auditing validation layer. The
generated capability manifest is the count source of truth for package, Rust,
