`shared_cad_and_meshing_adapters`. The tier-G2 lane of the research group
(its plan of 2026-09-03) consumes this group: the pilot device repository builds
the same named bodies as its G1 model, records the assembly manifest, the
STEP digest and the back-end versions, and proves its bodies against the
analytic forms and its faceting against the G1 volumes. Torus and sphere
primitives, DAGMC-ready faceting for OpenMC and per-body physical groups in
the volume mesh are separate increments with their own sources.
Item 3 as landed renumbered the usage-occurrence identifiers but left the
writer's line wrapping untouched; the wrap column is counted from the
pre-renumbering identifier lengths, so two exports of one assembly in one
process diverged once the process-wide counter crossed a digit boundary
(found by the pilot consumer's six-body assembly). The normaliser now
unfolds the writer's continuation lines (newline plus indent) before
renumbering — Part 21 whitespace is insignificant outside string literals
and the writer never wraps inside a string — and a regression test proves
byte identity across repeated exports and across an interleaved import.
The correction changes the normalised bytes of every export; no consumer
was pinned to the earlier form (the group had not been pushed).
## Addendum 2026-10-02 — physical STEP units and import scale
The B-rep coordinate contract is metres. The original assembly exporter
used CadQuery's default internal unit MM, so its native STEP contexts
declared millimetres while retaining metre-valued coordinate numbers.
Physical lengths were therefore 1000 times smaller and volumes one billion
times smaller. A default-MM round trip compared raw numbers and hid the
defect; provenance describing metres did not change the native units.
`step_bytes` now passes `unit="M", outputUnit="M"` to the public assembly
exporter. The writer creates the native unit contexts; the text normaliser
only changes its existing deterministic fields. Unit-aware CadQuery imports
into M and MM independently recover the same physical dimensions and
volumes. Both target-unit imports are interleaved with repeated exports to
exercise the writer's process-global unit state as well as its counters.
The owned Gmsh session sets `Geometry.OCCTargetUnit` to M before import.
It honours the native file unit rather than treating every coordinate as
metres: physically equivalent metre and millimetre encodings of an
off-centre rectangular prism each mesh to its analytic cubic-metre volume,
even after an earlier real session selected MM. Existing caller sessions
are refused before any unit option changes (ADR 0019).
This is a breaking export contract after consumer registration, so both
distributions advance to `3.0.0.dev0` and the Rust crate to `3.0.0-dev.0`.
STEP identities and any affected mesh identities must be regenerated at
adoption. Consumer source commits and inventory digests remain immutable;
publication and one-consumer-at-a-time adoption are separate operations.
The CAD kernels retain `native_parity=false`: these tests exercise the
pinned third-party C++ implementations, not a new independent Rust CAD
The benchmark has eleven operations after the placement, evidence and
revolution extensions. One ordered catalogue supplies the operation/backend
identities to both measured and unavailable output. Runner binding refuses
a length mismatch. If an optional backend is missing during a timed
operation, that row is unavailable and remaining operations continue.
Domain and unexpected runtime errors are not converted into availability
results. The v1 output schema and the existing physical kernels are unchanged.

`scpn-control` is one repository in a four-repository reactor-semantics path. Each
repository owns a distinct surface, and the boundaries between them are explicit
contracts rather than copied code. Understanding the split explains why a given
capability lives where it does, and where to look for the canonical version of a
physics model, a quantum routine, or a control surface.

| [`scpn-fusion-core`](https://github.com/anulum/scpn-fusion-core) | Physics-solver laboratory | Broad physics kernels, high-fidelity numerical formulation, external-code validation campaigns, facility-data integration, Rust and GPU solver paths, 3D equilibrium / stellarator / VMEC / free-boundary internals, and neural physics training stacks. |

| [`scpn-phase-orchestrator`](https://github.com/anulum/scpn-phase-orchestrator) | Reactor-semantic owner | Reactor configuration identity, phase and nonphase semantic carriers, regime meaning, U0 vocabulary and registry, and portable review-only handoffs. |

| [`scpn-control`](https://github.com/anulum/scpn-control) (this repository) | Control-grade integration and facade | Bounded public control APIs, NMPC and controller-loop integration, Petri-net and SNN runtime contracts, replay and campaign metadata, fail-closed adapters, HIL/CODAC/EPICS/WebSocket safety boundaries, control-side source and actuator gradients, and traceable claim surfaces. |

| [`scpn-quantum-control`](https://github.com/anulum/scpn-quantum-control) | Quantum and phase-dynamics research | Quantum disruption classifiers, Qiskit/PennyLane execution and provider integration, and quantum Kuramoto/UPDE variants. `scpn-control` consumes a bounded control adapter for the quantum disruption path rather than re-implementing it. |

Every cross-repository boundary is a contract, not a shared mutable file. When a

lines: Pulsed-control runtime admission separates a fast native control loop from a
production-admissible runtime claim. The native hot path may run in
microseconds, but SCPN Control only admits production timing evidence when the
- Linux kernel release and PREEMPT_RT or `/sys/kernel/realtime` evidence.
- Current process CPU affinity and the requested SNN, Z3, network, and heartbeat cores.
- Scheduler policy and priority for the calling process.
- CPU governor state for requested cores.
- Native PyO3 runtime snapshot when the extension exposes it.
| `off` | Emit a schema-valid skipped admission record. Use only for local diagnostics. |
| `warn` | Run admission and continue even when the host is not production-qualified. This is the default for developer workstations. |
| `require` | Fail closed before campaign execution if PREEMPT_RT, real-time scheduler, performance governor, core affinity, heartbeat, or memory-lock requirements are not met. |
`warn` evidence must be labelled as local regression evidence. It must not be
used to claim hard real-time PCS timing.
If any runtime condition is missing, the command fails before the native loop is
entered. That fail-closed behavior is intentional.
When heartbeat monitoring is enabled, the Rust bridge refuses to start unless
`SCPN_CONTROL_HEARTBEAT_KEY_FILE` names a non-symlink regular file containing
32–64 raw key bytes with no group/other permissions on POSIX hosts and
`SCPN_CONTROL_HEARTBEAT_ALLOWED_SOURCE` is one exact source IP. The bind host
defaults to `127.0.0.1`; set `SCPN_CONTROL_HEARTBEAT_BIND_HOST` explicitly for a
non-loopback interface. Raw key bytes do not enter CLI arguments or telemetry.
The accepted datagram is exactly 48 bytes: ASCII magic `SCPNHB01`, a strictly
increasing unsigned 64-bit big-endian counter, and the full HMAC-SHA256 tag over
`build_transport_heartbeat_frame()` to construct sender packets. Wrong source,
length, magic, tag, zero/repeated/reordered counter within one receiver
lifetime, or malformed configuration never refreshes liveness. Sender and
receiver must establish a new counter epoch after a receiver restart; this
one-way hint does not claim durable cross-restart replay protection.
This heartbeat is a bounded transport-liveness hint. It is not an independent
machine-protection interlock, safety function, or PCS deployment credential.
The returned report is JSON-serializable and includes
`production_claim_allowed`. That field remains `false` unless strict production
`runtime_admission` record. Emergency telemetry and post-run diagnostic dumps
therefore preserve the launch-time scheduler, affinity, governor, heartbeat,
and PREEMPT_RT assumptions that governed the campaign.
reads reports from `benchmarks/bench_runtime_admission.py`. Its default input is
report. Reading that file does not inspect the current host or authorise an
execution campaign. The top-level `scpn-control validate` command invokes the
reader by default; its runtime summary is one of several release declarations.
The frozen result records reader status/findings, exact input-byte SHA-256,
declared payload SHA-256, evidence class, production flag, probe status,
error-list count and positive sample count. `as_dict()` returns a fresh mapping.
Wrong-type declarations become `None` in typed string/boolean result fields;
invalid strings remain visible on FAIL. Read/decode failures have no digest;
decoded objects, including empty or schema-invalid objects, retain their byte
digest. Empty objects fail required fields.
The reader checks schema `scpn-control.runtime-admission-benchmark.v1`, a command
containing `bench_runtime_admission.py`, and a canonical self-digest computed
from sorted compact JSON with `payload_sha256` blank. Extra fields enter that
digest but are otherwise unvalidated. Duplicate keys and nonfinite floating
JSON tokens at all depths fail. A self-digest detects stale edits; an edited
and resealed report is not producer authentication.
Affinity must be a nonempty list of nonnegative integer CPU IDs, excluding
booleans. Start/end load arrays contain three finite nonnegative numbers;
platform, Python version and isolation method are nonempty strings. Samples
are positive integers. Six latency fields are finite/nonnegative; min, median,
p95, p99 and max are monotonic, with mean inside min/max. CPU existence or
uniqueness, actual isolation, sample recomputation, latency ceilings, timestamp
freshness and host qualification are not verified here.
production flags and nonempty-string error/warning elements. A failed local
probe needs explanatory errors and a false production flag; reader PASS still
grants no production timing. Production-shaped declarations need claim true,
probe PASS and empty errors, but are not independently qualified host evidence.
A probe PASS requires empty errors in either class.
The standalone command uses only the standard library, follows caller-relative
paths and symlinks, prints JSON/text to stdout and writes no report. Its exit
codes are 0/1 for PASS/findings and 2 for argparse errors. It imposes no filesystem
containment or input size/depth budget. The root command runs its other enabled
gates too; explicitly skipping them is a scoped reader check, not release
admission. Neither command starts a physical control loop through this reader.
This document defines what must pass before code moves from local execution to campaign-grade orchestration.
- environment checks that match the target mode,
- and explicit handling of missing or failed admission checks.
The runtime admission surface is the final gate in the execution boundary and should be treated as non-optional in any hardening flow.
Use this page to define what enters the production-timing admissible path.
- Apply these rules before running hot-path validation in native or threaded execution modes.
- Keep runtime admission checks consistent across benchmarking and campaign scripts.

milliseconds. For each transition, simultaneous contributions are summed at

lines: **Many systems succeed or fail on timing.** When thousands of microservices
retry in the same instant, the synchronised surge takes the cluster down. When
generators on a power grid drift out of step, the grid trips. When neurons fire
in lockstep, it looks like a seizure. When fusion-plasma modes phase-lock, the
reactor disrupts. These look like unrelated incidents, but they are one problem
wearing different clothes: **coupled rhythms drifting into — or out of — sync.**
SCPN Phase Orchestrator (SPO) is an **auditable assurance envelope** for that
problem — a Python library and CLI that wraps synchronisation analysis in sealed,
replayable evidence with *honest, false-alarm-controlled* claim boundaries rather
than one confident number. It takes the repeating signals a system already
produces — waveforms, event streams, state changes — turns them into a shared
language of **phase** (where each rhythm sits in its cycle), and gives operators a
way to ask three questions, each answer bound to a reproducible record:
1. **What is locking together,** and is that lock useful or dangerous?
2. **Is the system's damping falling toward a regime change?** SPO estimates this
where the signature is a physically deterministic mode — e.g. a grid
generic early-warning detection is at chance at an honest operating point, and
SPO is built to *report that* rather than overclaim (see **Evidence status**
3. **Which single, bounded knob** could steer it back — as a reviewable,
The same representation applies to a grid operator, an SRE chasing retry storms, a
plasma physicist, or a neuroscientist, because underneath these are
coupled-oscillator systems. SPO ships bindings for **36 such domains** (power
grids, fusion, cloud queues, cardiac and EEG rhythms, swarm robotics, traffic,
markets, and more) — a binding is a reusable scaffold, **not** a validated
detector for that domain — and it never actuates blindly: every proposed change
is bounded, rate-limited, and audit-logged for human review.

## Executive overview (What SPO Is and What It Is Not)

SPO is a synchronisation-analysis toolkit for systems that can be expressed as coupled oscillatory processes, with a review-only control-proposal surface. It gives teams a single interface for turning telemetry into phase variables, evaluating coherence, and *proposing* bounded control updates with replay evidence for human review — it does not close a control loop on hardware.
In practical terms, SPO is useful when:
- A domain has reusable cycle structure (time-of-day shifts, wave timing, phase-locked loops, rhythm-driven events, spatially propagating oscillations).
- Operational teams need explainable interventions before actuation, not black-box controller outputs.
- Governance requires deterministic evidence trails, policy guardrails, and cross-language consistency checks.

SPO is not a universal AI controller, a live PLC hardening platform, or a ready-made certified hardware stack. It is a synchrony-aware simulation and control framework that can be embedded in those ecosystems after domain validation and adapter-specific evidence are attached.

The immediate commercial value is the reduction of uncertainty in phase-control projects: instead of asking whether a system is "stable" from a single metric, teams get shared, auditable artefacts for **what was measured, what was proposed, what was bounded, and what was replayed**.

Scope of this document set: **architecture only** (structure, data flow,

SPO is a domain-agnostic coherence-control toolkit for hierarchical oscillator
systems. It takes a declarative description of a domain (a *domainpack*),
extracts phase from raw signals, integrates coupled phase dynamics (the Universal
Phase Dynamics Equation, UPDE — a Kuramoto/Sakaguchi family with extensions),
observes the resulting dynamics through a large array of monitors, and proposes
bounded, audited control actions through a supervisory layer. The design
posture is **review-only by default**: the core produces control *proposals* and
a tamper-evident audit trail; it does not actuate hardware itself.

per domain) from *physics* (the integrator and observers), so the same engine
serves power-grid, rotating-machinery, neural, swarm, plasma, and other domains
by swapping a domainpack rather than code.

The full board instrument remains planned and no measured result exists. Synthesizable
timestamp capture, a dual-clock record buffer, numeric event codes, a run-manifest schema and
host analysis exist. Both sampled plants, references, deadline/safe-state monitor, fault injector
and simultaneous-event capture feed the drain stream and host CLI in simulation. C, Rust and
RTL PID/LQR kernels have bit-exact parity, with an integrated fabric feedback loop and native
command replay through simulated actuator transactions. Native AXI simulation and Linux UIO run
software are implemented; physical I/O, power acquisition and processor timing remain unqualified.
No physical board is available. The
machine-readable design contract is `measurement-domain.json`, validated by
`tools/validate_measurement_domain.py`; changes to that contract also update its schema, this
PolarFire SoC Icicle Kit, device MPFS250T-FCVG484E, as described in the board user guide
(Microchip DS60001679E). Facts used by the design:
| SiFive E51 monitor core and four U54 application cores | E51 boots the system; U54 cores run Linux or a bare-metal controller |
| On-board 50 MHz oscillator | reference for the fabric clock conditioning circuit |
| PAC1934 power monitor on the processor subsystem I²C bus, four rails (VDD, VDD25, VDDA25, VDDA) | energy windows |
| Two Gigabit Ethernet ports | run control and data transfer to the host |
| Raspberry Pi 4 compatible header | optional mirror of the event strobes for an external logic analyser |
Not yet checked on hardware, and therefore not relied on: the asymmetric-multiprocessing
reference release for the current board support package, the PAC1934 sampling configuration of
the reference Linux image, and the fabric RAM budget used to freeze the event buffer size.
The board-facing `rtl/icicle_witness.sv` presents a 38-bit AXI4-Lite address port to a fabric
interconnect that selects the planned 256-byte register range at `0x60020000` through
`0x600200ff`. It passes the low eight address bits to `axi_control_witness` and exposes its
retained interrupt level. This boundary is exercised in simulation; the Libero interconnect,
capture clock, interrupt route and physical timing are not yet qualified.
The pinned Icicle reference source configures the FIC0 bus clock at 125 MHz from CCC GL0_0
and the witness capture clock at 100 MHz from CCC GL0_1. Those source settings do not
establish implemented clock rates or CDC timing closure.
50 MHz osc ───► │  CCC/PLL ─► 64-bit timebase (100 MHz, 10 ns)           E51: boot        │
│  Event witness ◄── strobes ── controller I/O register ◄── controller    │
│  Plant emulator (fixed point) ── sample-ready interrupt ──► MSS         │
│  Fabric controller (fixed-point PID / LQR) ◄─ placement select         │
│  Deadline and safe-state monitor ──► safe actuator value, fault flag   │

MSS I²C ─► PAC1934 (four rails) ─► Linux energy logger
Gigabit Ethernet ─► host: run control, transfer, analysis, report
A clock conditioning circuit derives 100 MHz from the 50 MHz oscillator. A free-running 64-bit
counter gives 10 ns resolution and cannot wrap in any planned run; the validator checks that the
counter width outlasts one repeat at the lowest sample rate. Multi-phase capture for finer
resolution is a later option and is accepted only if the known-period test shows the improvement.
A discrete-time second-order plant (mass, spring, damper) and a first-order thermal plant, in
signed fixed point with a documented Q format per plant. The plant updates once per sample period
(100 Hz to 20 kHz, 1 kHz by default) with the most recent actuator value that arrived before the
update; a late command is applied one period later and counted. A reference generator (step,
ramp, sine) provides the tracking target. Implemented Q8.24 equations, coefficients and ports
An AXI4-Lite peripheral on a fabric interface controller holds the sample register, the actuator
register and the cycle counter. It raises the `CONTROL` profile strobes:
| `SAMPLE_READ` | first bus read of the sample register in the cycle |
| `ACT_WRITE` | first timely actuator command in the cycle |
| `ACT_LATE` | first accepted out-of-cycle or deadline-edge command, tagged with its observation cycle |
| `SAFE_STATE` | safe actuator value applied by the monitor |
FIFO and separate reset-release synchronisers. It accepts one event-code/cycle tuple per
capture-clock edge without stalling the measured source. The original timestamp is retained
through the capture pipeline and drain. Event codes are declared in `measurement-domain.json`
and `rtl/event_codes_pkg.sv`. Public ports and reset/overflow behaviour are specified in

strobes before serialization; its ports are in [`PLANT_WITNESS.md`](PLANT_WITNESS.md). The AXI
The default buffer holds 16 384 records. A full buffer drops the newest record, pulses
`event_dropped`, latches `overflowed` and increments a saturating 32-bit count. Reset starts a
new run and flushes both clock domains; there is no independent-domain reset. Capture-domain
status is not a coherent processor snapshot. A nonzero overflow count invalidates the host run.
Linux is planned to drain at least 20 times per second. At 20 kHz with four periodic events per
cycle the buffer fills in about 205 ms, longer than the 50 ms slowest drain interval; the
validator checks that inequality and the declared Gray-pointer capacity. Drain frequency alone
cannot establish sustained throughput or prevent loss during software stalls; board RAM sizing,
drain bandwidth and physical CDC constraints still require qualification.
| time to safe state | `SAFE_STATE −` first missed `DEADLINE` |
A cycle misses its deadline when `ACT_WRITE` does not arrive before `DEADLINE`.
The monitor counts misses in hardware. After a configurable number of consecutive misses it drives
the actuator to a defined safe value, raises a latched fault flag and interrupt, and records
Drops a sample-ready interrupt, delays it by a number of periods, freezes the actuator register,
or requests a processor overload scenario from the software load generator. Every injection is an
event on the same timebase, so detection latency comes from the same clock as everything else.
`fixed_point_controller.sv` implements PID with conditional integration and discrete LQR.
`fabric_control_witness.sv` connects it to the sampled plant and existing independent monitor,
record capture and drain. In simulation the first read follows sample-ready by one tick and
the timely actuator write follows by another tick. This is a registered RTL schedule, not
physical timing closure. Arithmetic, reset, coefficients and native counterparts are specified
in [`CONTROLLERS.md`](CONTROLLERS.md). A board placement register remains planned.
The register, strobes and witness are built around a generic slot: an AXI4-Lite peripheral with
input and output registers, a start strobe and a done interrupt. The `COMPUTE` profile records
manifest derives input-to-start, compute duration, done-to-interrupt and input-to-output
intervals. In this repository the profile is exercised with a fixed-latency test peripheral
written for the purpose; accelerator-specific adapters live in the accelerator's own repository.

| `linux_user_space` | U54 application cores | user-space task, registers and interrupt through UIO, `SCHED_FIFO` with CPU affinity; with and without a PREEMPT_RT kernel if one builds for the board support package |

Controllers are textbook PID with anti-windup and discrete LQR, with identical coefficients in C,
Rust and fabric logic and bit-exact fixed-point parity checked in simulation. Native streaming
CLIs, the in-process Linux UIO entry and [dedicated-hart ISA capture](AMP_SIMULATION.md)
are implemented. The latter executes source-bound firmware against production RTL; Linux/HSS/PMP

maps separate explicit mailbox/fabric resources without owning the controller IRQ, using the same

remain unqualified. The implemented host load generator covers idle, CPU arithmetic,
memory/cache strides, private loopback UDP and owned-file storage/fsync profiles. Source-bound
captures retain policy readback, actual operation counters and worker/native time brackets; see
[host load profiles](HOST_ANALYSIS.md#linux-host-load-profiles). These do not qualify physical
processor timing, NIC traffic or uncached block-device load. A Linux run
controller configures the fabric registers, starts and stops runs, drains the buffer, reads the
power monitor and writes the run files.
uses the Linux IIO interface. The logger must bind the selected BSP/driver revision, channel-to-rail
mapping, shunts, sampling configuration and accumulator units. An assumed `hwmon` interface or
automatic direct-I²C fallback cannot establish that acquisition contract.
The native UIO entry accepts `--power-config file --power-journal file` together. Its separate
normal-policy worker validates the actual IIO node, kernel release, driver, enabled accumulators,
labels, sample rate and unsigned shunt scales. It preserves each raw/scale attribute with its own
host and fabric read brackets. The journal is acquisition evidence; it is not the analyzer's
qualified `power.csv`. The current host has no PAC1934 device, so successful physical acquisition

for the explicit configuration and units.
Fabric counter brackets around acquisition and the driver's cache/refresh timing must be retained.
Sequential channel reads do not establish an atomic four-rail snapshot or an exact common fabric
tick. Energy-window alignment remains unqualified until the acquisition timing contract is
validated on the board. The reported metric is mean energy per control cycle over windows of many
cycles, per rail and for the four rails together, with the limits stated in

`tools/analyze_run.py` validates the run manifest and referenced file hashes, interprets the

Loop Timing Witness — fabric witness RTL
`rtl/event_witness.sv` connects the timestamp capture to a dual-clock FIFO. This is a
simulation-tested stream component. Peripheral event arbitration, AXI/UIO access, coherent
processor status snapshots, physical clock constraints and board qualification remain planned.
The domain maturity is `architecture_only`; the capability inventory remains empty.
| `event_valid`, `event_code[7:0]`, `cycle_number[31:0]` | capture | One tuple per rising edge when `capture_active` is high. No backpressure. |
| `capture_active` | capture | Local run reset has released. |
| `counter_ticks[63:0]` | capture | Free-running counter, cleared by run reset; record samples the pre-increment value. |
| `buffer_full` | capture | No new record can be accepted at the current write edge. |
| `event_dropped` | capture | High for each edge rejecting a pending captured record. Consecutive drops keep it high. |
| `overflowed` | capture | Sticky loss flag until run reset. |
| `overflow_count` | capture | Saturating count of rejected records; a lower bound after saturation. |
| `drain_request` | drain | Request the next record; empty requests do not advance the pointer. |
| `drain_valid`, `drain_record[127:0]` | drain | Registered result of the request at this rising edge; consume only when valid. |
| `drain_empty` | drain | No record currently visible to the read domain. |
A source tuple is captured at an edge, then offered to the FIFO at the next capture edge.
It retains the original timestamp even if it later crosses into the drain domain. The write
status and overflow pulse therefore refer to the pending captured record. The source must
supply event codes from `rtl/event_codes_pkg.sv` and the hash-bound domain snapshot. The host
rejects unknown codes, nonzero reserved fields, regressing ticks/cycles and duplicate events.
Arbitrate simultaneous source strobes before this input; this module cannot represent two
events at one capture edge. Clock crossing of asynchronous source strobes is also upstream.
Write its least significant byte first for the published 16-byte little-endian host format.
The record payload is unspecified when `drain_valid` is low, including during reset.
`rtl/shared_event_witness.sv` gives independent event FIFOs one common 64-bit capture
counter. Each channel supplies its own pre-edge valid bit, eight-bit code and 32-bit
identity. Channel buses are flat: channel `i` occupies bits `i*width +: width`,
with widths 8 for code, 32 for identity, 64 for run counts and 128 for a record.
Simultaneous tuples receive the same pre-increment timestamp, with zero
reserved fields in the existing 128-bit record layout. Codes and identities are supplied
by the caller's declared profile; the instrument does not interpret a neural state or
The shared capture reset and counter release together. Each registered tuple enters its
channel FIFO on the next capture edge. `attempt_count` counts those FIFO write attempts;
`accepted_count` counts accepted writes. A full channel drops its newest record and
updates its own sticky flag, drop pulse and saturating overflow count. Other channels
continue independently. Attempt and acceptance counts are 64-bit run counters; the
admitted run must end before their wrap. Capture-domain status needs a coherent snapshot
before crossing to a processor or drain clock domain.
the FIFO and single-channel witness limits. Every channel has its own drain request,
valid record and empty flag. An unused channel remains empty. Common reset flushes all
channels and clears the shared timebase and counts. Reset release, conservative FIFO
flags, physical CDC constraints and RAM qualification follow the same rules below.
The dedicated simulation exports simultaneous known-edge records, continuously captures
1,000 records plus two markers per channel at 1,024-record capacity before drain, and
exercises isolated full-buffer loss, saturation, an empty channel and queued-data reset.
These are instrument-port controls. Neural wrapper, complete export/report integration
and board qualification have separate acceptance requirements.
input, state and service capture streams, retaining original payload and alignment-marker
bytes. Its neural record vocabulary uses data codes 14, 15 and 16 respectively and marker
code 17; it does not register a neural profile in the CONTROL/COMPUTE domain. Missing
markers, identity gaps and empty streams remain visible. A marker-only service stream has
an empty payload; this alone does not establish that the encoder tail or export completed.
Reserved bits, marker positions, population bounds, record order and the 16-bit no-wrap
horizon are checked independently of file-digest and source binding.
records by their original step identities. It checks the complete requested populations,
continuous input cadence, one-tick registered observation phase and matching dedicated
markers across all three channels. Available pairs retain their original ticks and signed
intervals even when a run fails those checks. The result contains explicit refusals and
does not establish numerical equality, encoder provenance, loss-counter reconciliation,
export finalisation or physical timing. The separate RTL port controls exercise complete
1,000-step phased streams before drain and a service channel containing only markers.
versioned counter receipt in input/state/service order. Each channel retains the actual
attempt, accepted, dropped and drained counts, sticky overflow flag and compiled drop-counter
width. `reconcile_neural_capture` checks the original decoded record count against those
snapshots. Loss, mismatched totals, incomplete drain and missing exported records produce
explicit refusals. A drop count at its maximum remains a lower bound. A channel can satisfy
count reconciliation while missing alignment markers or an encoder tail; those independent
run predicates still require verification. The real RTL controls exercise both three-bit
saturation and exact unsaturated loss at the default 32-bit width.
SHA-256 and byte-length reference against one caller-admitted finite allocation. It reads a
complete regular file inside the source-custodied run directory and returns exactly the bytes
whose whole length and digest passed. The declared length plus the extra boundary byte must
fit the host's index-sized read limit; oversized declarations are refused before opening the
file. Decoders reuse those bytes. A present zero-byte service
payload can be bound with a zero-byte allocation; an absent file is refused. The source
directory and its files must remain frozen throughout verification and reporting.
`loop_timing_witness.neural_capture.load_neural_capture` combines these checks for all three
channels. It takes the original full/payload/marker references, a bound counter receipt and
the requested step count, service-ordinal population and no-wrap horizon. It verifies exact
projection bytes, reconciles counts and expected attempts including both markers, checks the
complete service-ordinal population and joins the original input/state observations. Known
loss, population, projection and phase failures remain located findings alongside available
observations. Unsupported declarations or unreadable/malformed bound inputs are refused.
of a report from those retained bytes. It preserves the requested populations, all original
observations, their raw record byte offsets, actual source hashes, declared and derived
projection hashes, alignment markers, counter bounds and refusal locations. Missing markers
remain null and an absent service population remains empty. The component reports shared-counter
ticks and makes no numerical, encoder-tail, source-qualification or whole-run acceptance claim.
`ADDRESS_BITS` accepts 1 through 14; capacity is `2**ADDRESS_BITS`, with the default 16,384
records. The capture pipeline is not an extra accepted storage slot. A full FIFO preserves
stored records and drops the newest pending record. There is no attempt to stall measured
source activity. `OVERFLOW_COUNTER_BITS` accepts 1 through 32, default 32. Invalid parameter
values fail elaboration/simulation. Any loss invalidates the run, including after the buffer
recovers. The host manifest must record the final capture-domain count before run reset.
The machine-readable `event_fifo` contract declares the Gray-pointer implementation,
drop-newest policy, 32-bit counter and reset policy. The schema requires those policy fields
when the implementation is declared; the validator checks a supported power-of-two depth.
Earlier v1 domain snapshots without that implementation declaration retain their original
sizing contract, so archived hash-bound runs remain interpretable.
`event_record_fifo.sv` uses binary pointers with an extra wrap bit, Gray-coded pointers,
two destination-clock synchroniser stages, registered full/empty flags and a dual-clock
128-bit memory. Full compares the next write Gray pointer to the synchronised read pointer
with its top two bits inverted. Empty compares the next read Gray pointer to the synchronised
write pointer. Synchronisation makes flags conservative: newly written data or newly freed
space becomes visible after destination-clock edges, rather than immediately. Synchroniser
registers carry `ASYNC_REG` attributes. This follows FIFO style 1 in Clifford E. Cummings,
[Simulation and Synthesis Techniques for Asynchronous FIFO Design, SNUG 2002](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252160343_Simulation_and_Synthesis_Techniques_for_Asynchronous_FIFO_Design).
Both clocks share `run_reset_n`. Assertion is asynchronous; each `clock_reset_release.sv`
instance waits for two local rising edges before release. A stopped clock remains in reset.
Assertion flushes the run, clears the timebase and loss state and prevents old records from
becoming valid. RAM contents and the invalid read payload are not cleared, preserving memory
inference. Independent reset of one pointer domain is unsupported. Hold the common reset low
for the device's required minimum pulse width and meet reset-recovery/removal constraints.
Capturing and draining need no coherent shared clock. Reading capture-domain status from
processor logic does require a separate coherent CDC snapshot; synchronising each counter
bit separately is insufficient. Gray-bus skew/max-delay constraints, placement of synchroniser
stages and RAM inference must be supplied and reviewed in the vendor integration. RTL simulation
and generic synthesis do not establish metastability rates, timing closure or physical RAM fit.
Run the dedicated public-port simulations and real host integration:
verilator --lint-only --Wall --top-module event_witness rtl/clock_reset_release.sv rtl/event_record_capture.sv rtl/event_record_fifo.sv rtl/event_witness.sv
The FIFO scoreboard exercises full capacity, requests at empty, four complete fill/drain
rounds, deterministic random traffic, faster/slower/equal clock rates, queued-data reset and
recovery. The witness scoreboard checks every accepted record and its original timestamp,
continuous events, 17 counted drops, small-width saturation, recovery and a fresh run. The
host tests bind the sources, compiled simulation and binary stream by SHA-256, check 5,000-tick
periods and 20-tick loop latency, and mark an actual overflow stream invalid. Those values are
test schedules, not board performance claims.
Generic synthesis must retain one 128-bit by 16,384 dual-clock memory at default capacity.
Post-optimisation equivalence uses a small FIFO configuration with memory mapping and
`async2sync` normalisation before comparing the prepared and synthesised designs. That proof
checks logic transformations under the normalised model; it does not prove physical CDC safety.

same dual-clock FIFO. Its group-queue and combined loss semantics are specified in

This document fixes how measurements will be taken and reported. It contains no board results:
none exist, and no physical board is currently available. Functional controller simulation
is specified in [`CONTROLLERS.md`](CONTROLLERS.md); native CLI wall times are local regression
evidence, not processor placement measurements. The numeric parameters that the validator can check live in
`measurement-domain.json` under `design_contracts`; a change to either place must change both.
The implemented host file formats and calculations are specified in
One configuration is one combination of:
- load case: idle, CPU stress, memory and cache stress, network stress, storage stress;
- sample rate: from 100 Hz to 20 kHz, 1 kHz by default;
- controller (PID with anti-windup or discrete LQR) with its coefficients, and plant
(second-order mechanical or first-order thermal) with its fixed-point format;
- fault schedule, empty for timing runs.
1. The board is powered from its own supply only. Room temperature is recorded.
2. The same bitstream serves every placement; the placement changes through a register only.
3. Each repeat starts after a reboot.
4. A fixed warm-up period is discarded; its length is recorded in the run manifest.
5. Each repeat runs 1 000 000 control cycles (about 17 minutes at 1 kHz).
6. Each configuration is repeated five times.
7. Every repeat writes its event file, power file, measurement-domain snapshot and run manifest
with SHA-256 of each referenced file, the bitstream, firmware, operating-system images and
controller binary, and the tool versions.
8. A repeat with any event-buffer overflow is invalid and is reported as invalid, not dropped.
The buffered RTL witness produces event files for host-tool verification through its actual
drain stream, including known-period and overflow simulations. Its drop-newest buffer retains
accepted records, latches overflow and counts drops with a saturating 32-bit counter. The count
is a lower bound after saturation, and `overflowed` remains set until common run reset. Record
status before reset: reset flushes both domains and clears all run counters. A processor logger
must implement a coherent capture-domain status snapshot before using it in a manifest; raw CDC
sampling is insufficient. RTL ports and reset timing are specified in
`source.kind: rtl_simulation` and remain simulation evidence even when the input series are
internally valid. A board run declares the source, all input and build artefact paths and their
SHA-256 values; the host checks the referenced bytes. The board acceptance flags in the run
manifest are operator declarations, not a replacement for the separate same-bitstream acceptance
- Latency and jitter are reported as distributions — median, 95th, 99th and 99.9th percentile and
maximum — per repeat and pooled, with the spread between repeats.
- Every statistic states its sample count and run duration. No single-run number is presented
- Per-run latency jitter means the absolute change in the same periodic event interval
between adjacent post-warm-up cycles. Both intervals must be complete; missing cycles
are never bridged. Pair counts, expected pairs and missing-pair coverage accompany the

The native capture path binds the executed source snapshot, configuration, executable, original
event stream, raw tracking and completion metadata to the run manifest. It declares
`source.kind: rtl_simulation`; its reports remain `simulation_only`, with physical acceptance

Optional hash-bound `native_metadata` preserves the final live miss, overflow, sample and record

A result may be reported only after the instrument has passed, on the same bitstream, the
known-period test, the injected-delay test, the overflow test and the bus-offset calibration

The public guard scripts dispatch to cohesive modules for strict inputs, deterministic reports, owned process execution, metadata, inventory, dependencies, attribution, workflows and documentation. Expected identity, schema/source hashes, resource bounds and role ownership are maintained constants. Received files cannot select executables, weaken expected schemas or enable network fallback.

JSON rejects duplicate members, nonfinite numbers and invalid scalar Unicode. YAML preserves the GitHub `on` key and refuses aliases, merges, executable tags and duplicate members. Source traversal checks actual kinds and counts before reading content; excluded tooling trees must be real local directories. Git tracking remains separately inspected.
Dependency alignment checks the complete known development package declaration
alongside the original scaffold form. Direct development requirements include the
one explicit local runtime input, with exact versions and unique package names.
These declaration checks retain the separate locked graph, installed producer,
provenance and audit gates; they do not qualify the evidence runtime or load a
received backend, entrypoint or include path.
The workflow guard checks one retained policy and all seven workflow inputs.
Its optional `--outcomes` file is read once through the bounded JSON reader.
The closed six-role projection accepts only flat outcome strings and requires
all six successes in addition to the complete static graph. Earlier graph
findings remain in the same report. Neither an omitted projection nor supplied

Inventory generation and verification are acyclic. Metadata validates before generation; final verification checks every required path and the actual metadata source digest. Preflight verifies only and preserves each role's observed result. Owned Linux process groups have bounded capture, termination and reaping. Required roles share one total deadline.

The evidence runtime is a separate source surface under development. Its six functions receive explicit bytes, limits, static schema registries and caller-owned sources; verification retains complete independent report axes and reference observations. The source module is `evidence_manifest_toolkit`. Its runtime is under development; the repository's qualified capability inventory remains empty. The functions below operate on caller-supplied bytes, configurations and sources. Operational root, signer, clock and scientific qualification are separate obligations.
| `canonicalize_json` | `data: bytes`, keyword `limits: Limits` | Complete RFC 8785 canonical bytes. |
| `reference_bytes` | `data: bytes`, keywords `media_type`, `digest_basis`, `schema_id`, `limits` | `BlobRef` identifying the selected raw or canonical bytes. |
| `inspect` | `content_json: bytes`, keyword `limits` | `Inspection` containing declarations and diagnostics; acceptance is `not_evaluated`. |
| `diff` | `left_json`, `right_json`, keyword `limits`, optional ordered `left_envelopes` and `right_envelopes` | `Difference` with content identities, changed pointers and receipt identities. |

| `seal` | `content_json`, keywords `schema_id`, `registry`, `resolver`, `limits`, optional `signing`, `signer`, `trust` | `SealResult` with canonical content, its reference and an optional detached envelope. |

All six limit fields are explicit positive integers: `max_json_bytes`, `max_blob_bytes`, `max_total_reference_bytes`, `max_reference_count`, `max_graph_depth` and `max_json_depth`. `Limits.validate()` checks the declaration; operations independently check it before acquisition. Construction supplies no defaults or unlimited mode.

`BlobRef` retains `digest`, decimal-string `byte_length`, `media_type`, `digest_basis` and optional `schema_id`. Its constructor retains the supplied declaration. `BlobRef.from_mapping()` and `to_mapping()` validate the complete wire shape; the returned mapping is detached and read-only. Neither method retrieves bytes or establishes their identity. The wire representation omits an absent `schema_id`; an explicitly received null is invalid.

`reference_bytes` requires `digest_basis="raw_bytes"` or `"jcs_content"`. Raw identity binds the original bytes; canonical identity binds the complete strict canonical document. The helper does not rewrite or store the input. A declared schema ID does not register that schema.

The caller selects a complete `SchemaRegistry`, including its snapshot reference and all fourteen fields of every `RegistryEntry`. Static schema bytes, dependencies, reference paths and common semantics are independently checked. An artifact cannot choose a Python implementation or network schema resolver.

Each read returns actual bounded bytes. A missing target raises `ReferenceUnavailable` with the exact original argument in `.reference`. A digest-only lookup retains the original digest string; it does not fabricate a missing length or schema declaration. Operations check returned identities and share cumulative reference budgets across the whole selected graph.
An uncached full-reference read receives the smaller of `max_blob_bytes` and the
remaining cumulative allowance. An exhausted allowance refuses before calling
the resolver. Cached bytes retain their metadata checks and require no new read.

`TrustContext` selects an independently accepted bootstrap policy, current snapshot, accepted sequence floor, evaluation mode and time, explicit control envelopes, and an optional archived snapshot. Historical mode requires the selected archive and retains current floor and revocation checks. Verification does not install a snapshot, advance a floor, issue a certificate or derive trusted time from a producer timestamp.

`VerificationPolicy` supplies the policy reference, exact required claim and purpose populations, and any declared reference requirements. The referenced policy and caller selections must agree. Selecting a narrower claim population preserves the full content and reference observations; it does not rewrite the inventory or supply a domain verdict.

Unsigned `seal` uses `signing=None`, `signer=None` and `trust=None`. Signed construction requires all three together and current authority. The actual caller-owned `Signer` exposes raw public-key bytes and `sign(message: bytes) -> bytes`. The signature covers the complete context-specific message and is checked before an envelope is returned. A signer failure does not trigger unsigned construction. Initial root issuance and adapter qualification are outside these functions.

`Utc(raw)` validates an original string using the Gregorian calendar, the selected leap-second history and the complete fractional token. It is an immutable string subtype. It preserves the original spelling, including the distinction between `T` and `t`, and uses ordinary string equality for wire identity.

`value.compare(other)` accepts `Utc` or a string, revalidates both operands and returns `-1`, `0` or `1` by exact instant order. It does not round through a floating-point epoch. Malformed scalar input raises `InputRefused` with the original located reason.

The caller's independently qualified `Clock.now()` supplies the time token. `Utc(clock.now())` validates that token; it does not qualify the clock's source, controller, capture, freshness or uncertainty. The existing clock precondition remains with its owner. Required unavailable clock qualification retains the policy refusal in the complete verification report.

Common eligibility reports the applicable common gates. `domain_verdict` remains `not_evaluated`; the separately owned domain consumer supplies scientific acceptance. Historical common eligibility does not establish current eligibility. Inspection and difference results do not authenticate receipts or accept evidence.

Thrown `EmtError` subclasses carry one complete `.reason`: `InputRefused`, `ConfigurationError`, `ReferenceUnavailable`, `SignerUnavailable` or `StorageError`. A `Reason` has `code`, `subject_digest`, `claim_id`, `pointer` and fixed `detail`. Unknown identities retain their null values. Returned verification refusals remain complete reports rather than being replaced with a successful Boolean.
After an eligible signing adapter is called, response failure uses the fixed
`SignerUnavailable` reason and known content digest. Other typed operation errors
retain their classification. Internal verifier errors are separate from adapter

The source checkout runs the commands through `python -m evidence_manifest_toolkit` from the `src/` directory, using explicit absolute input and output paths. Installed `emt` packaging remains under development. The grammar below uses the executable's design name.
emt seal --content FILE --schema-id ID --registry FILE --objects DIR --limits FILE --output NEW_DIR [--signing-request FILE --signer-config FILE --trust FILE]
emt verify --content FILE --schema-id ID --registry FILE --objects DIR --limits FILE --policy FILE --trust FILE --report NEW_FILE [--signature FILE]...
emt diff --left FILE --right FILE --limits FILE --report NEW_FILE [--left-signature FILE]... [--right-signature FILE]...

Every configuration is an explicit closed local JSON value. `--limits` supplies all six positive integer bounds described in the [Python API](api.md). Its initial read is bounded by the size measured on the same opened regular-file handle. Once decoded, its bounds control subsequent inputs. A small `max_json_bytes` does not impose that future bound on the limits file itself.
Native parser or canonical writer recursion exhaustion produces `limit_exceeded`
and exit `2` before successful output publication, including when the configured

Registry, policy and trust files encode the complete corresponding public value types. Bytes in configurations use canonical unpadded Base64URL. Decimal lengths, digests and UTC strings retain their original spelling. Repeated detached-signature flags preserve caller order; the command does not discover signatures in the object store.

Signed `seal` requires all three signing flags together. `SignerConfig` contains only `adapter_ref`, `signer_key_id`, `public_key` and `profile_id`. The reference names an owner-controlled, locally enrolled signing adapter. The current checkout supplies no qualified CLI adapter; selecting an unavailable adapter refuses signing. No private key or executable is loaded from these configuration fields, and a failed signed request does not become an unsigned result.

Trusted installation code holds the read-only association between an exact descriptor and an already existing signer. Caller configuration must match that descriptor; it cannot enroll or replace the object. A mismatch is a located configuration failure. An empty installation produces `signer_unavailable` with null subject, claim and pointer before signing or publication. Once an eligible signer is invoked, a failed response retains the known content digest in the original signer-response refusal.
A missing local verification provider produces `configuration_error` and exit `4`
before authentication, with null subject, claim and pointer. It creates no requested
report. Restoring the provider permits evaluation of the complete original input;
the command retains every verification gate and requires a fresh report destination.

`--objects` selects an existing directory. A digest `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` maps to the immediate file `<objects>/<64 lowercase hex>`. The store adds no extension, basis suffix or index. Captured bytes must satisfy every applicable declaration, including declarations sharing a digest under different bases.

The resolver anchors the directory descriptor and refuses symlinks and nonregular targets. It reads within the original per-object and remaining cumulative allowance. Input and store files remain unchanged. Artifact URLs and labels are not filesystem paths or network lookup instructions.

Unsigned `seal` creates a fresh directory containing exactly `content.json` and `refs.json`. Content is the bare canonical library result. The unregistered reference index contains exactly `content_ref`. Signed transport additionally carries the detached envelope and its reference when an eligible adapter supplies a verified signature.

Seal stdout preserves all three `SealResult` field names. `canonical_content` is represented by `{content_ref, output_file}`, where `output_file` is the selected directory joined with `content.json`. The root `content_ref` is that same complete reference. `envelope_json` is null for unsigned construction, or unpadded Base64URL of the exact detached-envelope file bytes for signed transport.

`verify`, `inspect` and `diff` exclusively create the selected report file. Stdout and that file contain the same complete report bytes. All transport JSON is strict UTF-8 RFC 8785 JCS without a BOM, padding or trailing newline. Serialization adds no accepted flag or registered evidence schema.

Output parents must already exist. The current directory publisher uses Linux `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` with an anchored parent, sibling staging, actual absent/occupied capability checks and complete file/directory synchronization. It never substitutes a check followed by an overwriting rename. Existing files, directories and symlinks are preserved. Support on other hosts and filesystems requires equivalent native validation.

Before publication, failures remove only the transaction's unchanged owned staging entries. After publication, a stdout or durability failure leaves the complete immutable output and returns an I/O failure. A retry uses a distinct fresh destination; the command does not delete or overwrite the previous result.
| `0` | Construction or diagnostic transport completed, or verification's requested common mode is eligible. |
| `2` | Input or verification gate refused without a higher-priority failure. |
| `3` | Required reference or signer unavailable, or actual storage, cleanup, stdout or durability failure. |
| `4` | Invalid invocation/configuration or unsupported implementation capability. |

Observed failures use precedence `4 > 3 > 2 > 0`. A report's successful publication clears no gate. Common or historical exit `0` does not establish scientific or current acceptance; read the complete report.

Thrown failures produce stdout `{"operation": ..., "reasons": [...]}` with the full located reasons and no success field. They create no requested successful report or seal destination. A well-formed returned refusal report can be published in full. Malformed invocations name a recognized command when available and otherwise use `operation="emt"`. Caller diagnostics use fixed authored details rather than interpreter messages or local paths.

The top-level architecture describes dependency direction. Domain implementation enrols each source and generated interface in its owning native checks; generated output is reproduced from its qualified generator rather than patched independently. Legacy compatibility and no-loss migration require actual installed consumers and failure/rollback evidence.
The scaffold is under construction. Its tooling separates source inventory,
native configuration validation, check orchestration and bounded process execution.
The inventory reconciles actual maintained files with the declared roots. The
configuration validator binds those roots to strict types, native lint and the
complete statement/branch coverage denominator. The preflight CLI executes the

stage cannot be overwritten by a later successful command. Each report stays
inside a fresh private directory in the selected checkout.

subprocess measurements, enforces 100% statement and branch coverage, then emits

The source projection uses Git's complete tracked and non-ignored untracked
file population, including an unborn local branch. It rejects private paths,
symlinks, oversized source files and observed source changes. It copies the

ordinary executable permissions, and records its file digests separately.
Licence validation runs on that complete projection. Internal planning and

This model describes the current source APIs and their Linux process route.
The caller supplies circuit programmes, dependencies, compiler output, engine
settings, resource policy and an owned workspace. Those data can be malformed,
misleading or costly to parse. The caller, operating system, Python runtime,
owned source and installed supplier code form the execution base. A separate
process or a matching digest does not establish their authenticity.
The assets are original programme bytes and declarations, private circuit data,
captured supplier results, compiler observations, the caller's files and the
host's available resources. An input author can try to alter include resolution,
substitute an artifact or result, hide changed semantics behind metadata,
overwrite runtime code, or exhaust time, memory, streams and storage.
| Input or boundary | Current control | Limit of that control |

| Engine and compiler selection | Fixed owned `WorkerKind` and `CompilerCase` values select source modules; the process command has no shell interpreter | Installed source and executable integrity still depend on their custody |
| Original programmes and dependencies | Linux sealed memory descriptors are mounted read-only at exact virtual filenames | Original bytes can still exercise defects in the SDK or native parser |

| Include and cost-profile resolution | Complete declared dependency bytes, normalised POSIX names, collision and cycle checks, lexical include inventory and explicit supplier built-ins | Lexical resolution records declarations; it does not prove each native file read |

| Runtime overlays | Data cannot replace protected runtime roots, device paths or fixed worker modules | The selected runtime roots are available to the worker; they must be appropriate for that execution |

| Supplier process environment | Bubblewrap separates PID and network namespaces, clears the inherited environment and mounts runtime roots read-only | Namespace containment is dependent on the host kernel and Bubblewrap, and is not an admitted platform profile |

| Native preparation and execution | Six explicit engine limits bound time, represented qubits, static operations, original input occurrences, captured output and per-process address space; startup memory is separate | Address space is not whole-job resident memory; caller-side allocation remains outside this cap |

| Controller and export | Separate controller limits cover its address space, namespace data, lifetime, request size, export bytes and file count | Caller preparation and validation use elapsed checks, without qualified hard whole-caller lifetime or memory containment |

| Returned archive | Every member is checked before extraction; only unique regular relative files are admitted, with no traversal or conflicting paths and with finite count and byte quotas | Imported artifacts are local custody; this does not authenticate a remote producer |

| Result decoding | Bounded unique-key JSON, original input/dependency/configuration joins, prior and terminal consumption records, and agreement with the typed native result | Agreement among these records does not prove the supplier's mathematics or an independent conversion |

| Worker cancellation | The owned process session is killed when still live and reaped, with a second cleanup guard | Arbitrary repeated asynchronous interruption and creation before process assignment remain unqualified |

MITIGATION-WITNESS provides Python components for quantum error mitigation,
including immutable measurement inventories and exact rational quantities.
The current distribution is a local development version. End-to-end witness
operations and the command-line application remain under development.

lines: © Concepts 1996–2026 Miroslav Šotek. All rights reserved.
© Code 2020–2026 Miroslav Šotek. All rights reserved.
# ADR 0005 — Level-0 device physics: compose, do not restate
Status: accepted (2026-09-04). Adds the third implemented capability,
This repository is unlike the other device families of the group in one
respect: it already carried physics. `OperationalLimits` computes the
Greenwald density limit and an elongation-corrected cylindrical safety
factor, and `ToroidalGeometry` computes the aspect ratio.
That changes what a level-0 capability should be here. In the families
that had nothing, the level-0 package **is** the physics. Here, most of
it exists and the question is what a record adds.
1. **The record composes; it does not restate.** The density limit and the
safety factor stay on `OperationalLimits`, and this package calls them.
A level-0 module that reimplemented its own repository's relations
would be two sources of truth for one number, and the drift would be
invisible until they disagreed. A test asserts the record's values are
the ones the configuration's own methods return.
2. **What it adds are the three closed forms nothing owned yet**, each
*Plasma volume* by Pappus's theorem — an ellipse of area `pi kappa a^2`
whose centroid travels `2 pi R` encloses their product. Not an
*The vacuum toroidal field across the plasma's own width*, `B_0 R_0 / R`
at the inboard and outboard edges, and their ratio. A tokamak plasma
does not sit in one field, and the record says by how much.
*The normalised plasma current* `I_p / (a B_t)`, with the model's vacuum
field on axis corresponding to Peng and Strickler's `B_t0`. Their
reported scale is not an enforced operating limit.
3. **And the compositions a reader would otherwise do by hand**: the
density the declared Greenwald fraction asks for, and the safety factor
against its declared floor, each with the margin stated. The margin is
**reported and not enforced**: a floor is a declaration, not a law, and
a record that refused a configuration for missing its own declared
floor would be making an admissibility decision that is not this
4. **The triangularity does not enter the volume, and that is written
down.** The volume reported is for the elliptic model, which does not
The docstring says so, the record's non-claims say so, and a test
asserts that two geometries differing only in triangularity give the
same volume — because a silent limitation is the kind a reader
5. **No kernel-library pin.** Every relation here is multiplication and
division; no transcendental enters, so unlike the three
magneto-inertial families this repository needs no pin for its physics.
## Anchoring: a pair of regimes, not a machine
These fixtures reproduce selected relations, not a real machine's complete
density limit itself — equation 1.3, `nG = I_P / (pi a^2)`, "where nG is
the line-averaged density in units of 10^20 m^-3" — which verifies the
relation this repository already implemented, in both form and units.
regimes**: a spherical torus has aspect ratio below two; at `A ~ 1.5` an
elongation of `kappa = 2` arises naturally from a dipole vertical field
alone; for `A > 2.5` the natural elongation is below `1.4`; and the
normalised current reaches about `7 MA/(m T)`.
So the anchor is two fixtures, one per owned configuration, each sitting
at a printed **pairing**. A pairing anchors better than a lone number
because it can be got wrong in two directions: a fixture that satisfied
only one half would not be where the source says such a device sits.
The spherical fixture's radii are 1.5 and 1.0 rather than 1.2 and 0.8 for
a measured reason: `1.2 / 0.8` is `1.4999999999999998` in binary and
`1.5 / 1.0` is exact, so the anchor test asserts an equality.
Every absolute fixture dimension is declared as a synthetic choice. The
source reports also contain dimensions and machine examples, but these
fixtures do not copy their complete parameter sets.
The repository has a level-0 record that adds what was missing and repeats
nothing. Its two anchors sit at printed regime pairings, and the one
limitation of its volume relation is tested rather than merely mentioned.
Nothing here predicts a disruption, a stability boundary or a
performance, and no value describes a real machine.

# ADR 0005 — Level-0 device physics as ignition condition and implosion figures
Status: accepted (2026-09-04). Builds on ADR 0002 (device configuration
model), whose `LaserDriver` and `TargetDeclaration` already carry the
driver energy, the pulse duration, the wavelength and the capsule's
A laser-ICF implosion is a radiation-hydrodynamics problem. Nothing in
this repository computes one, and a level-0 record that pretended to
would be worthless. What a filed review does supply is the algebra
around such a calculation: the condition a hot spot must satisfy to
ignite, stated four equivalent ways with every coefficient printed, and
the definitions a one-dimensional design is quoted by.
The review — R. S. Craxton et al., *Phys. Plasmas* **22** (2015) 110501,
already collected in this repository's internal papers ledger — also
prints one worked design completely enough that its own statements can
be checked against its own equations. That turned out to matter.
1. The capability `level0_device_physics` is implemented in three
modules split by responsibility — the ignition condition, the
implosion definitions, and the fuel inventory with its yield and gain
— and a fourth composing them into a record.
2. **All four forms of the ignition condition are carried, because they
constrain each other.** Equation 3-8's coefficient of 40 micrometres
is not independent: it is equation 3-6's reference radius scaled by
the ratio of the two printed pressures, and a test recovers it as the
same IEEE double. The three coefficients then close on the energy
relation `f_k E_k = 2 pi P R^3` to a fixed 0.53 %, at every energy
over three decades — the rounding of the printed numbers, asserted
as the measured offset rather than as an equality.
3. **The capsule layering and the implosion outcome are declared
inputs**, in two separate objects: what the capsule was before the
shot, and what the implosion did. Both come out of calculations this
4. **Definitions carry their conditions.** The in-flight aspect ratio is
read where the ablation front reaches two thirds of the initial inner
radius, and that fraction lives in the module rather than in the
caller. The convergence ratio is defined with alpha-particle
deposition switched off, which no code can enforce and which is
therefore stated in the docstring and in the record's non-claims. The
hydrodynamic efficiency divides by **absorbed** energy, not incident.
5. **Two of the review's own numbers are not reproduced by its own
relations, and both are recorded as tests rather than smoothed
away.** Its worked example of equation 3-7 states a required pressure
"exceeding 120 to 180 Gbar", where the equation at the stated inputs
gives 112 to 125 Gbar. And its one-dimensional gain of 48 is not
recovered from its printed geometry at its printed burnup fraction
with solid fuel at standard density: that reconstruction gives about
57, some 18 % high, because a quoted burnup fraction applies to the
fuel that assembles and burns and part of the printed inventory is
not in that state. **Neither number is used as an anchor.** Adjusting
an input until they met would have been the easy move and would have
6. Equation 3-6's coefficient is likewise carried as printed. Computed
from equation 3-5's own floors it is 115 Gbar; the review prints 100.
The implementation follows the printed value and a test carries the
arithmetic, so the rounding is recorded where a reader will find it.
7. The capsule's initial inner radius is **built**, not declared: the
outer radius the configuration carries, less the two declared
thicknesses. A layering that does not fit is refused, because it
describes a different capsule from the one the configuration
8. No kernel-library pin. Every relation is arithmetic and elementary
- The manifest gains the capability `level0_device_physics` at
count becomes three, and the derived inventory and studio descriptor
- The package root re-exports the record and the principal relations.
- The record reports the gain its declared inputs imply, which for the
review's design is the reconstruction near 57 rather than the printed
48. A reader who wants the printed figure must supply the burning fuel
mass, which this repository cannot compute.
- **What this ADR does not decide.** The family's tier-G1 and tier-G2
device models are not landed here. Unlike the gridded electrostatic
families, nothing blocks them: a capsule and its shells are solids of
revolution the shared library can already express.

Status: accepted (2026-09-04), amended the same day — see "Correction,

boundary mechanism the first version stated. Builds on ADR 0002 (device
configuration model), which owns the capsule's outer radius, and ADR

A laser-ICF target is small, layered and spherical, and every one of
those three facts changed a decision here.
**Small.** The bodies are millimetres across. Every other family in this
group models metres, and two things that hold at metre scale do not hold
at this one. They are recorded under their own heading below, because a
reader who assumes the sibling families' numbers transfer will build a
model that fails its own evidence gate — which is exactly what happened
**Layered.** The capsule is an ablator, a fuel layer and the vapour the
fuel layer encloses. All three are concentric about one point, and the
dimensions that define them already exist in this repository: the outer
radius in the configuration, because the configuration's intensity
estimate divides by it, and the two thicknesses in the level-0 capsule
declaration, because the fuel mass is computed from them.
**Spherical.** The shared kernel library gained spherical bodies and the
spherical shell in the increment this landing pins. Nothing here needs a
primitive the library does not have.
**One geometry declaration, and it is not the capsule.** The geometry
package declares only the radiation enclosure of an indirect-drive
target, because that is the one piece of hardware neither the
configuration nor the level-0 record carries. The capsule's three radii

defaults. The configuration model already refuses a hohlraum flag on a

The ignitor pulse of the fast-or-shock-ignition class adds no body. It
**The vapour is drawn, although it is a gas.** The beam-target family

nothing in its vacuum zone, both for the same reason: nothing is
declared to be there. Here the review prints the vapour's density and

**The enclosure's open ends are its laser entrance holes.** The wall is

claim a dimension no filed source prints.

SPIKE-LOG is the planned record and replay container for event streams. The selected design stores ordered canonical events and source-native side streams in chunked `.slog` files, with an index, integrity chain, capture provenance and a detached evidence seal.

The repository is under local scaffold construction. Evidence maturity is `architecture_only`; implemented domain capabilities, public claims and qualified schema inventories are empty. No container writer, capture adapter, replay engine or physical measurement is qualified here.

The product owns recording, replay, metadata inspection, complete container verification and provenance-preserving slicing. External format conversion belongs to SPIKE-FORMAT-BRIDGE. Event quality judgement and ground-truth generation belong to their own tools. LOOP-TIMING-WITNESS owns capture instrumentation; SC-NeuroCore owns neural adapters and model outputs.

Logical replay preserves original values, ticks and ordering. Requested native or scaled delivery does not guarantee wall-clock timing. A source-native side stream retains its exact codec identity; archiving bytes does not qualify unknown neural semantics.

See [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md), [roadmap](ROADMAP.md), [validation](VALIDATION.md) and [security](SECURITY.md). Contribution and support routes are [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md).

This is the authoritative, source-grounded map of SCPN-MIF-CORE: every component, its
inputs and outputs, its processing model, the backends that implement it and how they
are wired, and where each piece sits between *delivered* and *roadmap*. It is written
for three audiences — sibling SCPN repositories that consume MIF surfaces, the SCPN
STUDIO federation that renders MIF's capabilities, and engineers extending the core.
Counts in this document are mechanically derived from `docs/_generated/capability_manifest.json`
(an AST/file-system inventory) and `bench/dispatch.toml`; the per-component status is
architecture decision records (`docs/adr/`). Where a capability is roadmap or
hardware-gated, this map says so — see [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-delivered-versus-roadmap-honesty.md).
MIF-CORE is **the verified, deterministic, chamber-side trigger lane for pulsed
field-reversed-configuration (FRC) fusion** — a compiler from plasma kinematics toward a
sub-50-nanosecond hardware compression-trigger target, plus the integration hub across five
sibling SCPN repositories. It is *not* a plasma-physics laboratory: the equilibrium,
transport, and self-consistent compression physics are owned by SCPN-FUSION-CORE and
The core's value is the intersection of three things: an open-tool, machine-checked
safety/timing trigger fabric; a literature-anchored kinematic merge-window model that
consumes sibling physics as input; and a bit-true Python↔Verilator cosimulation.
| Plasmoid relative speed at merging | ≥ Mach 1 (`v_z ≥ 300 km s⁻¹`) |
